title: Screenshots throw RangeError when a never-look (or remote-surface) window lies to the left of the target window
scenario: A password manager (KeePassXC, Bitwarden and 1Password are on the default never-look lists), or on Windows any Remote Desktop/WSLg window, sits to the left of the window Ember is looking at. Typical cases are the other monitor, or a half-screen tile with a gap, and the private window reaches the target's top edge row. Every perceive_window with image=true then rejects with 'RangeError: The value of "end" is out of range', so the tool call fails instead of returning a picture or a '(No screenshot: ...)' note. The model retries and burns steps. captureRect is given masks for every private window on the whole screen, not just ones overlapping the capture rectangle (perception/index.ts: `const mask = await this.privateWindows(stack)`). maskRect does `rgba.fill(0, (y*width+x0)*4, (y*width+x1)*4)` with x1 < 0, so the end offset is negative on rows near the top. app/remote/mask.ts:26 is a copy that has the guard `if (!(x1 > x0 && y1 > y0)) return;`, so only the local path is affected.
evidence: Live, real sidecar + X11: target Electron window at x=500..1100,y=40, private window 'vault' at x=40..340,y=40..340, neverLook=['vault']: `perception.perceive({image:true,scope:'window',target:{pid}})` REJECTED with RangeError ... Received -640 (repro/exp22.test.ts). Without the never-look entry the same call returns a picture. Minimal: `maskRect(Buffer.alloc(100*50*4),100,50,{x:-60,y:0,width:20,height:10})` throws (repro/exp34.test.ts). Fuzz of 20000 random rects: 1258 throws, all left-of-image masks reaching the top rows (exp23, exp30). Model-based fuzz of Perception.perceive over 600 random layouts: 56 threw this error; the 544 that succeeded had every secret, private, cover and own-window region black. Re-run with a guarded copy of captureRect: 600/600 pass, window scope and screen scope (repro/exp24.test.ts, exp24b, exp35).
fix: In maskRect (capture.ts) return early when the clipped rectangle is empty, as app/remote/mask.ts does: `if (!(x1 > x0 && y1 > y0)) return;` placed before the fill loops. Add unit tests for masks wholly left of, above, right of and below the image. Optionally also clip the mask list to the capture rect in captureRect.

title: Windows UIA snapshot walks offscreen subtrees: long pages scrolled down read as empty, and screenshots of big pages are refused
area: perception / large trees (Windows UIA bridge + sidecar host)
scenario: On Windows, Chrome, Edge, Teams, Slack, Outlook-web and similar apps expose their whole page to UI Automation. Content above the viewport is reported IsOffscreen=true but with real bounds. The bridge's Walk.Visit goes pre-order and only prunes elements that are offscreen AND have no area (Props.Skipped, line 1744; PROTOCOL.md:300), so it descends into all offscreen content. The host asks for min(400*4, 4000)=1600 raw nodes per read and 6000 for the secret scan (reading.ts:28-34), counted over those offscreen nodes. Once the visible part is further than about 1600 elements into the tree, perceive_window lists only the window and the page container: nothing visible, with cut=['nodes'] and the text '(only the first 2 are listed. Scroll to the part you need...)'. That advice is wrong, because the part needed is on screen. Pages with more than 6000 accessible nodes (Gmail, GitHub PR diffs, long articles) also make secret_fields incomplete, so every screenshot is declined with 'the window is too big for Ember to check all of it for password fields'. The Linux sidecar and the macOS provider prune by what shows, so Windows is the outlier. host tree.ts:118 then discards every offscreen node and its subtree anyway, so descending into them is wasted work.
evidence: Reproduced on the real host code with the repo's FakeProvider, which implements the bridge's documented semantics (offscreen-with-bounds elements are listed and counted): 25 visible links preceded by N offscreen links. N=300 and 1200: all 25 listed. N=1700 and 3000: 0 of 25 listed, 2 nodes, truncated=true, cut=['nodes'] (repro/exp39.test.ts). C# source read: Walk.Visit recurses into every child returned by Children(), which filters only Props.Skipped, i.e. offscreen with no area. No test in the repo exercises a long or scrolled page on Windows (the benches are small WinForms/WPF windows). Not run on a real Windows desktop.
fix: In the bridge, do not descend into an element whose IsOffscreen is true (keep listing the node itself, with its flag). The host throws those subtrees away anyway (tree.ts:118, reading.ts:303), so behaviour is unchanged except that the budget goes to what shows. Alternatively order children on-screen first for every node, not only when there are more than 200. Add a Windows integration test with a few thousand offscreen elements before the visible ones, and word the 'nodes' note differently when the cut was in offscreen content.

title: Windows/macOS host has no protection for names that contain the value of a secret field the read didn't list
area: secrets in text sent to the model (sidecar host)
scenario: Chromium (Chrome, Edge, Electron, Chromium-based macOS apps) names a table cell, row, <label> or section after the values of the fields inside it; I confirmed live that Blink does this: section 'Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111', table cell 'PIN 4821'. On Linux the sidecar withholds such names even when the field itself is not in the read (scrolled partly out of view, or past the node limit) through unlisted_secrets/name_says_secret (ember_atspi.py:1855). The TS host only compares names with the values of secret fields it listed (Secrets.redact -> withheldIds over `hidden`). Fields that are offscreen are dropped in buildNodes (tree.ts:118) before their value is ever considered. So a checkout form scrolled so that the card row is cut at the viewport edge, with the label or cell still partly visible, puts the card number into perceive_window's output on Windows (and at_point/read_element, which use the same remembered values). The Linux tests cover exactly this case (PERC9-1/PERC9-3); there is no TS-host test or doc for it.
evidence: FakeProvider + real Host: DataItem named 'Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111' (partly visible) containing an offscreen Edit with that value: read_window lists `table cell name='Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111'` (repro/exp36.test.ts). The same page on Linux through the real sidecar names the container with the value (repro/exp37.test.ts). grep for unlisted/PERC9 in app/sidecar-host, test/unit/sidecar-host-*.ts and the docs finds nothing. Not run on Windows or macOS; whether UIA/AX expose the same container names there depends on Chromium's cross-platform naming, which is the basis for the finding.
fix: In buildNodes, for fields skipped because they are offscreen (or cut), still evaluate isSecret and put their raw values into `hidden` (the snapshot already carries `value` for offscreen elements with bounds) so Secrets.redact/withheldIds withholds the listed containers that say them. For fields the read cut off by maxNodes, withhold names of the last listed element and its ancestors, as the Python stop-set does. Add tests mirroring PERC9-1/PERC9-3.

title: Secret-label vocabulary misses seed/recovery phrases, '6-digit code' style one-time codes and non-English reveal toggles
scenario: Fields are protected by their name or label matching SECRET_WORDS (mirrored in ember_atspi.py SECRET_WORDS, kept equal by a unit test). The lists say they cover one-time codes and keys, yet they do not match: 'Seed phrase', 'Recovery phrase', 'Mnemonic' (a wallet restore screen); 'Enter the 6-digit code', '6-digit code', 'Authenticator code', 'SMS code', 'Login code', 'Sign-in code', 'Access code', 'Activation code', 'Unlock code', 'Pass code' (every 2FA prompt); 'Security token', 'Master key', 'SSH key'. A wallet seed phrase or a 2FA code typed into such a field is then returned in perceive_window's text and shown unmasked in the screenshot, so it reaches the cloud model. 'Secret Recovery Phrase' and 'Verification code' do match, which shows the intent. Separately, the reveal-toggle verb list (REVEAL, elements.ts:153) lacks ko, da, no, hu, ro, el, vi, id, ar, he and th, so an unlabelled revealed password field beside '비밀번호 표시', 'Vis adgangskode', 'Jelszó megjelenítése', 'Afișează parola' and the like is not treated as secret (the English, German, French, Japanese, Chinese and Russian toggles are).
evidence: Real Electron page through the real sidecar and Perception.perceive(image:true): `entry "Seed phrase" (editable, multi line) ... text="LEAKSEED apple banana cherry"` and `entry "Enter the 6-digit code" (editable) ... text="LEAK654321"` are printed and not marked secret, while `Enter secret` is secret; green text from those fields remains in the JPEG (repro/exp1.test.ts). isSecretLabel() over 80 labels: plain for Seed phrase, Recovery phrase, Mnemonic, 6-digit code, Authenticator code, Login code, Access code, SMS code, Sign-in code, Security token. secretIds() with a nameless entry beside toggles in 17 languages: only the 6 listed above flag it (repro/exp12.test.ts). test/fixtures/secret-labels.json has none of these phrases.
fix: Add to both lists (keep them identical): `(seed|recovery|backup|secret recovery) phrases?`, `mnemonics?`, `(\\d+|six|four)[- ]digit codes?`, `(authenticator|authentication|sms|text message|login|log-in|sign-in|access|activation|unlock|mfa|passcode|pass code) codes?`, `(security|session|refresh|id) tokens?`, `(master|signing|ssh) keys?`; extend REVEAL with the missing languages' verbs. Add rows to secret-labels.json (secret and plain: 'Discount code', 'Postcode' must stay plain).

title: Remote desktop helper has no Xlib error handler: a window closing between two X calls kills it
area: sidecar/helper crash recovery (SSH remote desktop child)
scenario: The desktop child is plain Node and uses x11.ts (stack(), activeWindow(), clientWindows(), describe()) and hands/input.ts. Each lists windows, then queries each one with XGetWindowAttributes, XGetWindowProperty and XGetGeometry. If a window is destroyed in between (a menu, tooltip or dialog closing right after Ember's click), the X server sends BadWindow and Xlib's default error handler calls exit(1). The helper dies, serve reports 'Ember's desktop helper on <host> stopped', and the task loses the remote screen until the PC asks again, possibly with a new consent prompt at the remote console. Electron's main process is protected (Chromium installs a handler) and the desk helper explicitly calls XSetErrorHandler (desk/agent-process.ts:26 'A window that closes between two calls (BadWindow) must not end the helper'), but the remote child does not. The race window is small, so this is rare in normal use but not impossible.
evidence: Plain Node + koffi: `XGetWindowAttributes(dpy, bogusWindow, buf)` prints 'X Error of failed request: BadWindow' and exits 1, while the same call in Electron 44's main process returns 0 and survives. The real openX11().stack()/activeWindow() loop in plain Node, run beside a GTK script that creates and destroys popup windows rapidly, exited with BadWindow in 3 of 3 runs within 12 to 447 requests. With one tooltip-like popup every 400 ms it survived 200 calls over 60 s (repro/hammer.ts, hammer2.ts; xerr/plain.js).
fix: Install a no-op XSetErrorHandler once when the child starts (move ignoreXErrors from desk/agent-process.ts into x11.ts and call it from openX11 when process.versions.electron is unset, or call it first thing in runDesktopChild). Ideally also have the child return null for a window that disappeared.

title: perceive() takes an unscanned whole-screen screenshot when the requested window is gone or busy
scenario: perceive({image:true, scope:'window', target}) computes `windowScope = scope === 'window' && !!(seen.window || seen.x11Window)`. When the target window has closed, never matched, or its app is hung (read returns window:null), windowScope is false and the code carries on to capture the entire screen (rect = screenBounds()). No secret fields are scanned (the `if (seen.window)` block is skipped), only never-look/own windows are masked, and the text says 'The focused window exposes no accessibility information; use the screenshot.' Today the Worker discards the image because it returns fail() when !p.window, so nothing reaches the model. But the capture still happens: on macOS it shows the recording indicator, a hung app costs about 3.6 s, and for SSH remotes the whole remote screen is PNG-encoded and shipped over the link (serve.ts perceive) before the PC drops it. One refactor of the Worker, or any new caller, would send an unmasked full-screen picture to the model on an operation that promises a window.
evidence: Target Electron app killed, or a nonexistent title: perceive returned capture rect {0,0,1600,900} with the other window's green card-number text still in it (190 green px) and window=false (repro/exp14.test.ts). With the target process SIGSTOPped: capture=true, rect full screen, 64 green px, busy=true, 3.6 s (repro/exp13.test.ts). worker.ts:1605-1613 shows the Worker dropping it.
fix: In perceive(): if opts.scope === 'window' && !windowScope, return noShot('the window can't be found (it may have closed or its app isn't answering)') before any capture. Keep whole-screen capture for scope 'screen' only.

title: read_window gives no 'page still loading' signal when a browser document isn't handed over yet
platforms: linux (Chromium/Electron via AT-SPI); Windows UIA likely similar
scenario: A very large page, or the first read after a Chromium app turns on accessibility, shows a 'document web' with childCount 0 and 0x0 extents until the browser has built its tree. scan_fields knows this (not_ready -> cut 'loading' -> secret_fields busy), but walk()/read_window ignore it. The read returns just the window frame and the browser's menu bar or toolbar, with truncated false and busy false, so perceive_window and describe_screen present an apparently complete window that has no page content. The model may say the page is empty or the window has only a menu bar. Only a screenshot request is told 'the app is busy ... try again in a moment', and a very big page stayed in this state for the whole 55 s I watched.
evidence: Electron page with 9000 links: pyatspi says `document found; childCount= 0 extents= {width:0,height:0} not_ready= True` for every poll up to 53 s, while read_window returned 6 nodes (frame, menu bar, 4 buttons), trunc=false, busy=undefined, and secret_fields returned complete=false busy=true each time (repro/exp19.test.ts, exp5, exp6). A 1800-link page of the same shape read normally.
fix: In walk(), when a document role is not_ready, call budget.cut_short('loading'); pass 'loading' through ReadWindowResult.cut and map it in Perception.read/notes() to '(The page is still loading, so its content isn't listed yet. Try again in a moment.)' instead of the 'depth'/'nodes' texts. Do the same in the TS host for a Document with no children and no area.

title: An app's own override-redirect popups are drawn in window screenshots without being scanned for secret fields
platforms: linux (X11); Windows popups by the same rule
scenario: coveringRects deliberately does not black out the target app's own override-redirect windows (menus, lists, tooltips) because they are 'part of what the worker looks at'. Their accessibility trees are not read for secrets, though: read_window walks only the target frame, and `others` lists only active or modal windows by name. A popup holding a field named 'Card number' or 'Login code' with its text visible (a GTK popover or entry-completion window, or a Firefox-style doorhanger or autofill panel; I did not test Firefox) therefore appears unmasked in the 'window with numbered marks' image. It is not in the text either, so the model sees an unlisted secret.
evidence: GTK3 app with a main window plus a POPUP-type window over it containing Entries named 'Card number' (4111 1111 1111 1111) and 'Login code': X stack shows the popup as overrideRedirect=true with the same pid; perceive of the main window returned a capture with 836 green pixels from the popup's text and no node for it in the read (repro/exp20.test.ts). I did not find a concrete production popup that carries a full secret; Chromium/Firefox popup behaviour is unverified.
fix: When the stack has same-pid override-redirect windows overlapping the target, scan their accessibility frames with secret_fields (they are top-level frames of the same app) and mask the secrets, or black out the whole popup when it can't be scanned. Cheap fallback: treat a same-pid popup as a cover if it overlaps the window and isn't a menu/tooltip by size.

title: Remote viewers and VM windows are not masked as remote surfaces on Linux and macOS
scenario: REMOTE_SURFACE is null for Linux and macOS, so only Windows blacks out Remote Desktop/WSLg windows (README and DEVELOPING.md 10.8 say so and list Hyper-V, VNC, TeamViewer and Citrix as not covered, but only for Windows). On a RHEL 8 workstation a window of virt-manager/virt-viewer, GNOME Boxes, Remmina or VNC Viewer (macOS: Screen Sharing, Microsoft Remote Desktop, Parallels, VMware Fusion, UTM) shows a whole guest or remote desktop that accessibility cannot see into. A window screenshot of it can contain the guest's password manager, login forms and revealed passwords, with none of the never-look or secret-field masking applying. Nothing in the docs tells Linux or macOS users that these are exposed, and the default never-look lists don't include them.
evidence: Code reading: remote-surface.ts REMOTE_SURFACE = { linux: null, win32: /^(msrdc|mstsc|...)/i, darwin: null }; Perception.remoteSurfaces() returns [] when no isRemoteSurface is passed (main.ts passes remoteSurfaceCheck(platform.os), undefined for Linux and macOS). DEVELOPING.md:700-702 'Linux and macOS are unaffected'.
fix: Add Linux/macOS rows for the common viewers (virt-manager, virt-viewer, gnome-boxes, remmina, vinagre, vncviewer, krdc, parallels, vmware, utm, screensharing, microsoft remote desktop) and black them out like Windows' clients, or at least state the gap in the README and doctor output.

title: offer_connect's Connect button is overwritten within milliseconds by the conversation's own bubble
scenario: The user says "open the logs on build-01" while build-01 isn't connected. The model calls offer_connect, and the runtime writes "Connect to build-01? [Connect] [Not now]" straight to main's setState, bypassing the BubbleOwner. When tool.execution_complete arrives a few ms later, Presenter.apply (presenter.ts:749-752) re-pushes the conversation's own bubble and wipes the offer. The tool result has told the model "Ember showed the user a Connect button... Tell them to click it", so Ember then says "Click Connect" with no button on screen. The headline 'name a computer, get a Connect button' flow is effectively dead for the user.
evidence: Scratch vitest with the real Presenter and the real buildTargets rig, both writing through guardWhileAsking. Screen log: 'Thinking…' -> 'Connect to build-01? | You asked for build-01 [Connect/Not now]' -> 'Thinking…' again, then after the tool-complete line 'Ember | I've shown a Connect button. []'. The final screen has no actions. Code: runtime.ts:547-552 (bubble() calls deps.showState directly), runtime.ts:1383-1388 (offerConnect), main.ts:1475 (showState: setState, no owner), presenter.ts:395-412 (apply consults only the owner, which doesn't know the runtime wrote).
fix: Make runtime bubbles owners in the BubbleOwner. Expose an AgentHost method such as agent.showNotice(key, bubble, {holdUntil}) that does a 'take' claim and sets owner.holder to a runtime token until the bubble is answered, expires or is hidden. Presenters then queue behind it as they do behind a question. Alternatively route offer_connect through the Confirmer, which already gives hold, arming, timeout and keys. At minimum, hold the owner while an actionable runtime bubble is up.

title: Runtime info-bubble timers blank whatever replaced them; stale presenter hide timers blank runtime bubbles
scenario: After connecting, Ember shows "Ember is on build-01 / Ask away: I'll work there" for 7 s (INFO_MS). The user takes that invitation and asks at 3 s. The answer streams and finishes at about 5 s. At 7 s the runtime's timer calls hideBubble, which unconditionally writes IDLE_BUBBLE, and the answer disappears after about 2 s instead of its 7+ s reading time, along with its 'Read all' button. It works the other way too: an earlier answer's presenter hide timer still believes it owns the screen and blanks a runtime bubble shown meanwhile, such as 'Lost build-01 [Reconnect] [Stop trying]' or an offer.
evidence: Scratch vitest. (1) connect, then userPrompt, then answer, then idle, then fire the runtime timers: the answer thought is "There are 12 files in /var/log…" before and visible=false thought="" after. (2) answer on screen with hide armed for 7100 ms, then link 'lost' bubble shown, then the answer's hide timer fires: screen visible=false, title "". Code: runtime.ts:551 checks only shown?.seq (its own sequence) and runtime.ts:553-557 writes IDLE_BUBBLE; compare main.ts:429-431 hideIfStill, which checks lastState.bubble === bubble. presenter.ts:510-518 hide() pushes IDLE whenever owner.current === this, which the runtime's write never changes.
fix: In hideBubble, only clear if the bubble on screen is still the one it wrote (keep the object and compare with lastState, as hideIfStill does). Make Presenter.hide do the same check before pushing IDLE. The proper fix is the owner routing described in the previous finding.

title: "Lost build-01 [Reconnect]" is replaced by the stopped task's bare "Stopped.", and Ember silently works on this computer
scenario: A task is running on build-01 and the network drops. The runtime calls stopTasks, then shows 'Lost build-01 — The connection dropped… [Reconnect] [Stop trying]', and resets the active target to this computer (line 656). A moment later the aborted worker finishes as 'cancelled', and host.ts:875-876 shows presenter.outcome({title: task, text: 'Stopped.', mood: 'idle'}). That replaces the Lost bubble, so the user sees 'Check disk on build-01 — Stopped.' for about 6 s and then nothing. The Reconnect button is gone, the wording blames no one, and the handle badge has already gone (active target is local). The next request without a place word runs on this PC, and nothing said so.
evidence: Scratch vitest log: 'Lost build-01 [Reconnect/Stop trying]' then 'Check disk []', final on screen 'Check disk []'. Worker result for an abort is stoppedSummary() = 'Stopped.' (worker.ts:1246, 1352), and TaskManager maps abort to 'cancelled' (tasks.ts:256). runtime.ts:652-660 (lost branch) and :656 (setActive(LOCAL_TARGET)); host.ts:870-876 only silences kill-switch stops.
fix: Hold the Lost bubble in the owner (see the first finding). Give tasks cut off by a lost link a reason ('build-01 dropped, so I stopped this') instead of 'Stopped.'. Add 'Until it's back I'll work on this computer' to the Lost text. Keep the bubble until the user acts or SA's reconnect succeeds.

title: Short answers with line breaks are clipped to six lines with no "Read all"; the question at the end is cut off
scenario:
Ember answers 'You have three options:

1. Move the files…

2. Delete the duplicates

3. Leave everything as it is

Which would you like?' (134 characters). The bubble shows only the header and two options. The fade at the bottom is invisible because the sixth line is blank. Option 3 and the question are hidden, no 'Read all' is offered, and the bubble hides after about 9 s. The user decides on half an answer. Lists and paragraph breaks are the model's normal style, so this is common.
evidence: Chromium render of the built overlay: this answer measures 9 lines needed and 6 available, data-overflow=true, 0 buttons (screenshot s-options.png in the scratch folder). A 93-character 7-item list also overflows with no button. Cause: presenter.ts:768-769 offers 'Read all' only when full.length > LONG_ANSWER (260 characters), while the CSS clamp (bubble.ts:240-244) is 6 lines and pre-line keeps every newline.
fix: Decide by lines, not characters: estimate rendered lines as the sum of max(1, ceil(line.length/36)) over the answer's lines and offer 'Read all' when that exceeds 6. Better, let the bubble measure overflow after layout (it already computes `over`) and have the overlay add the ui:more action when a finished answer overflows.

title: "On <computer>" exists only as a visual badge: missing from screen-reader announcements, spoken questions, notifications, the no-compositor card and fill_cells questions
platforms: all (SSH and WSL targets); the card on Linux xrdp/VNC (no compositor)
scenario: A task on build-01 asks "May I? Click Save in gedit?". Sighted users on the compositor path see a 'on build-01' capsule. A screen-reader user hears 'Ember needs you: May I? Click “Save” in gedit?' with no computer named. With speech on, main speaks 'Ember asks: Click Save in gedit? Press Ctrl+Alt+Y…'. When the user is idle, the notification says 'Ember needs your OK: Click “Save” in gedit?'. In a no-compositor session (xrdp/VNC) the corner card never renders BubbleState.where or TaskCard.where, and its header shows the picker's target instead. With build-01 picked and a task bound to this computer, the card says 'build-01' beside a question about this PC. The fill_cells question (worker.ts:2513) carries no `where` at all. Approving a step without knowing which computer it is on defeats the 'one computer per task, questions say where' guarantee.
evidence: announcement() (bubble.ts:50-61) takes only title and thought; the badge is DOM-only in overlay/main.ts:164-174. Ran announcement(): connected -> 'Ember says: Ask away…' (host dropped); question -> no place. main.ts:691 and :693 use q.question.prompt with no where; worker.ts:3366 even comments 'a badge in the bubble, and in the spoken question' but no code speaks it; handle/main.ts renders only s.target (Chromium render s-fallback.png: the card text contains no where). worker.ts:2513 passes no where.
fix: Add `where` to BubbleView and prepend it in announcement() ('Ember needs you, on build-01: …'). Pass q.question.where into the spoken text and notification in main.ts questionChanged. Render b.where and task.where in the fallback card, preferring them over the picker badge. Add where to the fill_cells question.

title: Unsolicited offers never expire, park Ember where it stands, and take clicks immediately
scenario: The user runs `ssh build-01` in a terminal. Ember pops 'You're connected to build-01 — Bring Ember there too? [Bring Ember] [Not now] [Don't offer again]' beside the cursor. If they ignore it, the bubble has no timer, and any bubble with actions makes overlay.ts setState park the follower, so Ember stops following the cursor and sits frozen with a pulsing 'Needs you' chip until a button is pressed or Ember happens to speak. A user who clicks in the terminal near the cursor can hit 'Bring Ember' or the permanent 'Don't offer again' at once, because (unlike a question) these buttons have no arming delay. The WSL offer and offer_connect's Connect behave the same.
evidence: showSeenOffer (runtime.ts:963-976), offerWsl (:1049-1054) and offerConnect (:1383-1388) call bubble() with no hideMs. overlay.ts:127-152: waiting(s) is true when bubble.actions.length > 0, which calls follower.park(here()); follower.step then returns parked ?? target (follow.ts:79-88). The 500 ms arm exists only in the Confirmer (confirm.ts:98) and the renderer arms only task: ids (arm.ts). The greeting, by contrast, hides after 7 or 15 s (main.ts:454).
fix: Give offers a 20-30 s expiry that counts as 'Not now' (without writing the permanent dismissal). Don't park the follower for unsolicited offers. Ignore presses in the first 500 ms as the Confirmer does.

title: "Needs you" mood is used for information-only notices; other state words are borrowed too
scenario: 'Stopped on build-01 — Someone at build-01 pressed Stop.', 'Back on this computer', and the screen-locked notice need nothing from the user, yet they render a purple pulsing 'Needs you' chip. A screen reader announces 'Ember needs you: Stopped on build-01…'. 'Ember is on build-01' shows a green 'Done' chip. 'Connecting to build-01…' shows a 'Thinking' chip with the thinking glow. A signed-out request gets the red 'Problem' notice while the same state's greeting is purple 'Needs you'. These runtime bubbles also never set Ember's emotion, so a 'Problem' bubble sits on a neutral face. docs/DESIGN.md defines Needs you as 'asking before a risky step'.
evidence: Rendered in Chromium (s-stoppedRemote.png, s-connecting.png, s-connected.png). Announcement output: 'Ember needs you: Stopped on build-01. Someone at build-01 pressed Stop.' runtime.ts:617, 623, 668 use mood "attention" with no actions; BUBBLE_LABEL (bubble.ts:21-30) has no connecting or info state; announcement() maps attention to 'needs you' (bubble.ts:56). host.ts:1356 (notice, mood error) vs main.ts:449 (greeting, attention).
fix: Use mood idle (chip hidden) for pure notices. Add a 'connecting' label and mood (or a chip override) for connection progress. Use 'attention' only when a button needs a decision. Pass an emotion with runtime error and notice bubbles.

title: Bubble titles truncate with an ellipsis exactly where they carry the decision
scenario: With the state chip (and a 'where' badge) sharing the header row, the one-line title is ellipsized. The command announcement 'Pushing feature-x to origin, as you asked' (the thing the user may want to Stop in 4 s) shows as 'Pushing feature-x to origin, as you …'. 'You're connected to build-01 from Ubuntu-22.04' loses the distro. With a badge, a task title like 'Tidy the desktop logs and rotate them' shows as 'Tidy …' when the host is a FQDN, and the badge itself reads 'on ip-10-0-12-34.eu-west-1.…', hiding the end of the name.
evidence: Measured in Chromium (scrollWidth > clientWidth on .eb-title). Without a badge: 'Pushing feature-x…' need=273 avail=253; 'You're connected to build-01 from Ubuntu-22.04' need=325 avail=253. With 'on build-01': 'Copilot didn't accept the sign-in', 'Turn on commands on this computer?', 'Can't connect to build-01' and 19 more cut at avail 151-175. CSS at bubble.ts:238 (.eb-title nowrap/ellipsis) and overlay/styles.css (.where max-width 160px).
fix: Let the title wrap to two lines in attention and announcement moods, or move the statement into the thought. Shorten the badge from the middle (keep the host's start and end) and cap it lower.

title: Error bubbles clip at six lines with no scroll or expand; ssh messages show literal backticks
scenario: 'Can't connect to build-01' with the host-key-changed message (255 characters) is cut at the last line and loses 'then connect again.'. A long hostname pushes the `ssh-keygen -R <host>` fix off the bottom. The sign-in-refused message plus a proxy note (265 characters) is also cut. Only attention bubbles scroll (up to 10 lines). The message also shows its backticks verbatim ('`ssh-keygen -R build-01`'), since runtime bubbles bypass plainMarkdown. fail() hides it after 14 s.
evidence: Chromium: error mood, keyChanged needs 7 lines and has 6 (overflow=true); signinProxy 7 vs 6; the same texts fit in attention mood (s-keychanged.png). CSS: bubble.ts:240-244 (6-line clamp) vs :262-265 (attention scrolls). Texts from remote/ssh-errors.ts:45-48 (keyChanged + keyChangedFix) and host.ts:345.
fix: Treat error like attention (scroll up to 10 lines), or raise the error clamp to 8. Strip backticks (or render them as code) in runtime-sourced text. Keep the actionable sentence first.

title: Error bubbles tell the user to open settings but only some have the button
scenario: A session.error for a refused sign-in reads 'Copilot didn't accept the sign-in. Open settings to sign in again.' or 'Pick another one in settings (Ctrl+Alt+E)', but that bubble has actions: [] (line 780), so there is nothing to click. A failed task's outcome has none either. fail() and the not-ready notice always add 'Open settings', even for a transient 'Copilot stopped unexpectedly. I'm reconnecting' or a pure network outage where settings can't help, and the bubble then says 'Press Check again', a settings-window button.
evidence: presenter.ts:773-785 (session.error: actions: []) vs :521-533 (fail: Open settings always) and host.ts:1356 (notice: Open settings always). friendlyError texts at presenter.ts:46 and :48. explainStartError 'Press Check again' (host.ts:341) and host.ts:1183 surface in the bubble.
fix: Derive the button from the failure class: add 'Open settings' to session.error when friendlyError points to settings (sign-in, model, no access), and drop it for network and transient errors. Phrase bubble text without references to settings-window buttons.

title: Queued tasks show the purple "?" and are read as "Needs you:"
scenario: With two tasks running, a third queues. Its card detail says 'Waiting to start', but TaskManager publishes status 'waiting', so the card shows the 'waits for you' symbol in purple and screen readers hear 'Needs you: <task> Waiting to start'. The user is told something is needed from them when nothing is.
evidence: tasks.ts:292 maps queued to 'waiting'; overlay/main.ts:236 and handle/main.ts STATE_WORD.waiting = 'Needs you: '; shared/ember.css:170 draws the waiting symbol in --purple.
fix: Add a distinct 'queued' card status (neutral symbol, 'Queued: '), or map queued to running with the detail 'Waiting for a free slot'. Keep 'waiting' for tasks that are asking.

title: Connection progress rewrites the bubble on every download chunk
scenario: First connection to a host downloads Node (about 30 MB). The progress callback fires per network chunk, each firing calls bubble() and a full-state IPC to the overlay and the handle, although the text ('12 of 29 MB') changes only about 30 times. On a fast link that is hundreds to thousands of state pushes per second on the main thread and two renderers.
evidence: Scratch vitest: 30 MB in 16 KB chunks produced 1832 showState calls with a bubble but only 31 distinct texts. Callback per chunk at remote/runtime-download.ts:176; runtime.ts:1108-1109 (bubble per progress event) and remote/connections.ts:396.
fix: Skip the write when progressWords() equals the last words, or throttle to about 4 per second.

title: State chip and title repeat each other ('Thinking | Thinking…', 'Listening | Listening…', 'Showing you | Showing you')
scenario: While thinking the header reads 'Thinking  Thinking…'. When listening: 'Listening  Listening…'. For a guide step the chip says 'Showing you' and the step row says 'Showing you' (point_at). Errors read 'Problem  Something went wrong' above the real sentence. It makes the bubble look templated and wastes the header's limited width.
evidence: Chromium render s-thinking.png and s-guiding.png. presenter.ts:591 and :692 (title 'Thinking…'), main.ts:864 and :889 (title 'Listening…'), TOOL_STEPS.point_at 'Showing you' (presenter.ts:252, 264) vs BUBBLE_LABEL.guiding 'Showing you' (bubble.ts:26), presenter.ts:529 and :780 ('Something went wrong').
fix: Hide the title when it equals the chip's word (or drop the ellipsis title and let the chip carry it), vary the step text ('Pointing at it'), and title errors with what failed ('Couldn't reach Copilot') instead of 'Something went wrong'.

title: Mixed first/third person and jargon in bubble copy
scenario: One bubble says 'I can't reach Copilot' (title) and 'Ember can't reach GitHub right now. It will try again when the network is back.' (text). Others: 'Its running commands stop in 15 s unless the link comes back. Nothing new is sent meanwhile.' (static, 'link' and 's' jargon), 'Copying Ember's helper to build-01 (12 of 29 MB)…', 'Ember's Copilot runtime is missing or can't start. Reinstall Ember (sudo dnf reinstall ember).' and 'Ember connects with Windows' SSH. Add your key to Windows' ssh-agent, or connect once from PowerShell…'. The announcement 'On build-01. It starts in 4 seconds.' repeats the badge and stays '4 seconds' for the whole window. 'Thinking…' quotes the user's request cut at 120 characters with no ellipsis.
evidence: host.ts:303-312 and :339 (titles vs explainStartError), runtime.ts:646 and :1085, remote tests pin 'Copying Ember's helper…'; presenter.ts:641-644 (announce text), :591 (slice(0, 120)).
fix: Pick one voice (first person, as target-copy.ts's header says) and rewrite: 'build-01 hasn't answered for 5 seconds. Commands running there stop in 15 seconds unless it comes back.', 'Copying what Ember needs to build-01…', no commands in bubbles (settings only). Count the announcement down or say 'in a few seconds'. Add '…' when the quoted request is cut.

title: friendlyError leaves common failures as raw text: bare '400' and token-limit errors
scenario: A JSON-bodied 400 ('Error: 400 {…}') shows as 'Copilot reported a problem: 400'. A prompt-too-long error from a long conversation ('prompt token count of N exceeds the limit of M', code model_max_prompt_tokens_exceeded) is not matched by the context rule and shows as 'Copilot reported a problem: CAPIError: 400 prompt token count of 140000 exceeds the limit of 128000'. The user gets technical text and no next step.
evidence: Ran friendlyError on sample strings with the built bundle. 'Error: 400 {…}' gives 'Copilot reported a problem: 400'; 'CAPIError: 400 prompt token count … exceeds the limit' gives the raw text. The context rule at presenter.ts:50 matches only context length/limit/window, 'too long/large' and max tokens. The exact SDK message shapes are from memory of the Copilot API, so confidence is medium-low.
fix: Add /prompt token count|exceeds the limit|token_?limit|max_prompt_tokens/ to the context rule ('This conversation has got too long. Ask me again and I'll start fresh.'). When the stripped message is only a status code, say 'Copilot refused that request (400). Try rephrasing.'

title: target-copy.ts is a second, unused copy of the bubble words that unit tests pin
scenario: ui-copy.test.ts pins sshSeen, offerConnect, connecting, connected, stalled, lost, commandQuestion, announcement and more from target-copy.ts, but the app imports only signInAgain from it. The real strings are inline in runtime.ts, flow.ts and presenter.ts and already differ: the pinned command question reads 'On build-01. It's shown in full in Ember's command window.' while flow.ts:671 sends 'On build-01: <first finding>' plus 'Your task: …'. Anyone editing the real wording gets no test failure, and the pinned copy gives false assurance.
evidence: grep: only app/main/targets/runtime.ts:52 imports target-copy; test/unit/ui-copy.test.ts:565-599 asserts on its functions. Compare with runtime.ts:646, :692, :740 and flow.ts:671.
fix: Have runtime/flow/presenter build their bubbles from these functions (then the tests pin what users see), or delete the unused functions and pin the real strings.

title: A large answer opened with "Read all" can sit over Ember and the task cards
scenario: With task cards stacked at the right and Ember beside them, the expanded answer (410×391 px) fits neither below, above nor beside Ember without covering the cards, so clearPlace falls back to a position that overlaps Ember's face. Cosmetic only (the bubble stays clickable), but it hides Ember while the user reads.
evidence: Chromium sweep with two running tasks and an expanded answer: Ember at (1100,360) and (1250,360) gave the bubble at (712,8) and (862,8), size 410×391, overlapping Ember's body. Normal-size bubbles and long questions had no overlaps over a 42-position grid (cards, handle and Ember all cleared).
fix: When no clear place exists for an expanded bubble, prefer a spot beside Ember over the cards' area, or shrink its max-height (16 lines) to fit the larger free side.

title: A long unbroken run of letters, digits, dots or dashes in command output freezes Ember for seconds to hours (quadratic redaction regex)
area: commands: output shaping and secret redaction
scenario: Any command, or a hostile remote, that prints one long token freezes the Electron main process after the command ends: overlay, hotkeys and the stop chord are dead. Examples: `xxd -p -c0 big.bin`, `od ... | tr -d ' \n'`, `head -c 100000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a`, or a prompt-injected page or compromised SSH remote that prints 100 KB or more of one token. finishRun runs the redaction three times over the whole kept output (up to 4 MiB).
evidence: KEY_VALUE starts with `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` before the keyword alternation, so every start position rescans the whole run: redactSecrets('a'.repeat(n)) takes 4.5 s at 50 KB, 18 s at 100 KB and 70 s at 200 KB. Through the real runCommandTool flow with the local runner, `head -c 60000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a` took 19 s end to end. shapeOutput alone took 7.7 s on 60 KB, and flow.ts:950/955/956 call it, cleanOutput and redactSecrets again. At the 4 MiB keep cap the cost is hours. Dropping the leading class from the capture (it is kept unchanged in the output anyway) made a 4 MB run take 16 ms and gave identical results on 11 samples. A repeated 'password'x20000 still took 4.2 s.
fix: Drop `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` from the start of KEY_VALUE; the replacement keeps the prefix as it is. Also cut every line to a bounded length (for example 4 KiB, or OUTPUT_MAX_LINE) before running any regex over output in cleanOutput and the taint copy. Consider doing the shaping off the main thread.

title: Almost every real shell script asks, and it asks with generic or misleading words; the docs imply only dangerous scripts ask
scenario: A first-week user says 'run the build script', or the model runs `./gradlew build`, `./configure`, `./ci/test.sh` or `deploy.ps1`. The docs say the script is read and judged and that only one that deletes, publishes or reads secrets asks. In fact any script with an if, for, while, case, function, `[[ ]]` or trap, any script of more than 64 commands, and any script over 8,000 characters always asks. The card says 'In build.sh: Ember can't tell exactly what this does.' and also 'You didn't ask for this.' even though the user named the script.
evidence: judgeScripts classifies the 64 KiB-capped script text with classifyCommand, which applies MAX_COMMAND_CHARS=8000 (classify.ts:48), MAX_SIMPLE=64 (lex-posix.ts:71) and treats compound keywords as unclear (classify.ts:2775). In the real flow with the local runner, a benign script with one if and one for gave a card with 'In build.sh: Ember can't tell…'. A benign 90-line script gave 'In many.sh: It has more commands than Ember can check one by one.' A benign 12.7 KB script gave 'It is longer than Ember can check one by one.' Of 155 shell scripts found on this machine (under 64 KB), 143 produced only unclear findings. PowerShell `if` or `foreach` gives unclear.the-keyword-*, and cmd `if` or `for` gives unclear.cmd-*. The docs (COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:120-132, 250-254, L8), CHANGELOG and README say scripts up to 64 KB are 'read and judged' and only larger ones fall back to the name rule.
fix: At least say it in the docs and in L8: scripts with control flow, more than 64 commands or more than 8,000 characters always ask. Better: teach the lexers if/for/while/case/functions/`[[`, classify long scripts in chunks instead of applying the 8,000 and 64 limits, and word the card 'Ember can't read this script completely' without 'You didn't ask for this' when the user named it.

title: 'You asked for exactly this' matches questions, hypotheticals, past tense and instructions about scripts, so destructive or publishing commands announce instead of asking
scenario: The user says 'should I delete build/ or keep it?', 'how do I delete build/', 'list build/ and tell me if I can delete it', 'should I push my branch to GitHub?', 'I pushed my branch already' or 'fix the Makefile target that deletes build/'. If the worker then runs `rm -r build` or `git push origin <branch>`, the card is skipped for a 4-second 'Pushing feature-x to origin, as you asked.' countdown. Only the model has to choose to run it, but this is the headline safety rule ('Only what you typed or said counts').
evidence: matchIntent only rejects the NEGATION word list (not/never/don't…) and then accepts any verb form (delete, deletes, deleted, deleting) plus the object anywhere in the words (words.ts hasVerb/verbForms). With decideCommand and the real flow's inputs, these give verdict 'announce': 'should I delete build/ or keep it?', 'how do I delete build/', 'can you tell me how to delete the build folder', 'I might delete build/ later, but first list the files', 'list build/ and tell me if I can delete it', 'should I push my branch to GitHub?', 'explain how to push my branch to GitHub', 'I pushed my branch to GitHub already', 'I deleted build/ yesterday', 'the script that deletes build/ is broken, fix it'. Only 'don't', 'what happens if' and 'why can't' were caught.
fix: Require request framing: reject words containing a question mark or opening with how, should, can, could, what, why, whether or explain/tell me. Reject modal or hypothetical words (might, maybe, if, later) and past or relative forms (-ed or -s used as a relative clause). Accept the bare imperative, 'please', or 'can you / could you' plus the verb. Add the phrases above to the corpus.

title: Ordinary output marks the task as 'looks like instructions', so every later command asks (hostnamectl, docker info, kubectl describe node, inxi)
scenario: The user asks 'what OS is this machine?' and the model runs `hostnamectl`. Its 'Operating System: Ubuntu…' line matches `\b(assistant|system|developer)\s*:`, the result gets the note 'The output contained text that looks like instructions…', and every further command in the task asks with 'I'm checking each step: an earlier command printed text that looked like instructions.' The user thinks they are under attack.
evidence: outputTaint returns output.role-label for ' Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS' (hostnamectl, `docker info`, `kubectl describe node`), 'System:' (inxi), 'Developer: ACME', and 'File system: ext4'. Through the real flow, a hostnamectl-like printf produced the taint note in the tool result. 'The agent will run' (a CI log or README) matches output.addressed-request, and so does 'Ember … should run'.
fix: Anchor role labels to a line start or a chat transcript shape (for example `^(assistant|system)\s*:` after trimming, with no word before it). Drop 'developer' and the `Operating System:` shape. Require the addressed-request rules to name Ember or the assistant directly (not 'the agent').

title: Read-only cloud, Kubernetes and Terraform commands ask with 'Changes AWS.' (aws s3 ls, terraform validate/output/fmt/init, kubectl config current-context)
scenario: A cloud engineer asks 'list my S3 buckets' and gets a card saying 'Changes AWS. You didn't ask for this.' for `aws s3 ls`. The same happens for `terraform validate`, `terraform output`, `kubectl rollout status`, `kubectl config current-context`, `helm repo list` and `ansible-playbook --check`. The false warning trains people to click Allow without reading.
evidence: CLOUD_READ lacks ls, tail, validate, output, fmt, init, current-context, get-contexts, api-resources and rollout status, and classify.ts:3670-3676 turns every verb not in CLOUD_READ into cloud.change. `says.ts` run: `aws s3 ls` → ask 'Changes AWS.'; `aws logs tail` → ask; `terraform validate` → ask 'Changes the infrastructure.'; `kubectl config current-context` → ask 'Changes Kubernetes.'; while `aws s3 cp s3://b/k .` and `aws ec2 describe-instances` run. `gsutil ls` takes the same path.
fix: Add the read verbs to CLOUD_READ and special-case multi-word forms (s3 ls, config current-context and get-contexts, rollout status/history, repo list, state list/show). Use 'Ember can't tell whether this changes AWS' for unknown verbs instead of asserting a change.

title: Hyphenated or digit-bearing project, folder and branch names are taken for computers, which cancels the 'as you asked' path and puts a false line on the card
scenario: 'delete the build folder in my-project', 'delete build/ in my-app', 'remove dist on feature-x', 'clean the cache in step2'. Kebab-case repos and branches are everywhere. The command asks instead of announcing, and the card starts 'You named my-project, but this runs on this computer.', which suggests the user asked for another machine.
evidence: placesNamed('delete the build folder in my-project', []) → ['my-project']; likewise my-app, feature-x, step2, project.v2, the-repo-name and my-downloads. The docs (COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:173-180) list 'a hyphen or a digit' as the rule, so this is documented, but the card wording is wrong for these cases.
fix: Narrow the unknown-place rule: require ssh-style evidence (user@host, a dotted domain with a known TLD, an IP, a port) or a host-noun ('the server X'). Also treat a hyphenated word that exists as a folder or git ref in the task's folder as a place, not a computer. At minimum, change the card line to 'It looks like you named another computer (my-project)'.

title: Output bookkeeping re-copies a 4 MiB string on every chunk once output passes 4 MiB, saturating the main thread
scenario: A command that prints more than 4 MB (journalctl, find /, grep -r, a verbose build, cat of a big log) makes Ember's main process spend 100% CPU while it runs: the overlay stutters and the stop chord lags. The producer slows too, because its pipe backs up.
evidence: OutputKeeper.add does `this.tail += text` then `this.tail = this.tail.slice(cut)`, which flattens a 4 MB cons string per chunk. Copy of the class fed with real build-log text: 40 MB in 64 KB chunks took 2.0 s, 12 MB in 8 KB chunks took 2.5 s, 12 MB in 4 KB chunks took 5.1 s. With the real local runner (about 50 KB chunks), 26 MB of `seq` cost 1.6 s of keeper CPU (3.97 s for the whole tool call).
fix: Keep the tail as an array of chunks with a running length (as run/local.ts already does), and trim from the front only when the total passes 2x the cap.

title: The 'offer to bring Ember along when I run ssh' scan is on by default for everyone, including existing users who never accepted a card, against 'off until you turn them on'
scenario: After upgrading, an existing user who never touched SSH has Ember poll the window title every 2 s. When a terminal's title changes it reads the process list for `ssh` command lines (Linux /proc, macOS ps, a hidden PowerShell CIM query on Windows, and per running WSL distro). It can pop 'You're connected to X — Bring Ember there too?'. The docs open with 'All three are off until you turn them on… nothing new happens until they accept a card', and the first-run text is unchanged (CONSENT_VERSION 1).
evidence: `offerSsh: z.boolean().default(true)` (settings.ts:120); the noticer is enabled by `sshAllowed(admin()) && settings.get().targets.offerSsh` (runtime.ts:1025) with no host record or card required. computers-copy.ts shows the switch checked unless it is explicitly false. §4.1 describes the behaviour but the intro and CHANGELOG do not.
fix: Default offerSsh to false until the user has added a computer or accepted one SSH card (or ask once with the offer itself). Otherwise state it plainly in the intro, README and CHANGELOG as the one default-on behaviour.

title: The ssh noticer offers 'Bring Ember there' for non-interactive ssh such as git over ssh, scp and rsync
scenario: A developer pulls from GitHub over ssh (`git fetch`, an IDE's auto-fetch) or runs scp/rsync while their terminal's title changes. Ember offers 'You're connected to github.com — Bring Ember there too?', and Bring Ember then connects to GitHub's ssh server.
evidence: sshDestination stops at the first word after the destination ('the first other word after it starts the command') but still returns the destination. It returns {dest:'git@github.com'} for `ssh git@github.com git-upload-pack 'o/r.git'`, {dest:'build-01'} for `ssh -x -oForwardAgent=no … -- build-01 scp -t /tmp`, and {dest:'devbox'} for `ssh -T -D 1080 devbox bash`.
fix: Return null when words follow the destination (a remote command is present). Optionally also skip -T, -D and other non-interactive shapes and well-known git hosts.

title: The SSH consent card, README, CHANGELOG and docs understate the helper's size; the install extracts the whole Node distribution
area: docs/consent text vs code: SSH install
scenario: The consent card the user clicks Connect on says 'about 31 MB, unpacked to about 125 MB in ~/.local/share/ember-remote'. Reality is larger, and different on a Mac. Users on small or NFS-quota homes and IT admins are surprised.
evidence: Pinned Node 24.21.0 linux-x64: the tar.xz is 31,890,184 bytes (sha256 matches remote-runtime.json) plus 0.8 MB of parts, i.e. about 33 MB. The gz fallback used when the remote has no xz is 58,088,022 bytes. It unpacks to 208 MB (bin/node 121 MB, include/ 67 MB, lib/ 19 MB). The docs (COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:389-393) say 29 MB download and 125 MB unpacked. The card always names the Linux path even though macOS remotes install under ~/Library/Application Support/Ember Remote. The bootstrap untars everything with --strip-components=1.
fix: Correct the numbers (about 33 MB, or 59 MB without xz; about 210 MB unpacked) in the card, README, CHANGELOG and docs. Exclude include/ and lib/node_modules from the extraction (saves roughly 80 MB). Make the card's path OS-neutral, or ask the OS first.

title: Docs describe three behaviours the code doesn't have: a task-triggered commands card, a WSL offer on first sight, and Wayland remotes with controls
scenario: A user or admin follows §2.1 'The first time you turn one on (or a task needs one), Ember shows the card…': with commands off (the default), run_command isn't even offered to the model, so no card ever comes from a task. §3.1 says 'When Ember first sees WSL it offers…': the offer only appears after the user's request names WSL while it is off. §1's table says an SSH Linux Wayland desktop gives 'reading and using controls': packaged builds never enable that, so Wayland remotes (the default on RHEL 8 and 9 GNOME and recent Ubuntu) are commands only.
evidence: commandCapability returns 'off' when settings.commands[id].on is false (local-service.ts:53), and worker.commandShells() returns null for 'off' (worker.ts:963), so there is no run_command tool and no flow.ts step-2 card unless a card version was bumped. offerWsl() is called only from the bind path in runtime.ts:1279 when the user said 'in WSL'. app/remote/main.ts:205 sets `waylandText: !o.packaged && EMBER_REMOTE_WAYLAND === '1'`. §4.4 and L5 are right; the §1 table row (line 25) contradicts them.
fix: Edit §2.1 ('the card appears when you turn the switch on in Settings'), §3.1 ('when you ask for something in WSL while it is off') and the §1 Wayland row ('none yet: commands only'). Do the same in CHANGELOG where it repeats them.

title: The shipped example policy omits the new keys, and the exec-denied message points to an 'Ember remote package' that doesn't exist
scenario: An RHEL admin copies /usr/share/doc/ember/policy.example.json to /etc/ember/policy.json as the starting point. It has no commands, features.wsl/ssh or ssh section, so commands are silently off everywhere while SSH and WSL stay allowed. Nothing in the example shows how to change either. On a fapolicyd or noexec remote the user is told to 'ask its administrator… to install the Ember remote package', which does not exist; §6.6 says it is 'planned'.
evidence: packaging/policy.example.json holds only the pre-release keys and is installed by packaging/rpm/ember.spec:76 and :112. ssh-errors.ts:60 (execDenied) and docs §4.8 line 505 quote the 'remote package' sentence while COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:628 says a root-owned remote package is planned.
fix: Add features.wsl, features.ssh, commands and ssh (with allowedHosts and desktop) to the example, with a comment key or a README beside it saying that a policy without `commands` turns commands off. Reword the message to the fapolicyd or noexec fix only, until the package ships.

title: After the merge nothing runs the SSH, WSL and commands integration suites on PRs, main or release tags; the primary platform's old ssh client is never exercised; Linux arm64 is untested
scenario: remote.yml triggers on push only for branches `ember-improve/20261022-sshwsl-*`, dispatch, and a weekly macOS-only cron. After merge, regressions in script(1), sshd, the bootstrap, WSL and PowerShell commands are not caught by PRs or the v* release tag (ci.yml runs only unit tests for them). The client side is always the runner's OpenSSH 9.6, but the RHEL 8 PC uses OpenSSH 8.0 (askpass through DISPLAY, no SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE), which no job runs. The test sshds disable password and keyboard-interactive auth, so password, passphrase and 2FA prompts through a real ssh are only unit tested. Linux arm64 remotes are advertised and shipped (Node arm64 pinned, koffi arm64) but no job installs or runs one.
evidence: on.push.branches in remote.yml:12-14; no pull_request trigger; schedule runs only ssh-macos (`if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || …`). ssh-linux and ssh-el8 install the client from the Ubuntu 24.04 runner (ssh-el8 uses Rocky 8 only as the server); sshd configs set `PasswordAuthentication no` and `KbdInteractiveAuthentication no`. `grep -i arm remote.yml` finds nothing.
fix: Add `pull_request` (paths-filtered to app/main/{commands,remote,wsl,targets}, app/remote, scripts/package) and `tags: [v*]` triggers. Run ssh-transport inside a rockylinux:8 container as the client as well. Add a password or keyboard-interactive sshd case (sshpass or an askpass fake) and an ubuntu-24.04-arm job.

title: Downloaded Node archives in userData are never pruned
scenario: Every Ember release that bumps the pinned Node leaves the previous archive (32 MB xz, or 58 MB gz) per target in ~/.config/ember/remote/runtime/ for ever, including after 'Forget'. Over a few releases a user accumulates hundreds of MB.
evidence: ensureRuntime writes <userData>/remote/runtime/<file> and only checks cachedOk for the pinned file; connections.ts:394 is the only user and nothing deletes other files in that folder.
fix: After a successful ensureRuntime, delete files in the folder that aren't the pinned name (and any *.part older than a day). Mention the folder in the README's uninstall list.

title: With commands off (the default, and for every upgraded user) Ember says it 'doesn't act in terminals' and never mentions Settings › Commands
scenario: An existing user reads the release notes and says 'run df -h'. Ember replies that it doesn't act in terminals and offers to guide them. There is no pointer to Settings › Commands, no 'Open settings' button (WSL has one, and only after the user names WSL), and existing users get no first-run page (L1).
evidence: methodRule(words, false) returns the old 'it doesn't act in terminals' text whenever PromptCaps.commands is false, which is every user until the switch and card. runtime.ts:1048-1054 is the only 'Open settings' offer.
fix: When commands are available but off, let the conductor say 'Commands are off — turn them on in Settings › Commands' and show an 'Open settings' bubble button, once per run.

title: Duplicate sshClientRow in ssh-config.ts is dead code and disagrees with the doctor row (fail vs warn)
scenario: A future caller of the unused helper would make a missing or old OpenSSH a 'fail' in `ember doctor`, although docs §5 say it is only ever a warning (SSH is optional) and targets/doctor.ts:50 does that.
evidence: grep finds sshClientRow(os, path, v) used only by test/unit/ssh-config.test.ts; the setup check and doctor use targets/doctor.ts sshClientRow. The two return different statuses for the same input.
fix: Delete the ssh-config.ts copy and its tests, or have doctor.ts call it with the warn mapping.

title: Command window: Tab, Shift+Tab and Esc are swallowed by the terminal, so keyboard focus cannot leave it
area: Command window: keyboard operability (WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap)
scenario: A keyboard-only user presses Tab from a run's command block. Focus enters xterm's hidden 'Terminal input' textarea and stays there. Tab, Shift+Tab and Esc are all consumed: on an interactive run they are sent to the process as \t, ESC[Z and ESC. The Stop or Close button and the other tabs sit after the terminal in the DOM, so they are not reachable from inside it. Even a non-interactive run (typing hint: 'This command can't take typing here') traps focus the same way, because xterm cancels Tab before it checks disableStdin. The typing hint names no way out. Alt+Tab away and back lands on the terminal again. The only in-window recovery is a mouse click, or leaving the terminal via the tab strip (Shift+Tab wraps through BODY to Stop). The keyboard-only way to stop is the global Ctrl+Alt+X, which stops everything.
evidence: Chromium run of dist/app/renderer/command with stubbed emberCommands (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/ux-a11y/xterm-trap.mjs and xterm-trap2.mjs). Tab order: tab button -> PRE.command -> TEXTAREA.xterm-helper-textarea and then it never moves. Five Tabs, one Shift+Tab and one Esc sent ['\t' x5, '\u001b[Z', '\u001b'] to the run (interactive case). In the non-interactive case nothing was sent and focus still did not move. DOM order in app/renderer/command/main.ts:278 is panel.append(header, block, host /*terminal*/, typing, foot /*status + Stop|Close*/). With term.attachCustomKeyEventHandler(e => e.key !== 'Tab') on xterm 5.5, Tab left the terminal (xterm-fix2.mjs). terminal.ts has no key handler.
fix: In createRunTerminal call term.attachCustomKeyEventHandler. For non-interactive runs return false for Tab and Shift+Tab (or give the helper textarea tabindex=-1). For interactive runs keep Tab for the process but add a documented escape (for example Esc then Tab, or Ctrl+Shift+M as VS Code does) and name it in TYPING_HINT. Also move the status line and Stop|Close before the terminal in DOM and Tab order. Add a unit test next to renderer-command.test.ts.

title: Command output is invisible to screen readers: xterm runs with screenReaderMode:false, so its rows are aria-hidden
scenario: A blind user asks Ember to run 'npm test' or answers an interactive prompt such as sudo or ssh in the command window ('where you can watch and stop them'). A screen reader finds 'Terminal input' (an edit box) and nothing else: the program's output, prompts and errors are not in the accessibility tree. The user cannot read what the command printed, cannot read a prompt they are asked to type an answer to, and cannot tell why a run failed beyond the status line ('Ended with exit code 2'). This is the central surface of the new commands feature. The README and docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md do not list it among the limitations (L1-L26).
evidence: CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree for a run that received 'PASS src/a.test.ts / FAIL src/b.test.ts': the tabpanel contains only generic 'What the command shows' > textbox 'Terminal input'. No node contains 'PASS' or 'FAIL', and none is ignored-with-text. DOM: .xterm-rows has aria-hidden="true" and its text is 'PASS src/a.test.tsFAIL src/b.test.ts' (command2.mjs). In xterm 5.5, screenReaderMode:true adds .xterm-accessibility with an aria-live='assertive' region (xterm-fix.mjs); false adds nothing. The option is pinned at terminal-options.ts:43 ('exactly as §3.10 sets them'). A non-interactive run also still exposes a focusable 'Terminal input' textbox that accepts nothing, which is misleading.
fix: Turn screenReaderMode on when assistive technology is active. Have main send sys.a11y.screenReaderOn() (it already exists) to the command page, or default to true, and pass it to terminalOptions. Update the options pin in renderer-command.test.ts. Give non-interactive runs a non-focusable helper textarea. Add the limitation to docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md if it stays.

title: No forced-colors support: under Windows contrast themes switches, the slider, selection state, focus rings and button edges disappear
area: All windows: Windows High Contrast / contrast themes (WCAG 1.4.1, 1.4.11, 2.4.7, 4.1.2)
scenario: A Windows 10/11 user with a contrast theme (Settings > Accessibility > Contrast themes) opens Ember. In settings: the 'Listen for Hey Ember', 'Speak replies', 'Start Ember when I log in' and Calm mode switches are invisible (no track, no knob, no on/off), the Size slider is invisible, the selected character card is not marked, the status dots are gone, and the 'Remove' buttons are plain text. Keyboard focus is invisible everywhere. The command window shows 'Allow' and 'Not now' as bare words with no button shape or primary distinction, and the selected tab is not marked (every tab looks the same). The overlay's task cards lose their state symbol (ring, question mark, tick, cross), so 'working vs failed' is not shown at all. The bubble's Allow and Not now lose their capsules and focus ring. Everything stays unchanged for the screen reader.
evidence: No @media (forced-colors) rule or forced-color-adjust anywhere (grep over app/ and packages/ CSS and bubble.ts). Chromium run with forcedColors:'active' (forced.mjs, forced2.mjs, forced3.mjs). Screenshots: scratchpad/release-review/ux-a11y/home-forced.png, home-forced-voice.png, forced-active-switch-focus.png (compare forced-none-switch-focus.png), forced-active-btn-focus.png (no ring on the focused 'Remove KeePassXC'), overlay-forced.png (cards have no symbol), cmd-forced.png. Cause: all control chrome is drawn with background-color, box-shadow and mask-background, which forced colors remove or override. Examples: ember.css:195 `.btn:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:… }`, the switch rules at ember.css:207-232, overlay/styles.css:57-58 (.task::before mask), bubble.ts:292-306 (.eb-actions button), home/styles.css:85-101 (range) and 100-ish (.card). The overlay stays transparent in forced colors (alpha 0 verified), so it is not a screen-covering bug. PLAN.md manual item 14 ('Windows contrast themes keep the bubble readable') is still owed.
fix: Add an @media (forced-colors: active) block to ember.css, bubble.ts BUBBLE_CSS and each page's styles. Give every control a real 1px ButtonText border. Replace outline:none with outline:2px solid Highlight on :focus-visible. Draw the switch with a border and a Highlight-filled checked state. Set forced-color-adjust:none on mask symbols and dots and fill them with CanvasText, LinkText or GrayText. Give the selected card and tab an outline or border, and the slider a ButtonText track and thumb. Then run PLAN item 14 on a real Windows contrast theme.

title: A shortcut taken by another app leaves keyboard-only users no way to ask Ember; the offered fallback is the mouse-only handle and shortcuts cannot be remapped
area: Keyboard operability of the primary entry points (WCAG 2.1.1)
scenario: On Windows with PowerToys (the README notes its Command Palette uses Win+Alt+Space, Xbox Game Bar uses Win+Alt+M), Ember's Ask shortcut fails to register. The setup check says: 'Another app already uses Win+Alt+Space. Use Ember's handle in the bottom-right corner instead.' The handle window is focusable:false and its button has no keyboard route. Settings has no ask field, and there is no setting to rebind any shortcut. A user who cannot use a pointer (keyboard, switch, screen reader) cannot ask Ember anything. Relaunching Ember does open Settings (second-instance handler, main.ts:325), but nothing there can send a request. Voice ('Hey Ember') is the only other route. The greeting (main.ts:441) gives the same 'click my handle' advice.
evidence: main.ts:1283-1295 registers each accelerator once and retries every 60 s. There is no remap setting (grep of settings.ts and ipc.ts shows none). handle.ts:49 and overlay.ts:282 create their windows with focusable:false. environment.ts:121 and main.ts:441 point users at the handle. README.md 'Shortcuts' paragraph names the known Windows conflicts.
fix: Offer user-configurable shortcuts in Settings (Comfort and access), or pick a documented fallback chord automatically when one is taken. Add a keyboard route that does not need a global chord: an 'Ask Ember' field or button in the settings window, and an Ask entry in the Start menu or app-launcher jump list. Change the setup-check wording so it does not send keyboard users to the mouse-only handle.

title: Announced commands start after a fixed 4 s with no keyboard hint; the Stop button is mouse-only and the countdown cannot be extended
area: Timeouts and keyboard operability (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable, 2.1.1)
scenario: A user asks by voice or text for something Ember announces instead of asking about (a push, an overwrite they requested). The bubble says 'Pushing feature-x to origin, as you asked. On this computer. It starts in 4 seconds.' with a Stop button, and the command runs when the countdown ends. For a screen-reader, switch or slow-reading user that is too short to hear the announcement (about 20 words, 6 s or more at normal reading speed; the bubble's live region and Ember's own speech read it at the same time), find the control and act. The Stop button is in the overlay (focusable:false) or in the command window, which is opened with showInactive. Nothing in the bubble, the spoken text or the command window card says Ctrl+Alt+X stops it. Ordinary questions do carry a key hint, and announcements do not.
evidence: flow.ts:175 `ANNOUNCE_MS = 4000`; flow.ts:700-710 awaits svc.window.announce(card, ANNOUNCE_MS). presenter.ts:634-646 announce() sets step: null, actions: [Stop] and calls onAnnounce(text), which speaks only the words. The questions' hint comes from Confirmer.keyHint (confirm.ts:222), which announcements do not use. renderer/command/main.ts:203-225 buildAnnounce has the countdown (role=timer, aria-live off by default) and Stop, with no key hint. commands/window.ts:228-230 reveal() uses showInactive. Live region content checked in overlay.mjs: 'Ember needs you: <title> <thought>', no key.
fix: Lengthen the window when a screen reader is on (sys.a11y.screenReaderOn()) or add a 'More time to react' setting (for example 15 s or ask-always). Put 'Press Ctrl+Alt+X to stop' in the announcement bubble, in its live-region text and in the spoken line. Consider answering the announcement with Ctrl+Alt+N like a question.

title: SSH, WSL and command-card bubble actions have no keyboard or screen-reader route, and the model is told to tell the user to 'click' them
scenario: The overlay and handle windows are focusable:false, so bubble buttons cannot be tabbed to. Only Confirmer questions get global keys (Ctrl+Alt+Y/N, main.ts:655-662). Everything else is mouse-only: 'Bring Ember' / 'Not now' / 'Don't offer again' (SSH seen offer, runtime.ts:958-975), 'Connect' (offer_connect), Reconnect / Stop trying / Disconnect / Cancel, 'Read all' on a long answer, 'Show the command' / 'Read it' on a command or consent question, and Always in app (click-only by design). For offer_connect the tool result tells the model 'Tell them to click it' or 'connect it from Ember's menu' (runtime.ts:1382, 1389, 1189). The handle menu is not keyboard-reachable either. A keyboard or screen-reader user is told to click a button they cannot reach. Equivalent routes exist (Settings > Computers, Ctrl+Alt+X, Conversation in Settings) but are never mentioned.
evidence: windows created with focusable:false (handle.ts:49, overlay.ts:282). bubbleAction ids owned by the targets runtime (runtime.ts:1420-1475) are plain bubble actions, not Confirmer questions, so Ctrl+Alt+Y/N does nothing for them (confirm.ts answerKey only reaches the current question). presenter.ts:769 'Read all' is ui:more. The live-region text built by announcement() (packages/bubble/src/bubble.ts:50-61) names no keys.
fix: Say the keyboard route in the offer text and in the tool result ('or open Settings > Computers (Ctrl+Alt+E)'). Add key answers for offers (the same Ctrl+Alt+Y/N while an offer is up) or a focusable fallback, and give 'Read the last answer' a shortcut.

title: Command block is a focusable <pre> with aria-label, so a screen reader gets a label for the command instead of the command
area: Command window: names and roles (ARIA 1.2 naming prohibited on generic)
scenario: A screen-reader user Tabs to the card's command block (it has tabIndex=0 so it can be scrolled). It is exposed as a generic with the name 'The command, every character shown', and many readers speak the name and not the text. The safety-critical content (the command, with zero-width and mixed-script characters made visible) is only reached by browse-mode reading. Tabbing to Allow gives no description of the command either.
evidence: CDP tree (command.mjs): `generic name="The command, every character shown" focusable=true` with the command only as a child StaticText. axe reports aria-prohibited-attr (needs review) on this node, for both the card and the tab panel's block. The ask card in the same window labels its region from the heading, which works.
fix: Use role='textbox' aria-readonly='true' aria-multiline='true' with the aria-label (the command is then its value), or role='group' with aria-labelledby pointing at the heading and the command itself as content; remove the aria-label from the bare <pre>. Give Allow aria-describedby pointing at the command block.

title: Setup-check fix buttons all have the same name ('Turn on', 'Open System Settings'), unlike every other list button
scenario: On macOS a VoiceOver user setting up permissions Tabs to four identical 'Open System Settings' buttons (Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Microphone) and hears no indication which pane each opens. On Linux and Windows several 'Turn on' buttons are the same. The rows' computers, grants and never-look buttons already carry specific aria-labels.
evidence: AX tree of the settings window with two failing checks: `button 'Turn on'` twice with listitem names empty (home.mjs). Code: `btn.textContent = platform?.fixLabels[fix] ?? 'Turn on'` and no aria-label or aria-describedby.
fix: Set btn.setAttribute('aria-label', `${label text}: ${c.label}`) or aria-describedby on the row's label span, so the name reads 'Open System Settings: Screen Recording'.

title: First-run: focus is dropped to <body> when Start Ember removes its own button
scenario: A keyboard or screen-reader user ticks 'I agree' and presses Start Ember. The page then hides the start row (and the Start button that holds focus) and reveals all the after-setup sections. Focus falls to the document body, and nothing announces that setup finished or where they are. The tagline is the only live text.
evidence: Chromium run (home-focus.mjs): focus on #start, Enter, then the settings echo with onboarded:true. document.activeElement === BODY and start-row hidden=true. $('start').addEventListener('click') (line 150) only calls updateSettings. By contrast renderAgent hands focus on when its buttons disappear.
fix: When onboarded flips to true while Start (or #agree) has focus, move focus to the 'Your Ember' heading (like showSection) or to the tagline region, and put 'Ember has started' in the status line.

title: Timeouts users cannot extend: questions expire after 120 s, answers and errors hide after 6-30 s with no way to pause
scenario: A switch-access or one-handed user needs more than 2 minutes to reach Allow or Not now and the question silently expires as 'no'. A slow reader or a user with low vision gets an answer bubble that hides after 6000 ms plus 50 ms per character (30 s cap) and error notices after 12 s; the bubble is click-through, so hovering cannot hold it. INFO bubbles last 7 s (runtime.ts:391). The only retrieval routes are 'Read the last answer' in the mouse-only handle menu and the Conversation section in Settings.
evidence: confirm.ts:97 `timeoutMs ?? 120_000`; presenter.ts:672 and :803 hideLater(min(30000, 6000 + n*50)); presenter.ts:532/546/783 12 000; main.ts:454 greeting 7 s or 15 s. No setting adjusts any of them; voice follow-up is a fixed 8 s too (README/consent text).
fix: Add a 'Keep messages until I dismiss them' (or 'More time') setting that lengthens or disables the auto-hide and the question expiry, and give 'Read the last answer' a global shortcut.

title: Question live-region text omits the answer keys; with Ember's speech disabled by policy a screen-reader user is never told them
scenario: A question appears. The bubble shows its key hint ('Ctrl+Alt+Y allow · Ctrl+Alt+N not now') in the step row, but announcement() builds the live-region message from title and thought only. Ember's own spoken question adds 'Press Control Alt Y…' only when maySpeak() is true. If the organisation sets features.speak=false, the screen reader says 'Ember needs you: May I click Save…?' and never says how to answer, and the bubble's buttons are not reachable. For command questions the spoken text (questionWords) never names the keys or says to Alt+Tab to the command window.
evidence: overlay.mjs live region: 'Ember needs you: May I click Save in Mousepad? Ember wants to click the Save button.' (step text appears in the page but not in the live region). main.ts:689-693 and runtime.ts:1566-1580 questionWords.
fix: Append the step text (the key hint) to the announced message for mood 'attention' and, for command and consent questions, add 'It is in the Ember commands window; press Alt+Tab to read it'.

title: Ask box: 'Ember will see: …' arrives after the field is focused and is only a description, so screen-reader users are not told what Ember will read
area: Ask box: announcements and privacy transparency (WCAG 4.1.3)
scenario: Ctrl+Alt+Space opens the box and focuses the field. The screen reader reads the field's name and description at once (place chip, key hints). A moment later the quick look finishes and 'Ember will see: Mousepad · notes.txt · 12 words selected' is filled in. A description change is not announced, so the privacy line that exists so 'nothing is sent by surprise' is never spoken unless the user re-focuses the field.
evidence: main.ts:777 askWindow.show(..., { sees: null, ... }) then main.ts:780 callContext.then(... askWindow.setContext). In ask/main.ts the context handler sets #sees and calls input.focus() (already focused). AX tree (askdesk.mjs) shows the description only after the update.
fix: Make #sees (or a visually hidden copy) a role='status' aria-live='polite' region so the late text is announced, or delay focusing until the context has arrived.

title: Desk 'Take over' mode sends every key, Tab included, to the desk; the way out (Ctrl+Alt+End) is not exposed to assistive technology
area: Desk window: No Keyboard Trap advisory (WCAG 2.1.2)
scenario: A screen-reader user activates Take over and focus moves to the picture. All keys including Tab and Escape now go to the desk. The only way back is Ctrl+Alt+End, written in the header's visible hint, but the focused element is an image named only 'What Ember is doing on its desk' and has no description. The user is not told how to leave.
evidence: AX tree in control mode (askdesk.mjs): image 'What Ember is doing on its desk' focusable, with no description; the hint is a StaticText in the banner. img.tabIndex=0 at desk/main.ts:45 even when not taken over.
fix: Give #screen aria-describedby pointing at #hint, or set its alt/aria-label to 'Ember's desk. Your keys go to the desk. Press Ctrl+Alt+End to hand back' while control is on, and use a live region to say 'You have the keyboard on the desk'.
