title: Ember speaks aloud whenever a screen reader runs, with no way to turn it off, and the macOS module comment says the opposite
scenario: maySpeak() is true whenever 'Speak replies' is on or a screen reader is detected. The user's 'Speak replies' switch cannot switch it off while a screen reader is running. Ember's own local voice then speaks answers, questions, task results and announcements at the same time as the screen reader reads the bubble's live region (or on top of it), so a user with a braille display or who prefers the reader's voice cannot get one voice. Only Ctrl+Alt+X (hush) stops it for the moment. darwin/system/a11y.ts's header says VoiceOver detection exists so 'Ember then doesn't speak over it', which is the reverse of what main.ts does; the Windows and Linux probes make the same call.
evidence: main.ts:702 `policy.features.speak !== false && (settings.get().speak || sys.a11y.screenReaderOn())`; used at main.ts:689, 1513, 1529, 1545. Settings copy in home/index.html ('With a screen reader running, Ember also speaks its questions and results'). darwin/system/a11y.ts:2-3 header comment. Chromium cannot show how the reader and Ember overlap; this is from the code.
fix: Make speech a three-way setting (Automatic when a screen reader runs / Always / Never) so an explicit 'Never' wins, and correct the macOS comment or decide the intended behaviour. If the reader reliably voices the live regions, speak only what they cannot (announcements, command questions).

title: Settings: the Size slider's <output> is an implicit live region, so each arrow key speaks the new value twice
scenario: A screen-reader user changes the character size with the arrow keys. The slider's aria-valuetext announces '62 pixels' and the <output id='size-out'> (role status, live polite) also announces '62 px'.
evidence: AX tree (home.mjs): `slider 'Size '` with `LabelText > status '' live='polite'`. `<label for='size'>Size <output id='size-out' for='size'>…</output></label>`.
fix: Add role='presentation' aria-live='off' to the output (or make it a plain <span aria-hidden='true'>) and keep aria-valuetext as the one source.

title: No text-size control for the overlay, bubble, cards, ask box or command and prompt windows (11-14 px fixed)
scenario: A low-vision user raises the OS text size. Ember's floating surfaces do not follow it: the bubble body is 14 px, steps 13 px, hints and chips 11-12 px, and the ask box key hints about 10.5 px. The overlay, handle and ask box cannot be zoomed (no focus, no menu); the fixed 440x300 prompt and the command windows can be zoomed but scale into clipped content. The 'Size' setting scales only the character.
evidence: Type tokens in ember.css:20-27 and bubble.ts:186, 282, 227 use fixed px. Windows are created fixed-size (windows.ts:76-92). No setting for text size exists in settings.ts.
fix: Add a 'Text size' setting (or follow the OS scale) that multiplies the type tokens and the bubble's CSS, and let the prompt and command windows grow with it.

title: No accessibility documentation: README and docs say nothing about screen-reader behaviour, keyboard routes or known gaps
area: Screen reader compatibility notes (Orca, NVDA, Narrator, VoiceOver)
scenario: A screen-reader or keyboard-only user cannot find which controls have a keyboard route, that the overlay and handle cannot be focused, that Ember speaks aloud when a screen reader runs, that Ctrl+Alt+X is the way to stop an announced command, how to read a command before allowing it (Alt+Tab to 'Ember commands'), or how to leave the desk and the terminal. Only a sentence in docs/DEVELOPING.md:129 and the settings 'Comfort and access' note mention it. COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 do not list the terminal's missing screen-reader mode.
evidence: grep -n -i 'screen reader|Orca|NVDA|Narrator|VoiceOver' README.md docs/*.md: only DEVELOPING.md:129 and DESIGN.md:78. PLAN.md manual item 14 is the only plan for testing Narrator, NVDA and VoiceOver.
fix: Add an 'Accessibility' section to the README: per-OS reader notes, a keyboard-route table for every bubble, card, window and mouse-only action, speech behaviour, and the known gaps from this report.

title: Handle's microphone and computer-state dots are colour-only and hidden from assistive technology
scenario: The persistent 'is my microphone listening, muted or broken' indicator is an 8 px dot (orange, grey or red) whose words live only in a title tooltip on an aria-hidden <i>. Colour-blind users cannot tell orange from red, and screen-reader users get nothing. The remote computer's state dot (green, amber, grey, red) is also colour-only visually (the words are only in the tooltip and aria-label). 'Microphone off' is shown as text for 2.5 s after toggling (main.ts:845) and then is gone.
evidence: handle/index.html `<i id='mic' class='mic' hidden aria-hidden='true'>`; handle/styles.css:25-28 and 52-58; handle/main.ts:119 sets only title.
fix: Add a short visible or sr-only word to the handle line ('Mic off', 'Hearing you') or a distinct shape per state, and expose it in the handle's accessible text.

title: Prompt window exposes role=dialog on the <main> element, replacing the main landmark
scenario: A screen reader on the SSH password, host-key or consent card finds no main landmark; the dialog still announces its name and description.
evidence: axe-core on every card kind: [minor] aria-allowed-role 'ARIA role dialog is not allowed for given element' on #card (prompt.mjs). Dialog name and description were correct in the Chromium tree.
fix:
Use

and keep the dialog.

title: Ctrl+Alt+Space does nothing when Caps Lock (or Win) is remapped to Ctrl (or Alt)
area: hotkey chord check (x11.ts keysDown, hotkey.ts freshAskPress)
scenario: A user turned on GNOME Tweaks > Keyboard & Mouse > Caps Lock behavior > 'Make Caps Lock an additional Ctrl' (XKB ctrl:nocaps), or Alt/Win remaps such as altwin:alt_win or altwin:ctrl_alt_win. They press Caps + Alt + Space. Electron's global shortcut fires, but Ember's re-report guard asks x11.keysDown() whether Ctrl and Alt are down. keysDown() maps Control_L to ONE keycode with XKeysymToKeycode, which returns the lowest keycode (the real Left Ctrl, 37), so a Ctrl produced by another key reads as not held. freshAskPress() then rejects the press: the log gets 'ask.hotkey_ignored' and the ask box never opens. Nothing is shown to the user. The handle menu and the wake word are the only ways in for these users.
evidence: Reproduced exactly: setxkbmap -option ctrl:nocaps, XTest-pressing keycodes 66+64+65 (Caps, Alt, Space). x11.keysDown() returned {control:false,alt:true,space:true}, so freshAskPress() is false. The real Left Ctrl (37) gives control:true. An Electron 44 main-process test with globalShortcut.register('Control+Alt+Space') under the same keymap printed 'CALLBACK fired; Ember's keysDown() says {control:false,...}' for the Caps chord. With altwin:swap_alt_win (Alt on a different key) the Alt check also depends on keycode lookup. Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/k1.ts and gs/main.js. Caller: app/main/main.ts:1273-1274, guard: app/main/hotkey.ts:25.
fix: Stop deriving the chord from a single keycode per keysym. Use the modifier state the server already reports: XQueryPointer's mask (x11.pointer() already returns it) with ControlMask (4) and Mod1Mask (8), or XkbGetState's mods. That is the same state the X grab matched on, so every remap works. Add a unit test with a keymap where Control_L sits on two keycodes.

title: GNOME Typing Assist (Slow/Bounce/Sticky Keys) makes Ember's keys vanish or corrupt, and its chords switch Sticky Keys off
area: XTest keyboard input vs AccessX (hands/input.ts keycode, borrow.ts keys/type)
scenario: A user has Slow Keys, Bounce Keys or Sticky Keys on (Settings > Universal Access > Typing Assist, which sets XKB AccessX controls on the core keyboard). Ember's synthetic keys go through the same filters. Slow Keys (300 ms): press_keys 'ctrl+a' or Ctrl+V, and the type path, are dropped completely, yet the borrow reports success ('Done with the user's mouse...'). Bounce Keys: repeated letters or digits are swallowed, e.g. 'hello world' arrives as 'helo world', and a Ctrl press inside the debounce window is dropped so 'v' can be typed as text instead of pasting. In LibreOffice Calc, fillCell types the cell and presses Enter BEFORE it checks, so a bounced '100' is committed as '10' and the error then says the sheet 'still shows 10 ... didn't take it'. Sticky Keys with GNOME's default 'disable if two keys are pressed together': the first Ember chord (Ctrl held while A goes down) switches the user's Sticky Keys off, and GNOME's keyboard-accessibility daemon follows the server state. The user must re-enable it by hand.
evidence: Xvfb, XkbSetControls on the core keyboard, then Ember's CursorBorrow type('hello world') + keys('ctrl+a') into a focused window. Normal: received 'hello world' plus Ctrl+A. Slow Keys 300 ms: received '' and 0 Ctrl+A events, no error from the borrow. Bounce Keys 500 ms: received 'helo world'. Sticky Keys with TwoKeys: enabled_ctrls bit true before, false after Ember pressed Ctrl+A (the app did see Ctrl+A). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/a1.ts and a2.ts. Nothing in app/ or docs/ mentions AccessX (grep). The desk is a private X server, so it is unaffected.
fix: Read XkbGetControls().enabled_ctrls (XkbSlowKeysMask 1<<1, XkbBounceKeysMask 1<<2, XkbStickyKeysMask 1<<3) before a keyboard borrow. Give XInput a blockedReason() on X11 that refuses with a plain sentence ('Typing Assist (Slow, Bounce or Sticky Keys) is on, so Ember can't use your keyboard; the desk still works'). Add a check-up row. Mouse-only borrows can still go. If pacing is preferred instead: hold each key longer than slow_keys_delay and wait longer than debounce_delay between presses of one key, which cannot be done for Sticky Keys' two-key rule. Do not auto-disable and restore: a crash would leave the user's setting off.

title: keys('ctrl+1') presses Ctrl+Shift+1 on layouts that type digits shifted (French, Belgian, Czech...)
area: shortcut key choice (borrow.ts keys, win32/keys.ts virtualKeyFor)
platforms: windows (verified in a simulation), linux (same Shift in the key state)
scenario: On Windows with a French AZERTY layout (or Belgian, Czech, Slovak), the user approves 'press ctrl+1' (switch to the first tab, or Format Cells in Excel). Windows has no KeyLayout, so keys() uses x.needsShift(sym). For a digit, win32/keys.ts:146 sets shift:true on layouts where VkKeyScan says the digit needs Shift. keys() then adds Shift_L and presses Ctrl+Shift+VK_1. Apps match VKs, so Chrome and Edge do nothing for Ctrl+Shift+1, and Excel applies the Number format to the selected cells (Ctrl+Shift+!) instead of opening Format Cells. The user approved 'ctrl+1', not Ctrl+Shift+1. 'alt+1' and 'ctrl+0' have the same fault. A physical user on these layouts presses Ctrl+& with no Shift. (Typing a bare digit, 'press 1', correctly needs the Shift.)
evidence: Simulation with openWin32Input and a fake Win32Api whose VkKeyScanExW answers French ('1' -> 0x0131, '&' -> 0x0031), run through CursorBorrow: SendInput log for keys('ctrl+1') is down LCtrl, down LShift, down VK_1, up VK_1, up LShift, up LCtrl. 'ctrl+0' and 'alt+1' show the same extra LShift. test/unit/platform-win32-keys.test.ts:121 pins digit shift:true only for typing; no test covers digits with modifiers. On X11 (real Xvfb, layouts fr, be, cz) keys('ctrl+1') sends Shift down and Ctrl+Shift+ampersand (state=5). GTK strips a consumed Shift, but other toolkits may not. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/w1.ts and m3.ts.
fix: In borrow.keys(), do not add the implicit Shift when Ctrl, Alt or Super is among the modifiers and the key is a digit. Windows digit VKs are layout-independent, so Ctrl+VK_1 is Ctrl+1 on every layout. Keep the Shift only when nothing but Shift is held (typing a digit). Equivalent: pass the modifier set to needsShift. Add a Windows test for keys('ctrl+1') on FRENCH. Consider the same rule for X11 digit shortcuts.

title: A left-handed core pointer button map (xmodmap / XSetPointerMapping) turns every Ember click into a right click
scenario: A left-handed user swapped the buttons with xmodmap -e 'pointer = 3 2 1' (or xinput/XSetPointerMapping) in .xinitrc or a startup script. XTestFakeButtonEvent takes the physical button number and the server maps it, so Ember's click(1), the only button the worker ever uses (worker.ts:2128), arrives as button 3. Every tier-3 click opens a context menu instead of activating the control and can leave the menu open. The Windows backend handles SM_SWAPBUTTON (layouts.ts buttonInput, input.ts swapped()), but X11 never reads the pointer map. GNOME's own libinput left-handed toggle swaps at the device level and is probably unaffected.
evidence: Xvfb: with the default map a borrow glide + click gave the app 'ButtonPress b=1, ButtonRelease b=1'. After XSetPointerMapping(map with entries 1 and 3 swapped, 10 buttons) the same code gave 'ButtonPress b=3, ButtonRelease b=3'. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/b1.ts.
fix: In XInput.button(), call XGetPointerMapping and send the physical number whose mapped value is the logical button wanted (invert the map), as the Windows backend does for SM_SWAPBUTTON. Re-read it per press, since it can change while Ember runs. Leave wheel buttons 4-7 alone.

title: macOS: an active input method, or missing Input Monitoring, refuses mouse-only borrows with a message about typing
scenario: A Mac user whose current input source is Japanese, Pinyin or Korean (common all day, toggled with Eisu or Caps Lock) asks Ember to click a button. CursorBorrow.borrowNow calls blockedReason() before every borrow (borrow.ts:334), and it returns INPUT_METHOD_REASON whenever the source is not a plain layout. The click is refused with 'Switch to a keyboard layout (not an input method) so Ember can type, or let Ember fill the field directly.' even though a click never composes text. textKey() already refuses typing under an IME (input.ts:401), so the up-front test only adds false refusals for clicks, scrolls and Cmd shortcuts. The check-up's Mouse and keyboard row also turns to fail while the IME is active. The README says that without Input Monitoring Ember 'won't use the keyboard', but the same preflight refuses the mouse too.
evidence: Code path: borrow.ts:334-335 throws the blockedReason before anything runs; darwin/input.ts:413-421 ends in inputSourceReason(); test/unit/platform-darwin-input.test.ts:447 and borrow-platform.test.ts:97 pin the refusal and use a plain hand.click() as the action. Read from code and unit fakes only; not run on a Mac.
fix: Keep secure input and Accessibility as global refusals. Check the input source only where it matters: in textKey() (already done) and for keys() that type a character with no Command, Control or Option held. Let clicks, scrolls and Cmd shortcuts through. Make the message say what is refused. Align the README row for Input Monitoring with what the code does (it also stops the mouse).

title: Quitting Ember mid-borrow leaves the pointer and focus on the target, not 'pointer home'
scenario: The comment says a running borrow 'lets go (keys up, pointer home) before the connection closes'. The handler calls borrowRef.stop() then xinput.close() in the same tick. close() sets open=false, so the borrow's async finally (move home, restore focus) runs against a closed input and does nothing. Held keys and buttons are released, but the pointer stays wherever the glide was and the target window keeps the keyboard. This only matters when quit comes without the user touching the mouse (logout, SIGTERM); a Quit click already ends the borrow as a takeover.
evidence: Xvfb + mutter, borrow gliding to (800,450) with the user's focus elsewhere, then b.stop(); x.close() as in the handler: the borrow ended with 'Stopped.' and a fresh XInput read pointer {800,450} (home was {1152,720}) and the target window focused. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/q1.ts.
fix: In will-quit, move the pointer home and re-activate the previous window synchronously before closing, or let the borrow finish its finally (await a short settle) before xinput.close(). Otherwise correct the comment.

title: Handle menu "Ask Ember…" never opens the ask box (the menuClosing guard swallows every real pick)
platforms: linux (verified, Electron 44.5 on X11 + mutter); windows and macOS run the same guard
scenario: A new user, or anyone whose Ctrl+Alt+Space is held by another app (the greeting then says "Click my handle in the corner to ask me something", main.ts:443), clicks the pill and chooses "Ask Ember…". The menu closes, nothing opens, and log says ask.menu_ignored {reason: menu-closing}. Keyboard (Down, Enter) and mouse picks both fail. Only the hotkey still works. On Windows and macOS, where the chord is Win+Alt+Space or Control+Shift+Command+Space, the handle is the likely way to ask, so "Ask" from the handle is dead there too, as far as the code shows.
evidence: Ran the real app under mutter. Wrapped Menu.buildFromTemplate to timestamp events: "MENUTRACE will-close 87938" then "MENUTRACE click 'Ask Ember…' 87939", then log {"msg":"ask.menu_ignored","reason":"menu-closing"}. Electron emits menu-will-close ~1 ms BEFORE the picked item's click, so menuClosing (set at main.ts:565) is always true when the click arrives; the code comment at :527 assumes the opposite. "Stop everything", "Settings…", "Stay put" (no guard) fire normally. Pressing Esc on the menu fires no click at all, so the spurious-first-item case the guard targets does not reproduce here. Fix verified: patching the built bundle to `if (false)` made "Ask Ember…" open the box (log ask.open/ask.reveal source=menu), typing worked and Enter returned focus to the user's app; bundle rebuilt afterwards. Unit tests do not cover showMenu.
fix: Remove the menuClosing guard. The other protections stay: the released() gate before popup, registerAccelerator:false, and the post-close ask.spurious_after_menu hide (which skips real picks because opens is already true). If a guard is still wanted, ignore only clicks that arrive within ~150 ms of menu.popup(), never after menu-will-close. Add an xvfb integration check that picks the first item and expects ask.reveal source=menu.

title: "Bring Ember to a computer…" opens Settings behind the user's app, unfocused, and often at the top instead of Computers
platforms: linux verified; the same code paths run on windows and macOS
scenario: With a host added (so the item shows), the user clicks the pill and chooses "Bring Ember to a computer…" with Settings closed (the usual case). (a) Settings is created but the user's app stays focused and drawn on top of it. With a large or maximised app, Settings is hidden and the item looks like it did nothing. (b) In 3 of 5 runs Settings opened at "Your Ember" (scrollY 0, Computers heading 1744 px down) instead of at Computers, as the docs and CHANGELOG promise.
evidence: (a) toMenu() (main.ts:608) passes the targets runtime's click straight through and never sets `opens = true`, so 150 ms after the menu closes the handle-menu callback runs `if (kept && !opens) giveFocusBack(back)` (main.ts:578) and re-activates the user's window while Settings is still loading. Real run with a 190x55 xterm as the user app: X input focus stays on the xterm, Electron says Settings foc=false vis=true, and the screenshot x/b2-big-small.png shows Settings behind the xterm. Picking "Settings…" (opens=true) leaves Settings focused. (b) sendToHome waits for did-finish-load, but home/computers.ts:116 reveals the Computers section only after the async targets list arrives, and home/main.ts:615 `showSection` returns silently when the heading is hidden. Five runs: scrollY 0 / 1713 / 0 / 1713 / 0.
fix: (a) Mark window-opening runtime items: give targetMenu items an `opens` flag for "bring" (and for "Work on" picks that can raise a consent card) and have toMenu set `opens = true` before calling click. (b) In home, remember the requested section while its heading is hidden and apply it from draw() once the Computers section is revealed (or have main send focusSection only after the page reports ready).

title: Late "what Ember will see" update resets the history cursor and throws away the user's draft
scenario: The user opens the box and presses ↑ ↑ to reach an older question, or types half a question and presses ↑ to peek at history. When the quick look finishes (every open sends a second askContext without `opened`), `at` and `draft` are reset. The next ↑ goes to the newest entry instead of the one before, and ↓ no longer returns to the half-typed draft (the draft is lost).
evidence: Ran the built ask page in Chromium with a mock emberAsk. History [first, second, third]: ↑ gives "third", ↑ gives "second", late context {sees, history} arrives, ↑ then shows "third" (expected "first"). Draft case: fill "my half typed draft", ↑ shows "third", late context, ↓ shows "third" (expected the draft). Script: scratchpad release-review/ux-ask/hist-test.cjs.
fix: In onContext, reset history/at/draft only when c.opened is true; on later updates refresh the `sees`, `where` and hint chips and leave the cursor and input alone.

title: Pasted text is silently cut at 2000 characters and multi-line pastes are flattened to one line
scenario: A user pastes a stack trace, a log excerpt or a code snippet and asks "what's wrong with this?". The box is a single-line <input maxlength=2000>: every newline becomes a space (code, YAML and comments lose their structure) and anything past 2000 characters is dropped with no indication, so Ember answers about a partial, flattened question.
evidence: Real Electron ask window: clipboard.writeText(multi-line traceback) + webContents.paste() gives value "Traceback (most recent call last):   File \"app.py\", line 12, … ValueError: bad" on one line. A 2569-character paste gives len 2000. main.ts:1026 also slices to 2000 silently.
fix: Use a textarea that looks like one line and grows up to 3-4 lines (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line). Raise the limit or show "Only the first 2000 characters will be sent" when a paste is cut.

title: Placeholder example "turn on Night Light" works only on Linux/GNOME
scenario: The only example the box shows is "turn on Night Light". On Windows and on macOS (where it is called Night Shift) a first-time user who tries the suggestion gets no quick settings change; Ember has to drive Settings window by window or says it can't.
evidence: hands/system.ts:24 and platform/linux use gsettings for night_light. platform/darwin/system/settings.ts:15 offers only dark_style ("Dark Mode") and win32/system/settings.ts:27 offers only dark_style; darwin change() throws "Ember can't change night light on a Mac." The placeholder is static HTML and is the same on every OS.
fix: Use an example that works everywhere, e.g. “turn on dark mode”, or have main pass an OS-specific example in the context message.

title: "Ember will see: App · Title" understates what the request carries
scenario: The box tells the user what Ember will see so nothing is sent by surprise, but the chip shows only app and window title. The same context also sends the focused control's selected text (up to 300 chars, including the X PRIMARY selection on Linux) or the first 120 characters of its text, and the app and title of every other open window ("Open windows:" list). A user in a mail compose window, or with a bank tab open elsewhere, sees only "Thunderbird · Write: Re: Q3".
evidence: quickContextText (perception/index.ts:745-765) builds the Focused/Selected text/Its text begins lines plus the Open windows list; Perception.withSelection (:353-362) appends the selection; askEmber passes context.text to agent.ask. The chip builds only [app, title] (main.ts:782). The type comment in shared/ipc.ts:185 promises "Mousepad · notes.txt · 12 words selected", which was never implemented.
fix: Extend the chip (or add a hover/second line) with what is sent: "+ selection", "+ field text", "+ N other window titles". Alternatively stop sending the open-window list and field text unless the question needs them.

title: Mic badge: 8 px colour-only dot, hidden from assistive tech, error state unexplained
scenario: The only sign that "Hey Ember" is listening, muted or broken is an 8 px dot on the face: orange (waiting), orange with halo (hearing you), grey (muted), red (error). A colour-blind user cannot tell orange from red reliably, and a screen-reader user gets nothing (the dot is aria-hidden). On a denied microphone permission or a lost device the pill reads "Ready" beside a red dot; the only words are a hover tooltip, "Microphone problem", with no way forward (the menu does not mention it). The states needs-models, downloading and starting show no dot, so "Hey Ember" silently does nothing.
evidence: handle/index.html:14 `<i id="mic" class="mic" hidden aria-hidden="true">`; styles.css:99 `.mic{width:8px;height:8px}`; the state is colour only (muted is grey, error red). Real run with mic:"error": pill says "Ready" with a red dot; hovering shows the tooltip "Microphone problem" (x/tip.png). voice.ts keeps the detail only for the settings window. micShown (main.ts:116) excludes starting, downloading and needs-models.
fix: Give each state a shape as well as a colour (slashed mic for muted, "!" for error) and a role="img" aria-label. On error, put "Microphone problem" (or the reason) on the pill's idle line and add a menu item "Microphone problem: open Settings…". Show a dot, or "Voice isn't set up", while models are missing.

title: Ask-box chips: title truncated by the "Ember will see:" prefix, no tooltip, pop-in reflow, target chip ignores connection state
scenario: The line under the field is one 560 px pill. With the three key hints on the right, the "Ember will see: Visual Studio Code · ext…" chip keeps room for the app name only, so which document or terminal is cut. With an SSH or WSL target it is worse ("On build-01 Ember will see: Terminal ·…"). The chip arrives after the quick look, so the pill jumps from ~190 px to full width a moment after opening. "On deploy@build-server-…" is cut at 160 px with no tooltip and looks the same whether the host is ready or lost.
evidence: Rendered the built page at 2x (scratchpad release-review/ux-ask/am-sheet.png, ask-where.png, am-3-lost-ssh.png). `.meta{width:fit-content}` with `.where{max-width:160px}`; neither chip sets title=; targetChip() (handle/badge.ts:27) ignores t.state while the handle's own badge shows it.
fix: Drop the "Ember will see:" prefix when a where chip is present (or use an eye icon). Set title= to the full text. Reserve the row's height/width so late context doesn't reflow. Add the state to the chip ("On build-01 (lost)"). Say "Ember won't look at this window" for private windows.

title: The handle can't be moved or hidden, and "Hide Ember" leaves it on screen
scenario: A 200x56 always-on-top pill sits 12 px from the bottom-right corner of the primary display, over status bars, zoom sliders and scroll corners of maximised apps. The window is movable:false with no setting, and "Hide Ember" hides only the cursor-following character: the menu flips to "Show Ember" but the pill and its face stay.
evidence: handle.ts:22,45,116-120: fixed PILL, movable:false, corner() always primary-work-area bottom-right. Real run: click "Hide Ember", pill and face still drawn (x/hide-sheet.png) and the menu reads "Show Ember". No docs mention moving or hiding the pill.
fix: Let the user drag the pill (remember the corner) or choose a corner in Settings; make "Hide Ember" fade the pill to a small tab, or rename the item "Hide the character".

title: Handle-menu copy has two sources of truth; the tested one is dead code and docs disagree with the live menu
scenario: menu-copy.ts (pinned by test/unit/ui-copy.test.ts:548) says "Bring Ember to a computer…" shows whenever SSH is allowed and offers "Disconnect" while connecting. The live menu (app/main/targets/menu.ts:47,50) shows it only once a host exists or there are two targets, and offers Disconnect only when the target is ready. COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:338 and CHANGELOG.md:66 describe the menu item without that condition. A first-time user with SSH allowed and no host sees no such item, and nobody can cancel a connecting host from the menu. docs/DESIGN.md:12 also says characters are chosen "in the handle menu, or by voice"; neither exists.
evidence: grep: menu-copy is imported only by test/unit/ui-copy.test.ts, and the built dist/app/main.cjs contains no radioLabel/menu-copy. Real menus: with no host there is no Bring item (x/m1-crop.png); with a host there is (x/m1-host-crop.png). Both test files pass, pinning different behaviour.
fix: Delete menu-copy.ts and point its tests at targets/menu.ts, or make the runtime use it. Decide whether Bring is always offered, and make the docs and CHANGELOG say what ships. Offer Disconnect while connecting. Fix the DESIGN.md sentence.

title: No Cut/Copy/Paste context menu in the ask box; key hints use PC wording on macOS
scenario: Right-clicking in the field does nothing (there is no context-menu handler anywhere in the renderers), so a mouse-only paste or copy of a previous question is impossible. On macOS the hint reads "Enter to send" where the key is Return, and the handle menu spells the chord out as "Control+Shift+Command+Space" instead of ⌃⇧⌘Space.
evidence: grep for context-menu in app/: only a desk image preventDefault. ask/index.html hard-codes <kbd>Enter</kbd>. shortcuts.ts:46 darwin label is the spelled-out chord.
fix: Add a small native context menu for the ask input (Cut, Copy, Paste, Select all). Use "Return" and glyph chords on macOS.

title: Windows and macOS have no typed-ahead hold: letters typed while the box is opening or the chord keys are still down may be lost or misrouted
platforms: windows, macos (not verifiable on this Linux container)
scenario: On Linux, Ember grabs the keyboard while the box opens and replays the first letters into it (verified: "fast typing test" typed immediately after the chord arrives intact). On Windows and macOS keyboardHold is null, and the chords are three or four keys long, so a fast typist starting before the modifiers are released may lose the first letters or fire another Win+Alt+letter / ⌃⇧⌘+letter shortcut instead.
evidence: platform/win32/platform.ts:69 and platform/darwin/platform.ts:56 set `keyboardHold: null`; main.ts:771 `held = look && platform.keyboardHold ? … : null`. Not documented anywhere. The consequence on Windows/macOS is inferred, not observed.
fix: Check on a real Windows 11 and a Mac. If letters are lost, add a native equivalent (a low-level keyboard hook, or an NSEvent monitor) or document "release the keys before typing".

title: A failed audit write (disk full, quota, read-only or root-owned audit file) leaves the task queue half-updated: a task the user was told failed runs later, and finished tasks stay on screen as "Working…" forever
area: main process robustness / low disk (agent TaskManager + AuditLog)
scenario: The disk fills up (or the audit file/folder is unwritable, e.g. root-owned after a past sudo run). (a) The user asks for a task: TaskManager.start() queues it, then audit.write('asked') throws before pump()/publish() (tasks.ts:122-124). The conductor tool call fails, so the user is told it failed, but the task sits in the queue with no card. When space is freed and the user asks for something else, pump() starts the old task too and Ember acts in the user's apps on a request it said had failed. (b) A task is already running when writes start failing: finish() (tasks.ts:277) throws before publish()/onFinished()/the removal timer, so run() rejects before worker.dispose() and pump() (tasks.ts:258,267). The card shows "Working…" for ever, nothing is spoken or notified, and any queued task never starts. Only a restart recovers.
evidence: Real app under xvfb, driven with Playwright and the offline mock model (scripts h/pw-audit-mid.mjs, h/pw-audit-phantom.mjs, h/pw-audit-full.mjs in the scratch folder). Healthy control: task done in 233 ms. (a) Audit file replaced by a directory before asking: bubble says 'Failed to execute start_task … Tool execution failed', task manager = ['Job A:queued'], 0 cards. After removing the obstacle and asking only for task B: manager = ['Job A:done','Job B:done']. (b) Audit made unwritable while 'Job number 1' and '2' run (3 queued): ember.log shows two 'unhandled rejection … EISDIR … audit-2026-10.jsonl'. For the next 14 s the overlay cards stay ['Job number 1:running','Job number 2:running'] while the manager says done/done and 'Job number 3:queued' never starts. No unit test covers an audit write that throws.
fix: Never let an audit failure break bookkeeping. Make AuditLog.write catch and log.warn once (keep a bounded in-memory buffer if wanted), or at least wrap the two TaskManager writes in try/catch. In start(), pump()/publish() must not depend on the audit line. In run(), use try/finally so worker.dispose() and pump() always run, and finish() must publish before it audits. If the action path should stay fail-closed, keep that in worker.audit() only and cancel the task with a plain message.

title: Ember exits silently (exit code 0, no window, no message) when its data folder can't be locked or written; it is treated as 'another Ember is already running'
area: startup in odd environments / single instance
platforms: all (reproduced on linux); any OS where userData is unwritable
scenario: ~/.config/ember (or %LOCALAPPDATA%\ember) is not writable: owned by root after an earlier `sudo ember` that kept HOME, a read-only or immutable home, NFS root-squash, no free inodes. Chromium cannot create SingletonLock, so app.requestSingleInstanceLock() returns false and main.ts:128-131 logs 'instance.handover' and calls app.quit(). The log folder can't be created either (logger.ts:63 falls back to stderr), so a launcher or autostart start leaves nothing at all. The user clicks Ember and nothing happens; support has no log to read.
evidence: Ran Electron as uid 65534 (setpriv) with EMBER_USER_DATA on a read-only directory: stderr 'Failed to create …/SingletonLock: Permission denied (13)', then {"msg":"instance.handover"}; the process ends with exit=0 and never opens a window. Same result when the data path is a file ('readlink … Not a directory'). The `try { mkdirSync…chmodSync } catch { /* reported when used */ }` at main.ts:101 never reports it.
fix: In the `!requestSingleInstanceLock()` branch, first check that userData is writable (fs.accessSync(userData, W_OK) or create and remove a probe file). If it isn't, call startupFailed(new Error("Ember can't write to <dir>. Fix its owner or permissions…")) so the user gets a dialog and exit code 1. Only then treat the false result as a handover to another instance.

title: While the local screen is locked, Ember keeps listening for "Hey Ember" and keeps reading and speaking about the user's apps; only the borrowed mouse checks for a lock, and the Linux check can't see GNOME's lock shield
scenario: The user locks the workstation (Super+L, idle lock) with Ember running and 'Hey Ember' on. The wake word is not speaker-specific, so anyone in the room says 'Hey Ember, what's in my open email?'. onVoice('utterance') goes straight to askEmber() with no lock check, accessibility keeps working for apps behind the shield, and the answer is spoken aloud (if speaking is on). Read-only tools need no confirmation, and apps granted 'Always' can be acted on. The docs say tasks stop when a REMOTE computer's screen locks (COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:418); the local PC has no such rule.
evidence: Code path read end to end: voice.setWanted() depends only on settings (main.ts:1603); case 'utterance' (main.ts:891-903) calls askEmber(); no code under app/main/agent, perception or voice consults a lock state. XInput.screenLocked is used only by hands/borrow.ts:349. Its Linux implementation (hands/input.ts:477-488) looks only at XScreenSaver state ScreenSaverOn and DPMS-not-On, which GNOME Shell's lock shield does not set before the display blanks (stated from knowledge of GNOME; not reproduced, since there is no GNOME lock screen under Xvfb). macOS has CGSSessionScreenIsLocked, but only borrow uses it. Electron's powerMonitor 'lock-screen'/'unlock-screen' events (Windows, macOS) are not used; only 'resume' and 'shutdown' are.
fix: Treat a locked or inactive local session like the remote case: stop listening (voice.teardown / mute) and refuse asks, speech and tasks while locked, and say so on return. Detect it with powerMonitor lock-screen/unlock-screen on Windows and macOS, and on Linux with logind LockedHint/Active (loginctl or org.gnome.ScreenSaver.GetActive over D-Bus), not only the X screensaver.

title: A settings.json saved with a UTF-8 BOM or as UTF-16 (PowerShell 5.1, older editors, deployment scripts) resets every setting, including consent and onboarding
scenario: An admin or user pre-seeds or edits settings.json with `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` or `Out-File` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM or UTF-16LE). readFileSync(file,'utf8') keeps the BOM, JSON.parse and lenientJson both fail, and read() falls into the 'cannot be read at all' branch: only the never-look list is salvaged. Character, size, grants, models and consent (so the user must onboard again) go back to defaults. Ember then rewrites the file and keeps the original as settings.json.bad-<time>.
evidence: Harness h/settings-harness.ts over SettingsStore.load(): the same content loads fully when plain (character=wisp size=80 grants={gedit:act}); with a leading U+FEFF, or UTF-16LE with a BOM, the result is character=cinder size=60 grants={} with recoveredFrom=settings.json.bad-… and the notice 'Some of settings.json couldn't be used, so those settings went back to their defaults'. admin.ts:121 parseAdminPolicy has the same JSON.parse(raw) and would lock Ember down on a BOM.
fix: Read the file as a Buffer: strip EF BB BF, decode UTF-16 LE/BE when the BOM says so, then parse. Do the same in parseAdminPolicy and in main.ts settingsText() (the doctor's WSL switch).

title: A transient read error at start-up (antivirus or sync lock, NFS hiccup) makes Ember start on defaults without a notice, and the first change overwrites the user's real settings with no backup
scenario: settings.json exists but readFileSync fails once with EBUSY, EPERM, EACCES or EIO while Ember starts (login-time scans). read(false) takes `this.current = DEFAULT_SETTINGS; return` (lines 306-313) for any error, not only ENOENT. Ember shows first-run onboarding again with no problem notice and no backup. The first save (a slider, any toggle) replaces the user's file with defaults plus that one change. Consent, SSH hosts, command consents and the never-look list are lost. The running case (running=true) already keeps the settings in use and raises a notice.
evidence: Harness h/settings-harness.ts with fs.readFileSync made to throw EBUSY on its first call: load() returns character=cinder onboarded=false, lastProblem=null. After store.update({size:70}) the file contains defaults with size 70, and the folder holds only settings.json (no .bad-* copy).
fix: At start-up retry a few times (50-200 ms) for EBUSY/EPERM/EACCES/EIO/ETIMEDOUT. If it still fails, run on defaults but call problem() and refuse to overwrite: copy the file to .bad-<ts> first, or keep saves in memory until it reads again, as the running case does.

title: The settings window swallows failed saves: with a full or unwritable disk the first-run 'Start Ember' button, toggles and the size slider do nothing and show no error
area: settings UX on failure / low disk
scenario: SettingsStore.save() throws (ENOSPC, EDQUOT, EROFS, EACCES, a locked file after retries) and the IPC handler (main.ts:385-391) rejects. Every caller in the renderer does `void window.ember.updateSettings(...)` (lines 68, 137, 143, 148, 153, 495, 709, 720, 755, 816, 820, 826). On first run the user ticks 'I agree' and presses 'Start Ember', and nothing happens and nothing explains why. Toggles keep their new look although nothing was saved or applied.
evidence: Playwright against the real app with settings.json replaced by a directory (all saves fail with EISDIR): after clicking 'I agree' + 'Start Ember' the page's only trace is a console pageerror "Error invoking remote method 'ember:update-settings': Error: EISDIR … rename … settings.json"; document.body.className is still 'first-run', #start-row is not hidden, and the screenshot (savefail-2.png in the scratch folder) shows an unchanged page with no message.
fix: Route all saves through one helper that catches the rejection, shows a visible message ('Ember couldn't save your settings: <reason>') and restores the control's previous state. Let the main process also push the failure through IPC.settingsNotice. Do not leave the first-run Start button silent.

title: Ember deletes the user's own ~/.config/autostart/ember.desktop at every launch while 'Start Ember when I log in' is off, and any other Ember with a different data folder rewrites it
platforms: linux (windows and macOS login items follow the same sync-to-setting pattern)
scenario: A user or admin enables autostart the usual Linux way (copying /usr/share/applications/ember.desktop into ~/.config/autostart, or GNOME Tweaks / Startup Applications, which write ember.desktop). Ember's own setting startAtLogin defaults to false, and main.ts:1084 calls sys.autostart.sync(false) at every start, so syncAutostart() sees a file that differs from `null` and rmSync()s it. Ember stops starting at login after the first run. A dev build, an AppImage, or any Ember started with another EMBER_USER_DATA shares the same autostart file and overwrites or deletes it too.
evidence: Harness h/auto.ts: with a hand-made ember.desktop in place, syncAutostart(false, cmd, file) returns true and the file no longer exists. The settings window will then show the switch off.
fix: Only remove or replace an entry Ember wrote (check for a marker such as X-Ember-Managed=true), or only touch the file when the setting actually changed during this run (on toggle, not on every start). Leave foreign entries alone and show their presence in the settings note.

title: Audit retention is by whole months and enforced only at start-up, so entries outlive the administrator's auditRetentionDays by up to a month or more
scenario: An organisation sets auditRetentionDays to 7 (or leaves the default 30) for privacy reasons. prune() only deletes a monthly file once the end of its month is older than the cutoff, and main.ts:1349 calls it once, at start. An entry from the 1st of a month stays about 38 days with retention 7, and about 61 days with the default 30. An Ember that runs for weeks (autostart, never quits) keeps older months until the next restart.
evidence: Harness h/prune.ts with retention 7 days and an entry written on 1 Sep: still on disk on 15 Sep, 30 Sep and 2 Oct (31 days old), deleted only on 20 Oct (49 days).
fix: Rewrite or trim files by line timestamp (or write per-day files), run prune daily (setInterval with unref) as well as at start, and apply the cutoff to the entry's own timestamp.

title: The consent text says what you ask is kept only while Ember runs, but the audit log stores the task goal and result summary for 30+ days
scenario: The first-run card says: 'a record of every action it took (kept 30 days) … What you ask and what Ember answers is kept only while it runs.' TaskManager writes goal (first 300 characters of the request) and summary (first 300 characters of the result) plus the window title to ~/.config/ember/audit/*.jsonl (tasks.ts:122 and :277). They stay on disk after Ember quits, longer than the label says (see the retention finding).
evidence: audit-2026-10.jsonl from the real-app run contains {"event":"task","phase":"asked","goal":"Do the thing"} and {"phase":"done","summary":"All done."}. The journal copy already reduces these to sizes (audit.ts journalLine), so the authors treat them as sensitive.
fix: Reword the card ('…a record of every action, including the task's goal and result, kept N days'), or store sizes only and keep goal and summary in memory like the conversation.

title: If the system clock steps back (VM time sync after resume, NTP step), the character flies about 230,000 px off screen and takes ~0.6 s to return
scenario: The overlay tick computes dt = (Date.now() - last)/1000. Follower.step clamps only the top (Math.min(dt, 0.05), follow.ts:85,87), so a negative dt passes through into the spring integration. After a resume or snapshot restore on a VM or VDI, or an NTP step back of seconds, Ember vanishes and flies back in.
evidence: Harness h/follow.ts with the real Follower: after a cursor flick, one step with dt=-3 puts Ember at x=233157,y=186465 on a 1280x800 screen; it takes 39 frames (~624 ms) to settle, 24 of them more than 5000 px away.
fix: Clamp dt to [0, 0.05] in Follower.step, and use a monotonic clock (performance.now()) for the tick.

title: A successful GitHub sign-in is reported as failed, and the token is lost, if saving the token throws (disk full, read-only data folder)
scenario: The user approves the device code on GitHub. tokens.save(token) (main.ts:993) runs inside the try block and TokenStore.save() does an unguarded fs.writeFileSync (auth.ts:55-57), so ENOSPC, EDQUOT or EACCES makes the whole flow report an error and never calls agent.start(token). The no-keyring case is handled gracefully ('sign-in lasts until Ember quits'); a failed write is not. The same non-atomic writeFileSync can leave a truncated github-token.bin on a crash.
evidence: Code read: main.ts:993-999 and auth.ts save(). Not reproduced end to end (it needs the real device flow).
fix: Wrap save() in try/catch and treat a failed write like 'no keyring': keep the token in memory, connect, and say the sign-in won't survive a restart. Write the token with tmp + rename.

title: EMBER_LOG_LEVEL with an unrecognised value (uppercase, 'warning', 'trace') turns on debug logging instead of being ignored
scenario: main.ts:105 casts process.env.EMBER_LOG_LEVEL to LogLevel without checking. For an unknown name ORDER[level] is undefined, `ORDER[lvl] < undefined` is false, and every line, debug included (sidecar and voice stderr, overlay detail), is written. Packaged builds honour the variable, so someone setting EMBER_LOG_LEVEL=WARN to quieten the log gets the noisiest one.
evidence: Harness h/log.ts: level 'info' writes 2 of 3 test lines; 'INFO', 'warning', 'verbose' and 'trace' all write 3 of 3, including the debug line. (Rotation itself is fine: ember.log + .1-.3, about 20 MB at most.)
fix: Lower-case the value and fall back to 'info' (with a warn line) when it is not one of debug, info, warn, error.

title: No logging of GPU/utility process crashes, and no recovery or logging for crashes of the command, prompt, desk-view and ask windows' renderers
scenario: Only the home, overlay, handle, ask and mic windows handle render-process-gone. Nothing listens to app 'child-process-gone', and the command window, prompt window (SSH password and consent cards, always on top) and desk view have no handler. A GPU-process crash loop, the usual cause of blank or black windows on VMs and RDP, leaves nothing in ember.log. A crashed prompt window stays on screen blank until the card times out.
evidence: grep of app/ for child-process-gone, render-process-gone and revive( finds only revive.ts, voice.ts:260, ask.ts:120, overlay.ts:314, handle.ts:75 and main.ts:300. commands/window.ts and remote/prompt-window.ts handle only 'closed'. (Not exercised by forcing a crash.)
fix: Add app.on('child-process-gone') and a web-contents-created hook that logs render-process-gone with the reason for every window, and apply revive() (or close-and-answer-no) to the command and prompt windows.

title: Hand edits of settings.json leave an unbounded pile of settings.json.bad-<time> files, and a valid-JSON-but-out-of-range value is rewritten under the editor while the user is still typing
scenario: With an editor that autosaves (VS Code, JetBrains), each intermediate invalid state while the user types creates a new .bad-<Date.now()> copy (keep() runs once per mtime and nothing prunes them). If the intermediate text parses but a value is out of range (size 800 on the way to 80), read(true) repairs and saves over the file immediately (lines 345-347), so the editor reports the file changed on disk.
evidence: Harness h/edit.ts simulating four autosaves: three .bad-* backups, and the file rewritten by Ember at the 'size: 800' state.
fix: Keep at most the last few backups (delete older .bad-* when making a new one). In running mode, for a repairable file wait for the file to be unchanged for a couple of seconds before rewriting it.

title: "Sign in with GitHub" cannot sign anyone in on a release build; the real path needs the GitHub CLI, which nothing tells the user to install
scenario: A non-technical user installs Ember on Windows or macOS (no gh, no terminal habit), agrees, presses Start and gets "Not connected to Copilot: sign in with GitHub below." Pressing the button gives "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”. Ember will notice…" with a Cancel button. The device flow is dead code because process.env.EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is read at runtime and nothing sets it (no build-time define; PLAN.md §7 Q1 'Open'). Nothing says gh must be installed, and ghCliToken() returns null both for 'gh missing' and 'not logged in', so Check again says only "No GitHub sign-in found… Run gh auth login". The README has no sign-in step and never says a GitHub account with Copilot is needed (grep for sign in/subscription/account/gh auth in README.md finds nothing relevant). The doctor's fix, "choose Sign in with GitHub, or run gh auth login", has the same gap. Only docs/DEVELOPING.md §'Connecting Copilot' explains it. Result: on a clean machine, first run ends at a dead end.
evidence: app/main/main.ts:964-981 (clientId check, 'waiting' message); app/main/agent/auth.ts:7; app/renderer/home/copy.ts:55; app/main/doctor.ts (copilot row fix); grep -rn EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID scripts packaging app finds only these reads; grep README.md finds no 'gh auth', 'GitHub CLI' or Copilot-subscription text; no user-facing 'install the GitHub CLI' string anywhere under app/. Rendered the macOS after-Start window: after the click only the Cancel button and the terminal instruction show.
fix: Preferred: register Ember's GitHub App and bake the client id into the build, so the device flow runs. If it must ship without that: (1) README 'Before you start' step: a GitHub account with Copilot, plus the GitHub CLI with per-OS commands (winget install GitHub.cli / brew install gh / sudo dnf install gh) and `gh auth login`. (2) Detect a missing gh (which/ghCliPath) and say "GitHub CLI isn't installed" with the install command or link in the Copilot section. (3) Relabel the button "Connect with GitHub CLI" so it doesn't promise a browser sign-in. (4) Make the doctor row say the same.

title: On a Mac, fixing the only 'Fix' row hides the Setup check, with Screen Recording and Input Monitoring still unfixed, from the first-run window
scenario: First launch on a Mac: Accessibility is a 'fail' (Fix), Screen Recording and Input Monitoring are 'warn' (Check). The consent text promises "macOS will ask you to allow Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring". Before Start, the Setup check is visible only because failing > 0. The user presses Open System Settings, allows Accessibility and returns; the window re-reads the status on focus, failing becomes 0, and `classList.toggle('after-setup', !failing)` hides the whole Setup section again (body.first-run hides .after-setup). The remaining Screen Recording and Input Monitoring buttons disappear, the tagline reverts to the generic 'Read how Ember works…', and the user can't finish granting before Start.
evidence: Rendered with real inspectEnvironment() data for macOS in Chromium: initial first-run screenshot shows 'Setup check – 1 to fix' with three 'Open System Settings' buttons; after setting the accessibility check to ok and dispatching 'focus', the page text contains only the welcome card, picker and Start (no Setup check). Code: app/renderer/home/main.ts:214-217; app/main/environment.ts:267-285 (only accessibility is 'fail').
fix: Keep the Setup section visible in first-run whenever any check is not ok (fail or warn) on macOS, or add a dedicated 'Allow Ember' step above Start listing Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring with their buttons. Tie the tagline to 'N permissions still to allow'.

title: Start ignores the setup check: the window closes and Ember greets as if ready even when Accessibility, the helper or the session is unusable
scenario: A Mac user with a gh sign-in (or any user whose Copilot connects) presses Start with Accessibility not allowed. settings.onChange -> settledPhase() -> phase 'ready' -> home.close() -> greet(): "I'll stay by your cursor. Press ⌃⇧⌘Space to ask me anything." The only permission surface (the Setup check, a collapsed fold near the bottom) closed with the window. The same happens on Linux with 'Screen reading: Accessibility is off' (RHEL 8's default, a warn), on Windows with 'Windows blocked Ember's accessibility helper' (warn, 'Unblock it') and on a Wayland session (fail). The README says 'its setup check says which are missing', but nothing brings the user there. macOS never prompts by itself either: Ember calls isTrustedAccessibilityClient(true), the one-pixel screen grab and CGRequestListenEventAccess only from the fix buttons. When the status says 'warn' the section is a closed fold labelled '1 to look at', the 'Setup' nav link has no badge, and the tagline says 'Press Win+Alt+Space to ask it anything.' (rendered). The handle says 'Ready' (idleWord looks only at Copilot).
evidence: app/main/main.ts:1104-1121 (decision uses only phase); greet() at 436-456 ignores env checks; app/main/main.ts handle idle word from agent status only; rendered after-start-win-ready.png with a 'blocked-download' warn and Copilot ready: no hint of the warning above the fold; grep for accessibilityTrusted(prompt)/requestListenAccess shows no automatic call.
fix: At first Start, if any check is fail or a capability-critical warn (macOS Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring; Linux Screen reading; Windows helper blocked), keep Settings open scrolled to Setup (as is already done for Copilot) and let greet() say what is missing. Add a count badge on the 'Setup' nav link, make the tagline mention open warns, and offer an 'Open settings' bubble action when a task can't read or capture.

title: Missing or revoked Screen Recording on macOS is reported to the user and model as 'the window is off screen'
scenario: Screen Recording not allowed (first run, never granted) or revoked later (also macOS 15's monthly re-approval declined). capture.ts returns null at once without asking macOS, so perceive() ends at `noShot("the window is off screen, or the screen couldn't be captured safely")`. The worker hears '(No screenshot: the window is off screen, or the screen couldn't be captured safely.)' and tells the user that, or retries; nobody mentions Screen Recording, there is no 'Open settings' action, and the handle still says 'Ready'. Because Ember never touches desktopCapturer without the permission, macOS never prompts either: the user only learns by finding the Setup check. The Accessibility and Input Monitoring refusals, by contrast, name the System Settings pane (ax-darwin-read.ts:54, darwin/input.ts:30,51).
evidence: app/main/platform/darwin/capture.ts:50-56 (null without permission, no reason); app/main/perception/index.ts:405-409, 507; PlatformWords (app/shared/words.ts) has no 'no screenshot because of permission' field; windows.screenRecording() exists but perceive() doesn't ask it.
fix: Add a platform word (e.g. screenshotsBlocked: "Ember doesn't have the Screen Recording permission (System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen Recording)") and have perceive() use it when the window system reports no screen access. Raise a bubble/notice with an 'Open settings' action the first time per run.

title: README leaves Windows users blocked by Smart App Control with no way forward
scenario: A user on a recent Windows 11 install (Smart App Control On) extracts the zip and starts Ember.exe. The README says SAC 'blocks unsigned apps outright and can't make an exception for one app' and stops. It doesn't say what the user will see, that SAC is under Windows Security › App & browser control › Smart App Control settings, that turning it off may be one-way on their build, or that they can use another computer or wait for a signed build. A home user cannot complete the install; an enterprise user is not told to ask IT.
evidence: README.md:34-41; grep -rn 'Smart App Control' app finds only vocabulary.ts (no detection, no doctor row, no in-app wording); docs/DEVELOPING.md:588 only repeats that the README covers it.
fix: Add the symptom (a 'Smart App Control blocked…' message with no Run anyway), the exact path to turn it off, the warning that turning it back on may need a Windows reset on some builds, and 'on a managed PC ask your administrator'. Better: sign the Windows build before release.

title: After the Linux 'Turn on' button the 'restart open apps' caveat disappears, and the README never mentions the switch
scenario: On stock RHEL 8 (toolkit-accessibility false) the Setup check says 'Accessibility is off, so Ember can only see screenshots. Turn it on, then restart open apps.' with a Turn on button. After the click the row re-reads as OK: 'Accessibility is on', and the instruction is gone. The user asks Ember to act in a window opened earlier; Qt, Chromium and Firefox windows opened before the switch are not readable until restarted or the user logs out and in (docs/DEVELOPING.md:65, doctor.ts:138 'then log out and in'). Ember says it is ready. The README Linux section never mentions the switch.
evidence: app/main/environment.ts:174-178; app/renderer/home/main.ts:195-200 (fix result just re-renders checks); app/main/doctor.ts:138 vs environment.ts:176 give different instructions ('log out and in' vs 'restart open apps').
fix: After the fix, keep a note on the row ('On. Restart apps that were already open, or log out and in, so Ember can read them.') until the user dismisses it or the sidecar sees an app. Make the doctor and the setup check say the same thing, and add a line to the README's Linux install section.

title: macOS 'Reset Ember's permissions' recovery is implemented but never offered; stale-grant recovery is a manual '−' and '+' instruction repeated on first run
scenario: Every update replaces the ad-hoc signature, so macOS shows Ember switched on while the permission no longer applies (README says so). The only recovery shown is the sentence 'If Ember is already listed and switched on, remove it with − and add it again…', appended to the Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring and Microphone rows (and to every doctor row), including for a brand-new install where Ember is not listed yet. The designed one-click fix 'reset-permissions' (tccutil reset Accessibility/ScreenCapture/ListenEvent) exists in darwin/system/environment.ts but no check ever sets fix: 'reset-permissions' (nor 'open-automation-settings'), so it is dead code.
evidence: grep -rn reset-permissions app: only the FixId type and darwin/system/environment.ts (RESET_SERVICES, label, apply); inspectMac() in app/main/environment.ts:267-285 never references it; rendered macOS Setup check shows the long sentence three times.
fix: Offer 'Reset Ember's permissions' as a button on the Accessibility row when it fails after Ember was previously granted (or always as a secondary button). Show the '−/+' sentence only after the first Open System Settings press, or as one note under the list.

title: Windows microphone: no setup-check row or button although the code says there is one; the doctor path names Windows 11 only
scenario: A Windows user whose 'Let desktop apps access your microphone' is off (common on managed PCs) turns on 'Hey Ember'. The Voice line says 'Not working: Ember wasn't allowed to use the microphone. To allow it, open the microphone's privacy settings in Settings.' with no button there. main.ts:1583 says 'the setup check has a button for it', and WIN32_FIX_IDS includes open-microphone-settings, but inspectWindows() never emits a microphone check, so the button appears nowhere (the row exists only in the CLI doctor). If Chromium reports that block as NotReadable, micHelp() says 'in use by another app'. The doctor and README give 'Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone', which is the Windows 11 wording; Windows 10 22H2 (supported) says 'Privacy › Microphone'.
evidence: app/main/environment.ts:224-255 (no microphone check for win32); app/main/platform/win32/system/environment.ts:43 (fix id with no producer); app/main/main.ts:1583-1585; app/main/platform/win32/system/doctor.ts:77-79; README.md:44.
fix: Add a Windows 'Microphone' check (warn with fix 'open-microphone-settings') when getMediaAccessStatus is denied/restricted, and a button next to the Voice error. Word the path for both Windows versions ('Settings › Privacy (Privacy & security on Windows 11) › Microphone').

title: 'Speak replies out loud' does nothing, with no message, when the system has no speech voice
scenario: A RHEL 8 user (AppImage, or an install without the weak dependency speech-dispatcher-espeak-ng) turns on 'Speak replies, questions and results out loud'. Chromium's speechSynthesis finds no voice, onstart never fires, and nothing is heard. The settings window shows no error, because the 'Speaking' row exists only in the CLI doctor ('speech-dispatcher is missing…'), not in the Setup check. The user concludes speech is broken.
evidence: app/renderer/mic/main.ts:61-72 (no onerror reporting, no voice check); app/main/doctor.ts speech row; app/main/environment.ts has no speech check; Voice.speak() at app/main/voice.ts only waits SPEECH_START_MS and gives up silently.
fix: When speak() gets no onstart within the timeout (or getVoices() is empty), report it to main and show it under the 'Speak replies' switch and as a Setup check row with the OS fix (Linux: sudo dnf install speech-dispatcher speech-dispatcher-espeak-ng).

title: README has no download location and the AppImage line omits the system packages it needs
scenario: 'Get Ember-0.1.0-win-x64.zip' (and the mac dmg) points at 'npm run package:win' or a manual CI run whose artifact is kept for 3 days (ci.yml retention-days: 3); there is no release workflow and no link, so a non-developer cannot find the installer. The Linux line 'Or run Ember-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage without installing' omits that the AppImage needs the system packages the RPM pulls in (python3-pyatspi, python3-gobject, at-spi2-core…); without them the Setup check says only 'Python accessibility bindings are missing: sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi' (it omits python3-gobject, which the doctor lists) and Ember can't read apps.
evidence: README.md:25, 29-30, 59-61; .github/workflows/ci.yml retention-days: 3 (no release job); packaging/rpm/ember.spec Requires list; app/main/environment.ts:174 vs app/main/doctor.ts:137.
fix: Link the GitHub Releases page once the files are published (and list the checksums). For the AppImage, name the packages (`sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi python3-gobject at-spi2-core`) and make the Setup check's message match the doctor's.

title: README's Gatekeeper steps stop at 'macOS 15'
scenario: The README lists 'macOS 15:' (Open Anyway) and 'macOS 13 and 14:' (Control-click). Ember reads macOS 26 correctly (permissions.ts maps Darwin 25 to 26) and the README says '13 or later', but on macOS 26 a user doesn't know which line applies (the Open Anyway flow is the same as 15's).
evidence: README.md:65-68; app/main/platform/darwin/system/permissions.ts:macVersionFromDarwin.
fix: Say 'macOS 15 and later' (and re-check the wording on macOS 26).

title: First-run window: Start and the agree box are below the fold, and the copy points to sections that aren't shown yet and to features of other OSes
scenario: At the default 760×640 window the first screen shows only the hero and the terms (rendered). The character picker, 'I've read how Ember works and I agree' and 'Start Ember' need a scroll that nothing hints at. The terms say 'turn on “Hey Ember” below' (the Voice section is hidden until Start), 'your never-look list' (the list is hidden too), and on macOS and Linux 'Ember can work in WSL', which is Windows-only (the WSL switch is hidden elsewhere). 'Accessibility service' is the only explanation of what Ember reads.
evidence: Rendered first-run-win-640.png (Start below the fold); app/renderer/home/index.html:31-36; app/renderer/home/copy.ts homePatches doesn't patch these bullets per OS.
fix: Put Start and agree in a sticky footer (or compact the terms); drop 'below' and 'never-look list' wording on first run; mention WSL only on Windows (patch via homePatches).

title: Setup check and doctor wording: an unexplained warning, jargon labels and a dead-end 'Tell the Ember team'
scenario: On RHEL 9, Fedora or Ubuntu the Setup check shows 'Check – Operating system – Ubuntu 22.04' with no reason (status warn, detail is just PRETTY_NAME; the README says RHEL 8 family only). The same Linux row is 'Screen reading' in Settings but 'Reading apps' in the doctor; the doctor also says 'Compositor', 'XTest', 'File watchers', 'Sandbox' to people who aren't admins, and on macOS lists both 'Microphone' ('Not checked here') and 'Microphone access'. The Windows 'Display scaling' warning ends 'Tell the Ember team.' with no address or link (the About section lists only a log file).
evidence: app/main/environment.ts:139-145 and 241-243; app/main/doctor.ts labels (Reading apps, Compositor, Mouse and keyboard); app/main/platform/win32/system/doctor.ts / doctor.ts:helperRow; doctor output for macOS rendered via formatDoctor.
fix: Add a reason to the OS warn ('Ember is tested on RHEL 8 and its family; this may work, but is not supported'), use one label per check in both surfaces, and give a concrete place to report problems (issue URL) in the About section and the 'Tell the Ember team' text.

title: A broken or too-new admin policy makes Ember delete every audit record older than 30 days
scenario: An organisation keeps audit logs for a year (auditRetentionDays: 365). One host's policy.json gets a typo, or a staged rollout reaches an older Ember that reads the new keys as a mistake (docs say this locks Ember down). On the next start admin.ts uses LOCKDOWN, which has no auditRetentionDays, and main.ts runs audit.prune(policy.auditRetentionDays ?? 30). Every monthly audit file older than 30 days is rm'ed, irreversibly, exactly when the administrator's intent can't be read.
evidence: Script (scratchpad e2.ts): files audit-2026-01, -05, -08, -10 in a dir, now = 2026-10-27. parseAdminPolicy({auditRetentionDays:365, futureKey:1}) returned error 'Unrecognized key' with retention undefined. After prune(retention ?? 30) only audit-2026-10.jsonl was left; with the valid policy (365) Jan, May and Aug would stay. The only use of admin.error besides display is a log line (main.ts:245).
fix: Do not prune while admin.error is set (a locked-down Ember should never delete evidence), or keep the largest retention ever seen in a sidecar file. Document that a broken policy never prunes.

title: Lockdown still connects the brain to GitHub Copilot and forgets the organisation's provider (BYOK) and never-look list
scenario: The organisation requires its own model endpoint ('provider': Ember then never uses a GitHub sign-in) and bans windows with neverLook. The policy is broken (typo, or a newer key on an older Ember, which is documented to lock down). LOCKDOWN turns off actions, voice, desk, screen images and commands but carries no provider and no neverLook. admin.error is only logged and shown in settings, so startBrain resolves a GitHub token (own sign-in, GH CLI or environment) and connects to Copilot. The conductor's describe_screen still reads the focused window, because features.actions=false only stops tasks starting, and the admin's never-look entries are not applied. Screen text the organisation wanted kept in-house goes to github.com. Docs promise only 'no actions, no listening', but the BYOK text says GitHub is never used.
evidence: Lockdown policy from a broken file: provider undefined, neverLook [] (scratchpad e2 and e11). main.ts:1307 builds the provider only from policy.provider; line 1558 'provider ? null : resolveToken(...)'. grep shows admin.error is read only at main.ts:245 and 369. startTask refuses on actions=false (host.ts:974) but conductor tools describe_screen and show_me are unaffected.
fix: While admin.error is set, do not start the brain (or start it only after an explicit user acknowledgement), and do not run describe_screen. At minimum state in docs and settings that a broken policy sends screen text to GitHub, and keep the last-good provider/neverLook values.

title: run_command runs gsettings, dconf and defaults writes unasked: proxy, screen lock, remote desktop, GNOME Shell extensions, macOS password-after-sleep
area: tiers / security settings parity between GUI and commands
scenario: On RHEL 8 a prompt-injected or confused task calls run_command with `gsettings set org.gnome.system.proxy mode 'manual'` plus a proxy host, `gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled false`, `gsettings set org.gnome.shell enabled-extensions "['evil@x']"` or `gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.remote-desktop.rdp enable true`. The verdict is run with no card, no announcement. The GUI policy asks about the same settings (proxy, security stems), so the command channel is a way round the 'security settings' rule. On macOS `defaults write com.apple.screensaver askForPassword -int 0` and `defaults write com.apple.alf globalstate -int 0` also run unasked, as do NSS `certutil -A` CA imports on Linux.
evidence: Classifier output through test/fixtures/commands/corpus.runCase (scratchpad e17/e18): every one of those commands gave verdict 'run', 'ordinary'. Their Windows equivalents (netsh winhttp set proxy, Set-MpPreference, reg add ...\Run) all ask. classify.ts:4584-4585 are two early `return`s for gsettings/dconf (the first is dead code after the second); only LSQuarantine is flagged for defaults. No corpus case covers gsettings or dconf; docs mention gsettings only for the WSL a11y fix.
fix: Classify gsettings/dconf writes to security schemas (org.gnome.system.proxy*, desktop.screensaver, desktop.session idle-delay, desktop.lockdown, desktop.remote-desktop*, desktop.privacy, org.gnome.shell enabled-extensions) and defaults writes to com.apple.screensaver/alf/security domains, plus certutil -A, as system.security (ask). Add corpus cases.

title: Windows 'never run programs' rules (Run dialog, Explorer address box, Open/Run-as commands) only match a few display languages
scenario: A Windows 11 user in Russian, Polish, Turkish, Swedish, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Greek, Ukrainian, Hebrew or Arabic (all unlisted) has given Ember a File Explorer grant. Their Run dialog (title 'Выполнить', box 'Открыть:') and Explorer's address box ('Адрес', 'Adress', 'Adresa', 'Osoite', 'Cím') are not recognised, so type_text of `cmd` or `powershell -c ...` into them is allowed with no question. The Enter or OK that runs it is asked, but the question never says a program will start. The same localized lists decide the Open/Run-as-administrator command labels, so none of the never-rules that exist for English apply.
evidence: Engine run (scratchpad e5, os win32, explorer grant): type 'cmd' into the Run box was deny for en, de, pt, zh-TW, ko, ja and allow ('Ember may act in Explorer') for ru, pl, tr, sv, cs, da, fi, hu, el, uk, he, ar. Address box was deny for en, tr, da, nl, pl, pt and allow for ru, sv, cs, fi, hu, he, ar, el, uk. READ_ONLY_WINDOW title list (vocabulary.ts:249), RUN_BOX (:211) and ADDRESS_BOX (:209) hold only en/de/fr/es/it/pt/nl/ja/zh/ko. The localized strings in the test are from memory; the point is that none of those languages appear in the regexes. Only English Windows is verified by win32-vocabulary CI.
fix: Key the rules off language-independent facts (explorer.exe + dialog class #32770 + the combo's AutomationId or ClassName, the address band's AutomationId) from the UIA bridge, or add the missing Windows display languages and test each one on a localized runner.

title: Explorer 'never open programs or scripts' does nothing while Explorer hides known extensions (the default)
platforms: windows (macOS Finder has no equivalent rule)
scenario: Windows hides extensions of registered file types by default, so setup.exe, install.bat, run.cmd, setup.msi show as 'setup', 'install', 'run'. opensProgram() decides by the item's name ending in .exe/.bat/..., so an Enter or open on such an item is 'any other item'. The user sees only 'Borrow your keyboard to press Enter on “setup” list item in Explorer?' and approving it starts the program with no further dialog (unless the file carries a web mark and the English-only 'Open File - Security Warning' check applies). The same applies to a click that activates the item.
evidence: Engine run (scratchpad e9, os win32, explorer grant): `Enter` on 'setup.exe' / 'install.bat' / 'run.cmd' / 'payload.ps1' = deny; the same keys on 'setup', 'install', 'run' = confirm with the generic 'Ember needs your mouse or keyboard' reason (and a click on 'setup' = allow). The limitation is stated only in a code comment (vocabulary.ts:274-281: 'such an item is judged as any other'). OPENS_PROGRAMS.darwin is empty, so Finder .app/.command items open the same way.
fix: Have the UIA bridge pass the item's ItemType ('Application', 'Windows Batch File', ...) or read the Type column, and refuse Enter and open clicks on those; failing that, refuse Enter on any Explorer item with no extension that isn't a known folder. Document the gap until fixed.

title: Settings that weaken protection or grant device access go through unasked once the Settings app is allowed (GNOME, Windows, macOS)
area: tiers: security settings are 'Never' in PLAN §5
scenario: After one 'Allow' (or 'Always in Settings'), a task in GNOME Settings, Windows Settings or System Settings can flip Automatic Screen Lock, Lock Screen on Suspend, Location Services, Camera, Microphone, Developer Mode, 'Allow Remote Assistance', macOS Camera/Microphone/Photos/Contacts/Bluetooth app toggles or Login Items without a question. A toggle is judged only by its own label's word stems (SECURITY_STEMS) or by an enclosing dialog's wording. App-name toggles ('Terminal' in macOS Camera) and these labels match no stem, and a settings page isn't a dialog. A page-injected goal such as 'turn off the screen lock' is therefore silent.
evidence: Engine runs (scratchpad e8, e7, e15). Linux gnome-control-center with an 'act' grant: switches Location Services, Camera, Microphone, Automatic Screen Lock, Lock Screen on Suspend, Automatic Login all 'allow' (Screen Sharing, Remote Login, File Sharing 'confirm'). macOS System Settings: toggle 'Terminal' in panes Camera, Microphone, Location Services, Photos, Contacts, Files & Folders, Local Network, Bluetooth, Login Items & Extensions, Sharing = allow; only Privacy & Security, Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Full Disk Access, Automation are denied (SECURITY_TITLE.darwin, vocabulary.ts:75). Windows SystemSettings: Camera access, Microphone access, Location services, Developer Mode, 'Allow Remote Assistance...' = allow (Remote Desktop and Sign-in options ask). macOS pane titles are assumed to be the window title.
fix: Treat the Settings apps of each OS (gnome-control-center, SystemSettings, System Settings) as 'security-sensitive': ask for every toggle, or add the missing stems (screen lock, lock screen, location, camera, microphone, developer mode, remote assistance, login/startup items) and the remaining macOS privacy pane titles.

title: The administrator's policy is read once at start on the PC (and a fixed policy isn't picked up either)
scenario: IT disables actions or SSH, adds a never-look entry, or repairs a broken policy. Ember is an autostarted, long-running agent and keeps the snapshot loaded at start; a locked-down Ember stays locked down after the file is fixed, and a running Ember keeps acting after a tightening. The remote helper re-reads every 10 s (app/remote/admin.ts POLICY_EVERY_MS), so the two sides behave differently. No document says a restart is needed.
evidence: grep: adminPolicy.load is called only at main.ts:210 (doctor) and 244 (start); PolicyWatch is used only under app/remote. PolicyEngine, TargetsRuntime and SettingsStore all close over the one `admin` object.
fix: Poll the policy source (mtime for the file, registry value) every 10 s like the remote does and rebuild the engine inputs, or state 'restart Ember after changing the policy' in DEVELOPING.md §5/§10.7/§11.7 and the settings window.

title: The administrator's confirmEveryAction does not apply to commands
scenario: An administrator sets confirmEveryAction: true ('A click before every action, every time') and commands.local: 'on'. Ordinary commands then run with no question, because decideCommand's policyAsk looks only at privileged, commands mode 'ask', the user's ask-every, taint and carried text. The GUI engine honours confirmEveryAction (policy.ts:1821). The docs list it only for GUI actions.
evidence: grep confirmEveryAction: used by PolicyEngine wiring only (main.ts:1416, targets/runtime.ts:1135, desktop-child.ts); not in local-service.ts, wsl-service.ts, remote-service.ts or flow.ts. decideCommand(...) for `ls` with mode 'on' returns 'run' (corpus defaults).
fix: Pass admin.confirmEveryAction into the command service and treat it as mode 'ask' (stricter-of), or document that only commands.* controls commands.

title: The Linux 'run or display' dialog and 'allow executing file as program' rules cover only en/de/fr/es/it/pt
area: never-rules: running programs from the file manager
scenario: On RHEL in Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Polish or Dutch, Nautilus's 'Run' button and Properties' 'Allow executing file as program' check box are not recognised. A task with a Files grant can tick the execute bit without a question, and clicking the dialog's Run button is likewise unasked (Enter on the file is still asked, but generically). Reaching the dialog needs a non-default Nautilus setting (executable-text-activation = ask).
evidence: Engine run (scratchpad e6, os linux, nautilus grant): Run button in en and fr = deny; ru 'Запустить', ja '実行', zh '运行', ko '실행', pl, nl = allow. Check box 'Allow executing file as program' = deny, but the ru, ja, zh, ko, pl, nl equivalents = allow. RUN_WORDS/RUN_FILE_DIALOG/RUN_ANSWER (policy.ts:738-754) list six languages, while RISKY_WORDS covers 16. The translated strings in the test are from memory.
