evidence: Ran buildTargets with host id 'build-01.example.com' (connected) and the picker on 'local': bind({userWords:'on build-01, check the disk'}) gave id 'local'; with choice 'build-01' it gave the 'isn't set up' refusal; with choice 'build-01.example.com' it gave 'The user didn't name that computer'; offerConnect('build-01', words) gave 'Ember doesn't know a computer called build-01…'. resolve.ts bindTarget on the registry's names gave the same results.
fix: Add the first DNS label of the host id, dest host part and resolved hostname as an extra name for each SSH entry when it is unique among hosts and at least MIN_NAME long. Use the same alias list in offerConnect's lookup (runtime.ts:1375). When two hosts share a short name, keep today's TWO_NAMED question.

title: A WSL distro with a versioned name ('Ubuntu-22.04', 'kali-linux') isn't named by 'in Ubuntu': the task silently runs on Windows and the wrong-target guard stays quiet
area: Naming a computer / WSL distro picking
scenario: A distro installed from the Store is called 'Ubuntu-22.04' or 'Ubuntu-24.04', and others are 'kali-linux' or 'openSUSE-Leap-15.5'. A distro's names are its exact name, '<name> (WSL)' and, for the default distro only, WSL/Linux. The docs' example, 'in Ubuntu, list my home folder', names nothing. With no model target the task binds to this PC and runs on Windows. 'in Ubuntu, delete build/' is the worst case: otherTargetsNamed and placesNamed find nothing ('Ubuntu' has no dot, hyphen or digit), so the delete is announced and run on Windows as 'asked'. If the model passes target 'Ubuntu', the user is sent to 'add it in Ember's settings (Computers)' as an SSH host.
evidence: resolve.ts targetsNamed with names ['Ubuntu-22.04','Ubuntu-22.04 (WSL)','WSL','Linux','Linux side']: 'in Ubuntu, list my home folder' gave [] and bindTarget gave local; 'in Ubuntu 22.04…' and 'in WSL…' gave the distro. Through the runtime rig (win32, WSL on, distro 'Ubuntu-22.04'): bind(no choice) gave local; bind(choice 'Ubuntu') gave the 'isn't set up…offer_connect' refusal; offerConnect('Ubuntu') gave 'Ember doesn't know a computer called Ubuntu. Tell the user to add it in Ember's settings (Computers).'; agent.othersNamed('local','in Ubuntu, delete build/') gave [].
fix: Give each distro an extra name for its leading word(s) before the first '-', '_' or digit ('Ubuntu', 'kali', 'openSUSE') when unique among distros. Also let otherTargetsNamed count that name, so a destructive request that names it always asks. If the words only partly match one distro, refuse with 'Did you mean Ubuntu-22.04 (WSL)?'.

title: The same computer added under two spellings creates two records, a second consent card, a repeated 'Bring Ember' offer and a connection that can fight the first for the remote's lock
area: Adding a computer / Bring Ember offer
scenario: The user adds 'build-01' (an alias) in settings and connects. They later run 'ssh deploy@build-01' in a terminal. The noticer compares dest strings only, so it offers 'You're connected to build-01. Bring Ember there too?' although Ember is already connected. Clicking Bring Ember creates 'build-01-2' (same deploy@build-01.example.com) with its own card and connection. Settings then lists two identical rows. The remote helper allows one agent per PC and user: the second agent waits the grace plus 3 s, then SIGTERMs the first. The first then shows 'Lost build-01' and starts its own reconnect loop, which does the same to the second, so they can alternate every 20 to 25 s. The same dedupe gap makes 'on build-01.example.com' match both hosts, and Ember then asks 'which one'.
evidence: Rig: host {id:'build-01', dest:'build-01'} connected; act add 'deploy@build-01' gave ok and settings.hosts [build-01:build-01:deploy@build-01.example.com, build-01-2:deploy@build-01:deploy@build-01.example.com], with a second consent card 'Bring Ember to build-01-2?'. Noticer with seen dest 'deploy@build-01' while 'build-01' is connected still showed the bubble 'You're connected to build-01'. sameDest (runtime.ts:193) compares h.dest and port only, and is used at lines 791 and 1039. app/remote/lock.ts:80-100 shows the same-pcId wait then SIGTERM takeover.
fix: Dedupe on the resolved identity (user, hostname, port, jump list) from ssh -G, not on the typed string. In addAndConnect, reuse the matching record and connect it. In the noticer's connected() and dismissed(), compare resolved identities too. Tell the user 'already added as build-01'.

title: First-use consent cards sit in a fixed 440x300 window and show only about half their text; 'Connect' / 'Turn on' works after 0.9 s without reading
scenario: The SSH card ('Bring Ember to build-01?') is about 360 px of text in a 198 px scrolling body: it shows through the helper-size paragraph. 'Your voice and your GitHub sign-in stay on this computer', what it reads on the screen there, and 'build-01 keeps its own record' are below the fold. The commands card is 426 px in 198 px, so the part about output going to Copilot, the privacy-related rules and the stop chord are hidden. Only a thin scrollbar (classic scrollbars on Linux; overlay scrollbars hide it on macOS and often on Windows 11) hints at more. The window is not resizable and nothing resizes it. Unlike the command card, the Yes button is not gated on the whole text having been seen.
evidence: Rendered dist/app/renderer/prompt at 440x300 with the real cards from consentText/sshConsent: body scrollHeight vs clientHeight was 364/198 (SSH card with jump host and key), 346/198 (machine changed), 426/198 (commands card with podman and root lines). Screenshots show the cut-off. windows.ts has width 440, height 300, resizable false, and prompt-window.ts never calls setBounds. pressResult/promptView set the consent Yes button to armed:true (a 900 ms delay) only.
fix: Size the prompt window to the card (consent cards about 520-560 px high, capped to the work area), or switch to a larger consent layout. Also keep 'Connect'/'Turn on' disabled until the body has been scrolled to its end, as the command card does ('Read the whole command to allow it'), or add a visible 'Scroll to read all' fade.

title: Connection failures, including 'host key changed', disappear after 14 s with no action; the documented 'identity changed' card is never shown and the bubble clips the fix
scenario: For every non-retryable failure the bubble 'Can't connect to build-01' has no buttons and hides after 2*INFO_MS = 14 s. This applies to changed host key, too many keys, a config line SSH can't use, no OpenSSH, an old OpenSSH, no disk space, noexec/fapolicyd, the admin's allowedHosts and remote policy, and most of the messages in the docs' §4.8 table. They all carry a fix sentence. When the connect came from a 'Bring Ember' or Connect bubble, nothing else shows the reason (settings' message line only shows for connects started there). The changed-key text is 7 lines in a bubble whose error mood clips at 6, so 'then connect again.' is cut. The bubble is also dropped entirely while a Confirmer question is up (guardWhileAsking drops bubble patches and the runtime never re-shows it). docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §4.1 promises 'build-01's identity changed', but the 'host-key-changed' card (renderer/prompt/copy.ts:66, remote-ui.ts, prompt-window.ts) has no producer: promptCard() never creates it.
evidence: Rig: failConnect(ConnectError kind host-key-changed, retry false) gave bubbles 'Connecting to build-01…' then 'Can't connect to build-01 | …Ember won't connect. If you know why… | actions [] | mood error', with one 14 s timer. Overlay render at 900x600: .eb-thought scrollHeight 140 vs clientHeight 120 for the key-changed text, overflow hidden, with a faded cut line. grep shows no code constructs kind 'host-key-changed' anywhere. guardWhileAsking (agent/confirm.ts:257) drops bubble patches while asking.
fix: Show non-retryable failures until dismissed (a 'Close' button, plus 'Open settings' where it applies) and keep the last failure in the host's settings row. Produce the host-key-changed PromptCard (it is already built and validated) for that case instead of a bubble, or at least use the 'attention' mood (10 lines, scrollable). Re-show a runtime bubble that was dropped while a question was up.

title: 'Bring Ember to a computer…' and the WSL offer's 'Open settings' don't scroll to Computers when Settings isn't already open
area: Settings navigation / WSL offer / adding a computer
scenario: The user clicks the WSL offer's 'Open settings', or the handle menu's 'Bring Ember to a computer…', with the settings window closed. main creates the window and sends focus-section 'computers' at did-finish-load. The Computers section is hidden until both the targets list and getStatus have answered, and showSection() returns silently for a hidden section. Settings opens at the top ('Your Ember', the character cards) with nothing marking Computers, which is about 1700 px down. The WSL switch or the host field is never focused.
evidence: Real Electron run under xvfb: closed the home window, app.emit('second-instance') (showHome), then sent 'ember:focus-section'/'computers' at did-finish-load exactly as sendToHome does. Result: activeElement BODY, scrollY 0, #computers hidden false, #computers-h top 1705 px. Static harness with a 1.5 s getStatus gave the same. Cause: renderer/home/main.ts:613 returns when the target is hidden, and computers.ts hides the section until summaries and settings are both known.
fix: Remember a pending section in the page when showSection() finds it hidden, and apply it from draw() once Computers appears. Focus the host input (or the WSL switch) after scrolling.

title: After a dropped connection Ember silently switches to this computer and stays there after an automatic reconnect
scenario: build-01 is the picked computer. The link drops and the bubble says 'Lost build-01 … I'll try to reconnect', without saying work moves to this computer, so the handle badge and ask-box chip just disappear. The reconnect then succeeds (adopt at line 1091). The bubble hides with no 'build-01 is back', and the picker stays on This computer. 'Check the disk' typed next runs here and its answer carries no 'on build-01' badge or note.
evidence: onLinkState 'lost' calls setActive(LOCAL_TARGET) and shows the bubble text above. The progress 'ready' handler only runs adopt() and hideBubble(lost:…). test/unit/targets-runtime.test.ts line 700 asserts active 'local' after loss and nothing after the reconnect.
fix: Say it in the lost bubble ('I'll work on this computer until it's back'). After an automatic reconnect show 'build-01 is back' with 'Work on build-01', or restore the picker if it was active when lost.

title: Cancel on the connecting bubble (or Forget, or the stop chord) leaves the first-use consent card on screen; its 'Connect' then does nothing
scenario: 'Connecting to build-01… [Cancel]' is on screen while the 'Bring Ember to build-01?' card waits. The user clicks the bubble's Cancel, or presses the stop chord. The card stays up with no hint that it's void, and answering it silently ends with 'Cancelled.' (nothing saved, no feedback).
evidence: Rig: pending card via pw.ask; bubbleAction('conn:build-02:cancel') gave pw.dismiss calls 0 and hideConsent 0; the later yes returned {ok:false,message:'Cancelled.'} and the host consent stayed {version:0}. askCard never wires the abort signal to promptWindow.dismiss.
fix: Pass the connection's AbortSignal to askCard and call promptWindow.dismiss(card.id) when it aborts (Cancel, Forget, stopAll).

title: Connection progress rewrites the bubble on every network chunk, over any answer or task the user is looking at
scenario: While Ember downloads the 29 MB runtime or copies the helper, the user asks something else or a task is streaming. Each chunk replaces the visible bubble with 'Connecting to build-01… Downloading… (12 of 29 MB)'. The answer or task bubble flashes and is overwritten many times a second until the connect ends, and IPC to the overlay and handle is sent per chunk.
evidence: Rig: 500 download progress events gave 500 showState bubble updates with only 30 distinct texts. The handler calls bubble() unconditionally and has no check on what the bubble currently shows.
fix: Update only when the words or whole-MB figure changes, and only if no other bubble has replaced the connecting one since (shown.key). Otherwise show progress in the handle's status or the settings row.

title: Add-computer form empties the field before the result and gives no feedback while the card or connection is pending
scenario: The user types 'bild-01.example.com' and presses Connect. The field clears at once. Ember answers 'Ember can't find bild-01.example.com. Check the name, or add it to your SSH config.' and the user must retype the whole name to fix a typo. Meanwhile (the SSH card waiting, or a 30 s connect) the page shows nothing; no row exists until the host is saved after the card.
evidence: Playwright harness: right after Enter the input value was '' and the act was pending; after the act resolved {ok:false} the input stayed '' and the message showed. computers.ts clears the input before awaiting act().
fix: Clear the field only on success, and show 'Waiting for your OK in the window that opened…' / 'Connecting…' in the message line while the act is pending.

title: A stopped WSL distro is announced as 'not connected' in the handle badge and its accessible name
scenario: The user picks 'Ubuntu (WSL)' in Work on while it's stopped (distros stop when idle). The handle shows a grey dot and the tooltip/aria-label 'Working on Ubuntu (WSL) (not connected)'. A distro isn't connected to anything and starts on the first command.
evidence: registry.ts gives state 'off' for a distro that isn't running; targetBadge returned label 'Working on Ubuntu (WSL) (not connected)' for it (run against the real functions).
fix: For kind 'wsl' and state 'off' say '(stopped)' or nothing, and use a neutral dot. Keep 'not connected' for SSH.

title: Status words in Settings' Computers list mislead: 'Connected: nothing yet', 'Connected: isn't answering', WSL distros 'Not available' when only WSL is off, 'Disconnect' while connecting
scenario: A connected headless host with commands off reads 'Connected: nothing yet', with no hint that turning commands on is the next step. A stalled link reads 'Connected: isn't answering'. With WSL off every distro reads 'Not available' (note: 'WSL is off in Ember') although the distro is fine and one switch away. A row that is still connecting offers 'Disconnect' where 'Cancel' is meant.
evidence: Rendered the Computers section with summaries can 'nothing yet' and 'isn't answering' and WSL 'unavailable' rows: the strings above appear. sshStatus() builds 'Connected: ${t.can}', wslStatus() maps unavailable to 'Not available', and connected includes state 'connecting'.
fix: 'Connected, commands off' (with a hint or link to the Commands switch), 'Connected, not answering', 'Off' for WSL-disabled distros, and 'Cancel' while connecting.

title: 'Remove Ember from <computer>' gives no progress, no cancel and no success message, and silently forgets the computer
scenario: The user confirms the dialog. Ember connects (possibly with a password or host-key card that is titled only 'Sign in to build-01', with no mention of removal) and runs the removal, which can take a minute. The row shows no change. If a task or command is running there it is stopped with no warning in the dialog. On success the row vanishes with no message, and the host record and its commands consent are also deleted (so the commands and SSH cards must be accepted again on re-adding). The dialog doesn't say any of that.
evidence: runtime.ts:837 'uninstall' awaits connections.uninstall(host) then forget(host.id), with no bubble or message. The progress handler ignores steps unless state is 'connecting'. The confirm text is: 'Remove Ember's helper from build-01? Its record of what Ember did there stays on build-01.'
fix: Show 'Removing Ember from build-01…' with a Cancel in the row, say 'Removed. build-01 is no longer in your list' on success, and add 'It also stops anything running there and forgets the computer here' to the confirm.

title: The SSH consent card is generic where it should be specific, and a repeat card doesn't say what changed
scenario: The card is built before the probe, so it always says 'unpacked… in ~/.local/share/ember-remote', even for a Mac that gets '~/Library/Application Support/Ember Remote/'. It always says 'On build-01's screen it reads and uses apps only when…' even for a server with no desktop. When ssh -G now resolves the name to a different user, hostname or port, the same card appears ('Bring Ember to build-01?') with the new details in the first line but no 'Your SSH settings now send build-01 to X (was Y)'. Only a changed machine gets a warning line.
evidence: consent.ts sshConsent hard-codes the install dir and the screen sentence and adds a warning only when facts.machineChanged. sshNeedsConsent (line ~159) returns true on resolution change without passing a reason. Rendered cards show identical wording.
fix: Add 'the folder for its system' wording ('~/.local/share/ember-remote on Linux, ~/Library/… on a Mac') or a 'Mac' variant. Pass a changedFrom fact so a repeat card leads with 'Your SSH settings now send build-01 to deploy@new.example.com:22 (before: deploy@old.example.com:22).'

title: Cancelling a password or passphrase card is reported as an error: 'Can't connect to build-01 — Connection cancelled' with 'Try again'
scenario: The user clicks Cancel (or presses Esc) on 'Sign in to build-01'. The connection ends and an error-mood bubble titled 'Can't connect to build-01' says 'Connection cancelled' with Try again. Declining the consent card or the bubble's Cancel are silent ('Not now'), so the same intent gets an error style here.
evidence: attempt() sets cancelledByUser when answer.ok is false; failureOf returns {kind:'cancelled', message:'Connection cancelled', retry:true}; runtime fail() then shows the error bubble.
fix: Treat a user-cancelled card like Cancel: hide the connecting bubble and return {ok:false, message:'Cancelled.'}; show no error bubble.

title: Remote app grants are listed in Settings as raw keys ('ssh:build-01:gedit', 'Remove ssh:build-01:gedit')
area: Settings: apps Ember may act in / WSL and SSH apps
scenario: The user answers 'Always in gedit' for a task on build-01. Under 'Apps Ember may act in without asking first' the entry reads 'ssh:build-01:gedit', and its Remove button's accessible name is 'Remove ssh:build-01:gedit'. Local entries read 'gedit'.
evidence: friendlyApp('ssh:build-01:gedit') returned 'ssh:build-01:gedit' unchanged (run with esbuild); worker.ts stores grants under hands.grantKey, which is `${id}:${app}` for remote targets.
fix: Render 'gedit on build-01' (and 'gedit in Ubuntu (WSL)') for keys with an 'ssh:<id>:' prefix.

title: The 'Ember can work in WSL' offer only appears after the user names WSL in a request while it's off; the docs say 'when Ember first sees WSL'
scenario: A Windows user with WSL installed who never says 'in WSL' is never offered WSL: the only path is settings › Computers. The offer then also needs the model to pass a target or the user's words to contain 'WSL' (not 'Linux').
evidence: offerWsl() has one caller, inside bind(), behind targetsNamed(words, 'WSL'). docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:271 says 'When Ember first sees WSL it offers…'; CHANGELOG repeats that WSL is off until turned on.
fix: Either offer once when discovery first finds a usable distro (after onboarding, at most once, with 'Not now' sticking), or change the docs to say it is offered after you ask for WSL.

title: Backticked commands show their backticks in plain-text bubbles and settings messages; a failed reconnect on an unknown host key says 'sign in again'
scenario: The key-changed fix reads 'remove the old key in a terminal with `ssh-keygen -R build-01`', and the OpenSSH-missing message 'Install OpenSSH (Linux: `sudo dnf install openssh-clients`; Windows: …)', with literal backticks, because the bubble and the settings line use textContent. Also the reconnect handler treats unknown-host-key as 'sign in again' (runtime.ts:1098), though no sign-in is needed.
evidence: Rendered the overlay with the message text: backticks are visible. bubble.ts setThought uses textContent. MESSAGES.* contain backticks; p.kind === 'unknown-host-key' maps to signInAgain().
fix: Drop the backticks, or render code spans in these two surfaces. Word the reconnect needing a host key as 'build-01 needs you to check its key again' with Reconnect.

title: A known host that isn't connected tells the model 'Connect it from Ember's menu first' and never mentions offer_connect
scenario: 'on build-01, check the disk' with build-01 added but disconnected binds to it, and handsFor refuses with that sentence. A model that follows it tells the user to use the menu (Work on › build-01), when offer_connect would put a Connect button right in the bubble, as it does for unknown hosts.
evidence: registry.ts:178 and runtime.ts:1189 produce the text; offerConnect() handles a known, disconnected host correctly (rig: it shows the 'Connect to build-01?' bubble).
fix: Make the refusal say 'Call offer_connect so the user can click Connect' (the lost case: 'Reconnect it from the bubble or Settings', since the menu item is disabled while lost).

title: Small copy and layout issues in Settings › Computers
scenario: The intro says 'Ember can work… in WSL' on Linux and macOS, where WSL is never offered. The host field's placeholder is cut at narrow widths ('…deploy@bu'). The 'Let Ember work in WSL' switch sits below every SSH row, so a Windows user with several computers has to scroll for it. Nothing shows which distro 'WSL' and 'Linux' mean (the default one), so with two distros the user can't tell where 'in WSL' goes.
evidence: Rendered at 900 and 420 px (Linux, then Windows with WSL rows): intro text above, placeholder truncated at 420 px, the switch after the rows. The summary never marks the default distro.
fix: Show the WSL sentence only on Windows. Shorten the placeholder ('build-01 or user@host'). Put the WSL switch above the list and mark the default distro 'Default for "in WSL"'.

title: A packaged Ember can only sign in through the GitHub CLI, and the install docs never say so
platforms: all (worst on Windows and macOS, where gh is not normally installed)
scenario: A person installs the RPM, zip or dmg exactly as README.md says and presses "Sign in with GitHub" in the first-run window. Ember's own GitHub App is not registered (PLAN.md §7 item 1 is still "Open"), and the device flow only runs when the environment variable EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is set, which a Start-menu or Finder launch will not have. So the button only shows "In a terminal, run 'gh auth login'...". Without the GitHub CLI installed, nothing in the window or in README.md tells them to install it, and no other sign-in path exists. The result is a running Ember that can never connect to Copilot. The doctor's Copilot row gives the same advice.
evidence: main.ts:964-972 reads process.env.EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. It is not gated by devEnv, but no packaged build supplies one. When it is unset, the only message is "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”..." (also app/renderer/home/copy.ts:55 and app/main/doctor.ts:168). `grep -n -i "gh auth\|GitHub CLI\|sign in" README.md` finds no sign-in guidance in the Linux, Windows or macOS install sections. The gh requirement appears only in docs/DEVELOPING.md:191-205. PLAN.md:389: "Who registers Ember's GitHub App? Open".
fix: Before release, register the GitHub App and bake its (public) client id into the build, for example from package.json or an esbuild define, keeping the env var as an override. If the release has to ship without it, put a "Sign in needs the GitHub CLI: install it from cli.github.com, run gh auth login" step in each README install section. Make the sign-in window say it, with a link, when gh is not found.

title: An install path containing a literal % makes every settings/IPC call throw "URI malformed"
area: paths with special characters / first run
scenario: Someone extracts the Windows zip to a folder such as D:\Tools\100% Free\Ember (or runs an AppImage from a folder with a % in its name). BrowserWindow.loadFile does not percent-encode the % in the file URL. isTrustedSender() then calls decodeURIComponent on the sender URL, which throws URIError. Every IPC handler guarded by it fails: ember:get-status, agent:status, agent:conversation, voice:status, targets:list, ember:activity and ember:presence. The windows open but stay dead: no status, no sign-in, no settings. Nothing explains why.
evidence: I staged the Linux tree and ran a copy at ".../Tools C# 100% (x86) & Zoë's/Ember/ember". The log has "Error occurred in handler for 'ember:get-status': URIError: URI malformed at decodeURIComponent at isTrustedSender (main.cjs)", 13 handler errors in all, 7 distinct channels. The same tree at ".../Tools C# (x86) & Zoë's/Ember" (spaces, #, &, ', parentheses and non-ASCII, no %) has 0 errors and shows its window. The only decodeURIComponent in app/ is windows.ts:138. A related nit: autostart.ts execArg (lines 25-29) does not double a % in Exec=, which the Desktop Entry spec requires.
fix: Make isTrustedSender total. Wrap the decode in try/catch and return false on a throw, or better, compare against pathToFileURL(appDir).href + "/renderer/" instead of decoding. Add a unit case with "100%" and "50%AB" in trusted-sender.test.ts. Escape % as %% in execArg.

title: Windows: the UI Automation bridge compiles its C# with Add-Type -Path, which treats [ and ] in the install path as wildcards
area: paths with special characters / Windows helper
scenario: A user extracts Ember into a folder with square brackets, for example C:\Users\Jane [Work]\Apps\Ember or D:\Tools [portable]\Ember. The bridge reads $PSScriptRoot\ember_uia.cs with [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes, which is literal and works. Both Add-Type calls then use -Path, so PowerShell resolves [Work] as a character class and finds no file. The cached-build branch falls back to memory, which fails the same way, and Write-Fatal reports "Cannot find path". Ember can then never read apps. The doctor's Accessibility helper row fails with a path error that does not mention brackets.
evidence: Source reading only; no Windows host here and pwsh is not installed. Add-Type's -Path is documented to accept wildcards, and -LiteralPath exists for exactly this. ember_uia.ps1:78 and :95 both use `Add-Type -Path $source`. The sibling askpass compile (askpass-win.ts) avoids the problem by using -TypeDefinition with ReadAllText.
fix: Use `Add-Type -LiteralPath $source` in both places (Windows PowerShell 5.1 has it). Add a W-series integration case that stages Ember under a folder named "a [b]".

title: AppImage doctor reports FAIL "Sandbox" on user-namespace-off hosts, with a fix for files that do not exist in an AppImage
scenario: On a hardened RHEL 8 host (user.max_user_namespaces=0) the AppImage's AppRun deliberately starts Ember with --no-sandbox, so Ember runs. The user then runs `Ember-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage doctor`. The doctor probes only user namespaces and a setuid chrome-sandbox next to the binary, which an AppImage cannot have, so it prints "FAIL Sandbox ... fix: sudo chown root:root /opt/ember/chrome-sandbox && sudo chmod 4755 ..." and "1 problem to fix before Ember can work", exit status 1. /opt/ember does not exist.
evidence: appimage.sh:44 adds --no-sandbox when max_user_namespaces is 0. The doctor's sandbox row (doctor.ts:200-204) has no way to know. I ran doctorChecks with sandbox {userNamespaces:false, suidHelper:false}: it prints the FAIL row, the /opt/ember fix and "1 problem to fix before Ember can work." (scratch script doctor-sandbox.mjs). On an AppImage the files are in a nosuid squashfs, so suidHelper is always false.
fix: Let the probe see that the process was started with --no-sandbox, or that APPIMAGE is set. In the AppImage case report a warn such as "Running without Chromium's sandbox (AppImage on a host with user namespaces off); use the RPM on hardened hosts", with no chown advice.

title: RPM upgrade replaces files under a running Ember, and nothing tells the user to restart
scenario: Ember starts at login and stays resident, so `sudo dnf upgrade ember` normally runs while the old Ember is up. rpm swaps /opt/ember/* underneath it. The old main process keeps its code in memory, but the next window it opens (settings, ask, command window) loads the new version's renderer pages and preload scripts from disk. A mixed-version Ember follows (IPC channel or payload mismatches) until someone quits and restarts it. The Windows and macOS README sections say "quit Ember" before updating; the Linux README has no update section at all. The spec has no scriptlet or notice about a running Ember.
evidence: Reasoning from code: %post/%postun/%posttrans (spec lines 89-103) only refresh desktop and icon caches. renderer and preload files are read by path on window creation (app/main/windows.ts:36 and friends, loadFile). The app has no check for its own install changing. I could not run rpm here, so the failure itself is not reproduced. README.md:52 and :86 give the quit-first instruction only for Windows and macOS.
fix: Add a README line for Linux ("quit Ember, then dnf upgrade; Ember starts again at your next login"). Better, have Ember compare app.getVersion() with the version in resources/app/package.json on disk when it opens a window and offer "Restart Ember". At minimum add a %posttrans echo.

title: Linux has no uninstall guidance, and the autostart entry survives dnf remove
scenario: A user who turned on "Start Ember when I log in" runs `sudo dnf remove ember`. ~/.config/autostart/ember.desktop stays and keeps pointing at /usr/bin/ember --autostart. ~/.config/ember (including github-token.bin, logs, audit and 126 MB of models), ~/Ember and the Node runtime for remotes also stay. README.md gives Windows and macOS removal steps listing exactly these paths; the Linux section has none.
evidence: autostartEntry (autostart.ts:31-45) has Exec= but no TryExec=, so the desktop cannot skip a missing binary quietly. The RPM has no %preun/%postun cleanup of per-user files (rpm cannot reach home folders). README.md:10-25 (Linux) vs :52-56 and :86-90.
fix: Add `TryExec=` (the same path as Exec's first word) to the autostart entry. Add a short "To remove Ember" paragraph to the Linux README: turn off start at login, `sudo dnf remove ember`, delete ~/.config/ember and ~/Ember.

title: The Linux launcher shows a raw Chromium error when there is no display
scenario: Someone runs `ember` from an ssh session without -X, or from a TTY. They get "ERROR:ui/ozone/platform/x11/ozone_platform_x11.cc:257] Missing X server or $DISPLAY" and "The platform failed to initialize. Exiting.", with no mention of `ember doctor`, which would have explained it. `ember doctor` itself handles the no-display case by going headless.
evidence: Ran the staged binary with `env -u DISPLAY ... --ozone-platform=x11`: exit 1, only those two Chromium lines. The launcher's default path (line 25) does not check DISPLAY, while the doctor branch (line 14) does.
fix: In the launcher, before the final exec: if DISPLAY is empty, print "Ember needs your desktop session (no display here). Run it from a terminal inside GNOME, or run 'ember doctor'." and exit 1.

title: README offers the AppImage "without installing" but it still needs the RPM's system packages
scenario: A RHEL 8 user without python3-pyatspi (or Xvfb, speech-dispatcher...) runs the AppImage as the README suggests. Ember starts, but cannot read any app: the sidecar runs on the host's platform-python and the AppImage carries only the Electron side. The window shows setup-check failures. The README sentence gives no hint, and the doctor's speech-model fix text also says "or install ember-voice-models", an RPM that an AppImage user cannot use.
evidence: The AppImage carries only dist/package/ember. python3-pyatspi, python3-gobject and at-spi2-core are RPM Requires (spec lines ~31-33), and the sidecar is spawned with the system Python (app/main/perception/sidecar.ts:186-190). My AppImage doctor run printed "warn Reading apps: Python accessibility bindings are missing" and "or install ember-voice-models".
fix: Change the sentence to "... without installing Ember itself; it still needs `sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi python3-gobject at-spi2-core` (run `Ember.AppImage doctor`)". Drop the ember-voice-models hint when APPIMAGE is set.

title: CI never upgrades or removes the RPM, and never builds the ember-voice-models package
scenario: The release RPMs (including the `with_models` branch: %package voice-models, the %install copy and %files voice-models) are first exercised by whoever builds them for release. A mistake in that branch, in an upgrade over the previous RPM, or in the removal that leaves /opt/ember or /usr/share/ember behind would first show up on a customer's host.
evidence: The package job installs once with dnf and checks files (ci.yml:147-185). It never runs scripts/voice/prepare.mjs (only the checks and eval jobs do, lines 60 and 231), so rpm.sh builds with with_models=0. There is no `dnf upgrade`, `rpm -e` or `rpm -V` step. I have no rpmbuild here, so I only read the spec.
fix: In the package job: build once with a stub voice-models folder (verified markers) and install both RPMs. Then rebuild with Release 2, `dnf upgrade`, `rpm -V ember`, `rpm -e ember ember-voice-models`, and assert /opt/ember, /usr/share/ember and /usr/bin/ember are gone while /etc/ember/policy.json is kept.

title: packaging/policy.example.json predates commands, WSL and SSH; copying it as-is switches those features off
platforms: linux (and any remote with the file)
scenario: An administrator copies the RPM's /usr/share/doc/ember/policy.example.json to /etc/ember/policy.json to start from the shipped example. A policy that exists without a `commands` key makes commands "off" for local, WSL and SSH, so the release's headline feature is silently unavailable. No row or message says why. The same file on a remote makes the helper there refuse commands.
evidence: admin.ts:196-203 commandMode: source !== null and no `commands` key gives "off". The example has no commands, ssh, features.wsl or features.ssh keys. The CHANGELOG and DEVELOPING.md warn about it, but the file the RPM actually ships does not show the keys.
fix: Add `"commands": {"local": "on", "wsl": "on", "ssh": "on"}` and an `"ssh": {}` example to policy.example.json, or a comment-style companion README, so the shipped example reflects the current schema.

title: stage.mjs does not require the SSH/command helpers it ships (askpass.cjs, remote-link.cjs, job-host.cjs)
scenario: A partial or stale dist/app, for example a build that failed after main.cjs, stages without error. The package then ships with no Windows job host or no SSH password helper or link worker, and SSH or command windows fail only at first use.
evidence: COMMON_DIST (layout.mjs:30) and each target's requiredDist list main.cjs, voice.cjs, the renderer files, and ax-sidecar.cjs/desk-agent.cjs. askpass.cjs, remote-link.cjs and job-host.cjs (built by scripts/build-app.mjs and located by connections.ts:272, askpass-server.ts:264 and router.ts:821) are not listed, although stage.mjs guarantees "Every file the target needs must exist".
fix: Add askpass.cjs and remote-link.cjs to the Linux and macOS requiredDist, and remote-link.cjs and job-host.cjs to Windows.

title: Removing Ember from a PC leaves its helper on every SSH computer, and the README removal steps do not mention it
scenario: A user deletes the Ember folder (Windows) or app (macOS) following the README without clicking "Remove Ember from build-01" first. build-01 keeps ~/.local/share/ember-remote with the Node runtime and parts, and per-machine consent, lock and audit files. The error text elsewhere says it needs about 400 MB, and nothing on the PC remains to remove it. The remote's README.txt tells an admin how to run uninstall.sh, but the person who set it up is never told.
evidence: README.md:52-56 (Windows) and :86-90 (macOS) list the shortcut, login item and data folder, but not remote computers. CHANGELOG notes "Remove Ember from build-01 removes the helper again". uninstall.sh and the part's README.txt exist only on the remote.
fix: Add "If you added computers over SSH, choose **Remove Ember from <computer>** for each before removing Ember (or run sh ~/.local/share/ember-remote/versions/*/uninstall.sh there)" to the removal paragraphs.

title: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES carries no licence text for @github/copilot-sdk, its runtime, sherpa-onnx or koffi's platform package
scenario: The packaged notices say "(no licence file in the package; its package.json gives the licence above)" for these four packages. For MIT and Apache-2.0 software the licence text and copyright line need to travel with redistributed copies. sherpa-onnx's WebAssembly also embeds third-party runtimes (for example onnxruntime) that the notices do not list, and the 136 MB Copilot runtime is a bundled application whose own third-party notices are not shipped.
evidence: grep in dist/package/ember/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES: sections at lines 133-135 (@github/copilot-sdk), 391-393 (sherpa-onnx), 424-426 (@github/copilot-sdk-linux-x64), 465-467 (@koromix/koffi-linux-x64) end in that fallback line. Apache-2.0 and MIT texts do appear for other packages, but with other copyright holders. I did not check upstream tarballs for notice files beyond what npm installed.
fix: Have stage.mjs fail when a package has no licence file and a small allow-list does not supply its text. Add the missing texts (MIT for the GitHub packages, Apache-2.0 for sherpa-onnx, plus onnxruntime's notice) to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Ask the upstream owners for a notices file for the runtime. This is a legal review item, not a build break.

title: docs/DEVELOPING.md §10.5 lists what the Windows folder holds but omits remote-parts, the WSL helper and the askpass source
scenario: A maintainer or administrator checking an extracted zip against §10.5 finds resources\remote-parts, resources\sidecar\atspi\ember_atspi.py and resources\ssh\ember_askpass.cs and has no description of what they are, or whether they should be on an allow-list (they are compiled or run by Ember at use).
evidence: layout.mjs:79-84 stages ember_atspi.py and ember_askpass.cs for win32 and stage.mjs:171-179 stages remote-parts. The §10.5 table names only sidecar\uia, ember.ico, ember-doctor.cmd and the notices.
fix: Add the three entries to the table with one line each (WSL's Linux-app helper, the SSH password helper compiled on first use, the helper archives sent to SSH computers).

title: "Sign in with GitHub" is a dead end: it only says to run gh auth login, and the README never mentions Copilot or the GitHub CLI
scenario: A new user on a packaged build (EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is unset) opens Settings, sees "Not connected to Copilot: sign in with GitHub below.", presses Sign in with GitHub, and gets "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”…". Nothing says the GitHub CLI must be installed first (Windows and macOS don't ship it), and "Check again" repeats "Run gh auth login". README.md has no get-started or sign-in section: its only sign-in mentions are about uninstalling and the SSH note.
evidence: Ran the real app under xvfb with GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN and EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID unset and gh off PATH. The Copilot section showed that agent line and button, and after the click "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”. Ember will notice within a few seconds and connect; no restart needed." (screenshot shots/signin.png under the scratch folder). Check again gave copy.ts:55 "No GitHub sign-in found on this computer. Run “gh auth login” in a terminal…". grep finds EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID only in auth.ts, main.ts and PLAN.md §7 (open question 1: the GitHub App is not registered). The gh-CLI route is documented only in docs/DEVELOPING.md.
fix: Short term, make the words honest: label the button "Connect with GitHub CLI", or have the message say "Install the GitHub CLI (cli.github.com), then run “gh auth login” in a terminal", and give copy.ts:55 the same sentence. Add a "First run" section to README.md saying you need a GitHub account with Copilot and, until Ember's app is registered, the GitHub CLI signed in (or GH_TOKEN). Better: register the app and bake the client id into packaged builds.

title: Command approval card shows a tool name and model-directed advice: "Open apps with open_app instead."
scenario: The user's task runs `gedit notes.txt`, `firefox …`, `notepad` or `regedit`. The Allow / Not now card reads "Ember can't tell exactly what this does.", then "Open apps with open_app instead.", then "You didn't ask for this." open_app is an internal tool name and the sentence is advice to the model, so it is meaningless to the person deciding. The same card also carries phrasing like "Ember can't tell what ls is given.", "It uses $ExecutionContext.", "It uses a translated string." and "It spells the program with ^ escapes."
evidence: Ran classifyCommand and decideCommand from the test fixtures: `gedit notes.txt` gives says = ["Ember can't tell exactly what this does.","Open apps with open_app instead.","You didn't ask for this."], and the same for firefox, notepad, regedit and Out-GridView. `ls $(pwd)` gives "Ember can't tell what ls is given." `echo $"hi"` gives "It uses a translated string." SAYS.openApp is used at classify.ts:1922, 3336, 4410, 4703, 4845 and 5101, and `says` goes straight to the card (flow.ts:671-676).
fix: Reword for the reader: "This opens an app window, which Ember can do itself without a command. Say no and ask Ember to open it." Also: "Ember can't tell which arguments ls gets.", "It uses PowerShell's $ExecutionContext, which Ember can't follow.", "It uses locale-translated text ($\"…\"), which Ember can't check."

title: A refused SSH command shows a doubled prefix and stray quote-period: "build-01 refused it: build-01 refused it: \"…\"."
scenario: build-01's own administrator policy (or gate 2) denies a command that the PC had already allowed. The command tab is already attached, and its status line reads "build-01 refused it: build-01 refused it: \"This computer's administrator has turned off commands from Ember.\"." The model gets the same doubling. The quoted remote sentence also says "This computer's administrator", which on the user's PC reads as the user's own computer.
evidence: The runner builds error = `${label} refused it: ${said}` (remote-runner.ts:181, pinned by remote-runner.test.ts:150), and statusLine prepends the prefix again. A probe of statusLine with that exact error prints: build-01 refused it: build-01 refused it: "This computer's administrator has turned off commands from Ember.". The trailing .". comes from clause() stripping only unquoted full stops. ui-copy.test.ts:274 pins only an unprefixed error, so the integrated path is untested. window.ts:500 calls statusLine on run.done, which passes the exit through unchanged.
fix: Make one side own the prefix: have the runner set error to just the quoted reason (command-flow.test.ts:1280 already feeds the flow an unprefixed error), or make statusLine skip the prefix when exit.error already starts with the label. Strip a trailing quote-plus-period before adding ".". Have gate.ts GATE_WORDS say "This computer" only locally, and let the PC substitute the label for remote refusals.

title: Stale refusal reasons say "Ember doesn't run commands" in a release whose headline feature is running commands
area: policy reasons shown in What Ember did and sent to the model
scenario: A task tries to type into or open a terminal app. The decision reason is "Ember doesn't run commands, so it never types into terminals" (also lines 2026 and 2028), and Settings › What Ember did shows it under "Refused". The model sees it too and may repeat "Ember doesn't run commands" to a user who has just turned Commands on.
evidence: Rendered real audit entries in the settings window: "Refused — Type into terminal in Terminal — Ember doesn't run commands, so it never types into terminals" (screenshot shots/activity.png). README and COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md describe commands that Ember does run in its own window. worker.ts:1100 and 1129 also say "Ember doesn't run terminals or shells."
fix: Reword to what is true: "Ember doesn't use terminal windows (it can run commands for you in its own command window when Commands is on)" for policy.ts:2025-2028, and drop "or shells" from worker.ts:1100 and 1129. Update the pinned tests.

title: "What Ember did" shows lowercase, third-person and model-facing fragments as the reason
scenario: The user opens What Ember did. Refusal and failure reasons are raw audit text: "this app is on the user's never-look list", "it didn't turn on", "no window known yet", "the control a click goes to can't be found" (all lowercase), and "The user moved the mouse or pressed a key, so Ember let go." (the user is called "the user"). The same list mixes capitalised and lowercase reasons, and the user is sometimes "the user" and sometimes "your" ("your organisation has turned off Ember acting in apps").
evidence: Rendered audit entries through the real settings window (shots/activity.png and the dumped text): lines "this app is on the user's never-look list", "first action in …", "your organisation has turned off Ember acting in apps", "The user moved the mouse or pressed a key, so Ember let go.", "it didn't turn on", "no window known yet". describeEntry passes e.reason straight through (copy.ts:209), and forUser strips only the listed tool names and codes. Sources: policy.ts:2018-2024, borrow.ts:29, worker.ts:1915 and the many lowercase reasons at policy.ts:1486-1962.
fix: Normalise in describeEntry: capitalise the first letter, end with a full stop, map "the user's" to "your" and "The user" to "You" (e.g. "This app is on your never-look list.", "You moved the mouse or pressed a key, so Ember let go."). Better, store a short user wording beside the model wording in the audit entry.

title: Setup-check rows for SSH and Mac remotes contain a double full stop, a repeated sentence, wrong version advice and literal backticks
scenario: setupChecks joins detail and fix as `${detail}. ${fix}` without checking punctuation. A Mac remote's row reads "…until \"Allow full disk access for remote users\" is on.. System Settings › General › Sharing › Remote Login › ⓘ › Allow full disk access for remote users." (double full stop, straight quotes where the consent card uses curly, and a fix that is a menu path, not a sentence). With no SSH client it reads "No SSH client found. Ember can't find SSH on this computer. Install OpenSSH (Linux: `sudo dnf install openssh-clients`; …)" (the same fact twice, with Markdown backticks shown literally). For a Windows client 8.1 to 8.3 it reads "Passwords can't be asked here: keys and the ssh-agent only. Ember needs OpenSSH 8.1 or newer: update…", which tells someone who has 8.1 that they need 8.1.
evidence: Ran setupChecks over sshClientRow, remoteTccRow, commandTerminalRow and powershellRow: the outputs are exactly the strings above (probe3). targets/doctor.ts:58 pairs the "Passwords can't be asked here" detail with OLD_SSH_WIN_FIX (line 42, "8.1 or newer"), while the real requirement for passwords is 8.4 (prompt/copy.ts, COMMANDS doc §4.6). doctor.ts:101-102 holds the straight-quote and period-plus-period text; line 40 holds the repeated sentence.
fix: Join with a check for a trailing full stop (`/[.!?]$/.test(detail) ? " " : ". "`), use curly quotes at doctor.ts:101, write the Mac fix as a sentence ("Turn it on in System Settings › General › Sharing › Remote Login › ⓘ."), shorten the no-client detail to "No SSH client found" plus the install sentence, strip or style backticks for the window, and give the 8.1-8.3 case its own fix ("Update the OpenSSH Client to 8.4 or newer to enter passwords in Ember").

title: Unrecognised Copilot errors are shown raw to the user, and common timeouts are not mapped
scenario: Any error that misses the regexes ("Request timed out after 60000ms", "Cannot read properties of undefined…", "Unexpected token < in JSON…", "Session not found: 7f3c") shows in the bubble, and is spoken aloud when speech is on, as "Copilot reported a problem: <raw text>". No next step is given and it reads as a code error.
evidence: Ran friendlyError on seven plausible raw messages (probe6): every one returns "Copilot reported a problem: <the raw text>". The network regex handles ETIMEDOUT and "fetch failed" but not "timed out" or "timeout".
fix: Add /timed? ?out|timeout|took too long/ → "Copilot took too long to answer. Try again in a moment." For the fallback, say "Copilot reported a problem. Try again; if it keeps happening, check Settings › Copilot." and keep the raw text only in the log.

title: The approval question names controls with accessibility jargon: "Click “Save” push button in Mousepad?"
scenario: The question seen most often in the product uses the raw AT-SPI role: "Click “Save” push button in Mousepad?", "Switch “Night Light” toggle button in Settings?", "Choose “Vegetarian” in “Meal” combo box…", "Click “Advanced” page tab…". The same Settings page's activity list uses friendly words ("a button", "a drop-down", "a tab"), so the vocabulary is inconsistent. Windows and macOS use the same names because roles.ts maps them to the AT-SPI vocabulary.
evidence: Probe of plainQuestion (probe2) printed exactly those four strings plus "Borrow your mouse to click “Send” push button in Mousepad?". app/sidecar-host/roles.ts:6 states buttons are "push button" on every OS.
fix: Map roles for the question the way home/copy.ts ROLE does: push button → button, toggle button → switch, combo box → drop-down, page tab → tab, check box → checkbox, radio button → option, e.g. "Click the “Save” button in Mousepad?" Share one table between the question and the activity list.

title: Linux and macOS users are told Ember works "in WSL"
scenario: WSL exists only on Windows, but the first-run "Before Ember starts" list ("Ember can work in WSL, on computers you reach over SSH…") and the Computers intro ("Ember can work on this computer, in WSL, and on computers you reach over SSH.") are static HTML and are never patched per OS. On RHEL and macOS the user reads about a feature that cannot exist on their machine.
evidence: Dumped the real settings window's text on Linux: "Ember can work on this computer, in WSL, and on computers you reach over SSH. Your voice and your GitHub sign-in always stay here." The first-run screenshot (shots/home-first.png) shows the onboarding bullet the same way. Both strings are fixed in index.html:36 and 127 (mirrored in computers-copy.ts:14 and 24) and homePatches never touches them.
fix: Add patches for #computers .intro and the onboarding li that drop "in WSL" unless platform.os is win32 (e.g. "Ember can work on this computer and on computers you reach over SSH."), and make FEATURE_TEXT skip wsl off Windows.

title: Internal terms leak into user-visible text: "job host", "The worker stopped…", "Node download", "Ember v1", "needs vision", "brain"
scenario: The command tab for a broken Windows or WSL install ends "Couldn't start: Ember's job host is missing, so it can't run commands safely here." (no next step; the other missing-part messages say "Reinstall Ember"). A task that dies without finishing shows "The worker stopped without a summary." on its card, in the notification and in the activity list. A failed SSH set-up says "Ember couldn't check the Node download for build-01…". The Wayland check on the settings page says "Ember v1 needs “GNOME on Xorg”" and the Platform row says "… is not supported in v1", although the app is 0.1.0. The model picker reads "Model for tasks (needs vision)".
evidence: statusLine probe: "Couldn't start: Ember's job host is missing, so it can't run commands safely here." Also local.ts:127 and 781, wsl/discover.ts:136 and wsl/runner.ts:691 ("job host"), worker.ts:1356 ("worker"), ssh-errors.ts:72 ("Node"), environment.ts:137 and 150 ("v1"), index.html:73 ("needs vision"), conductor.ts:517 ("Ember's brain is not connected yet.").
fix: "Part of Ember's install is missing, so it can't run commands safely here. Reinstall Ember."; "The task stopped without saying what happened."; "…couldn't check what it downloaded for build-01 (it doesn't match the expected file)"; "Ember needs “GNOME on Xorg”" and "… isn't supported"; "Model for tasks (must understand images)".

title: "Tell the Ember team." is a non-actionable fix for mixed display scaling
scenario: A Windows user with monitors at different scaling sees a warning that Ember "may click in the wrong place on some monitors. Tell the Ember team." There is no contact, issue link or workaround in the app or README, and the user cannot act on it.
evidence: Text at environment.ts:242 and doctor.ts:98 (fix: "Tell the Ember team."); README.md has no support or issue-tracker pointer.
fix: Give a workaround and a place: "Set all monitors to the same scale in Settings › System › Display, then restart Ember. If you can't, report it at <issues URL>." Add that URL to the README.

title: "What Ember did" omits commands, connections and WSL entries, though the docs say it lists every action
scenario: The user turns on Commands, a task runs `npm test` on build-01 and a dangerous command is allowed or refused. Settings › What Ember did shows only the task's "Task" and "Finished" lines. No line says which command ran, where, whether it asked or was allowed, or that an SSH connection was made. docs/DEVELOPING.md:140 says the list "lists every request, question, action and refusal", and the welcome page promises "a record of every action it took".
evidence: Called describeEntry with audit entries {event:"command",phase:"decision"|"started"|"ended"}, {event:"remote"} and {event:"wsl"}: all return null (probe4). The switch handles only task, decision, confirm, action and stop (copy.ts:196-218) and the default returns null; flow.ts:542, 804 and 827 audit with event "command".
fix: Add cases for command ("Ran" / "Asked you" / "Refused" with the target, shell and exit status, never the command text) and for remote or WSL connects and disconnects, or change the docs and the fold hint to say commands and connections are only in the audit folder.

title: CHANGELOG is still "Unreleased" and covers only SSH, WSL and commands, not the Windows and macOS port
scenario: The release candidate also contains the Windows and macOS ports (README documents installs for both), but the only release-notes section is "## Unreleased: commands, WSL and other computers". A "Changed" entry says Windows treated WSLg apps as Remote Desktop "before", though nothing earlier was ever released. Readers get no 0.1.0 heading or date.
evidence: grep "^## " CHANGELOG.md gives one heading, line 3. README.md and package.json say 0.1.0.
fix: Retitle to "0.1.0 (date)", open with the first-release summary (Linux, Windows and macOS, voice, characters), keep the new features as a section, and drop the "Changed" wording that refers to unreleased behaviour.

title: Quit question uses "it" for several tasks, and "tasks running" reads awkwardly
scenario: With three tasks under way, Quit Ember asks "Ember is still working on 3 tasks." with the detail "Quitting stops it where it is." (should be "them"). The mixed branch computes the plural correctly. Elsewhere "once the tasks running are done" (home/copy.ts:67, home/main.ts:466 button "Reconnect now (stops the tasks running)", host.ts messages) is clumsy.
evidence: quitQuestion(3,{commands:0,connections:0}) returns {"message":"Ember is still working on 3 tasks.","detail":"Quitting stops it where it is."}; the mixed case returns "stops them where they are".
fix: Reuse the `one` logic for the tasks-only branch: tasks === 1 ? "stops it where it is" : "stops them where they are". Say "tasks that are running" in the tagline, button and host messages.

title: Time units: "15 s" breaks across lines, and "s" mixes with "seconds"
scenario: The stalled-connection bubble says "Its running commands stop in 15 s unless the link comes back." and in a 360 px card the line breaks between the number and its unit ("15" / "s unless…"). The announcement bubble says "in 4 seconds", the command window "Starts in 4 s.", and the status lines "3.2 s" and "2 min 5 s". "link" is jargon for the connection.
evidence: Rendered the real handle card with that text (shots/handle-all.png, first panel): "Its running commands stop in 15 / s unless the link comes back." Sources: target-copy.ts:61, runtime.ts:646, command/copy.ts:35-43, 133 and 142.
fix: Use "seconds" in sentences ("…stop in 15 seconds unless it answers again") and a no-break space (U+00A0) before the abbreviation in status lines ("3.2 s").

title: One thing, several names: the organisation's model service, plus "machine" and "PC" among "computer"
scenario: The organisation's own model endpoint is "model service" in Settings and the Setup check label, "AI endpoint" or "AI service" in bubble errors, "your organisation's endpoint" in the doctor detail and "AI service" in the README. Elsewhere the product says "this computer", but the settings tagline says "this machine" (and "a couple of things" even when one thing fails), and two consent lines say "another PC".
evidence: presenter.ts:38, 40, 42, 47, 53 and 55; doctor.ts:165; home/main.ts:315 and 323; README.md:81; home/copy.ts:64; prompt/copy.ts:192 and remote-policy.ts:125 ("WSL on another PC"). The Setup check summary also says "to look at" while the CLI says "worth a look".
fix: Pick "model service" everywhere. Change the tagline to "Ember needs N thing(s) fixed before it can work on this computer." and use "computer" in the two WSL lines.

title: The same check has different names in the settings window and in `ember doctor`
scenario: On Linux the settings window calls the accessibility row "Screen reading" while `ember doctor` calls it "Reading apps" (docs/DEVELOPING.md refers to "Screen reading"). On macOS the window says "Reading and using apps", "Applications folder" and "Microphone", while the CLI says "Accessibility", "Location" and "Microphone access", and README calls the permission "Accessibility". The tool is "check-up" in the CLI heading, "Setup check" in the window and "doctor" in the command.
evidence: Ran `electron . --doctor`: "warn  Reading apps  Python accessibility bindings are missing."; the settings window dump: "Screen reading — Python accessibility bindings are missing: sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi". Sources: doctor.ts:141, environment.ts:174-178, 270-271, 291, darwin/system/doctor.ts:20-45.
fix: Use one label per check in both surfaces (e.g. "Reading apps") and one name for the tool ("setup check") in the README, window and CLI heading.

title: macOS names Command two ways, and the Intel row doesn't say "best effort"
scenario: Shortcut chips say "Control+Shift+Command+Space", but key presses in What Ember did read "Cmd+S" (labels: cmd → "Cmd") and the file-dialog hint says "Cmd+Shift+G". The README says Intel Macs are best effort and the Windows Arm row says "(best effort)", but the macOS Platform row for Intel just reads "macOS on Intel".
evidence: shortcuts.ts:41 (label "Command") versus KEYS.darwin.labels cmd: "Cmd" (line 99) and words.ts:60; environment.ts:262 versus :208.
fix: Label the key "Command" (or use ⌘) everywhere users read it, and make the Intel row "macOS on Intel (best effort)".

title: The command card mixes "I" and "Ember"
scenario: The command window card is written in the third person ("Ember wants to run this command", "Ember can't tell exactly what this does.", "You asked Ember to check every command with you."), but two lines switch to first person: "I'm checking each step: a step came up that you didn't ask for." and "I'm checking each step: an earlier command printed text that looked like instructions." The bubbles are first person by design; the card is not.
evidence: decide.ts:26, flow.ts:111 and 210. target-copy.ts's header says first person is for bubbles.
fix: "Ember is checking each step: a step came up that you didn't ask for." (and likewise for the output line). Update the pinned strings.

title: macOS app menu has no "About Ember" item
scenario: The Ember app menu starts at "Settings…" and has Hide and Quit, but no About item, so a Mac user cannot see the version from the menu (it is only in Settings › About this build, which only has a version line).
evidence: main.ts:1180-1189 builds the template with Settings…, hide roles and Quit Ember.
fix: Add {role: "about"} first, with app.setAboutPanelOptions for the name, version and licence.

title: docs/DESIGN.md says a character can be chosen in the handle menu; there is no such item
scenario: "All four ship in the app and are chosen in setup, settings, the handle menu, or by voice." The handle menu has Ask Ember…, Stop everything, Work on, Mute, Read the last answer, Settings…, Stay put or Follow my cursor, Hide or Show Ember and Quit Ember, and no character picker.
evidence: app/main/main.ts:529-548 (the whole menu template); no character or submenu entries, and grep for the character names in main.ts finds none in the menu.
fix: Drop "the handle menu" from DESIGN.md, or add a character submenu.

title: Notification body is cut at 240 characters with no ellipsis; the Ask placeholder example is Linux-specific
scenario: A long question or task summary appears in a notification cut mid-word (body.slice(0, 240)). The Ask box placeholder suggests “turn on Night Light” on every OS, but macOS calls it Night Shift and Windows "Night light".
evidence: main.ts:698 (slice with no marker); ask/index.html:16 placeholder, which is static and not patched per OS.
fix: Cut at a word boundary and add "…"; patch the example per OS (e.g. “turn on dark mode”, which works on all three).

title: Prompt window (SSH password, passphrase, host key, consent card) is never given the keyboard on macOS and Windows
scenario: macOS: the user asks by the hotkey or ask box (a non-activating panel, so their own app stays active) "on build-01 run df". Ember needs the SSH password, so reveal() runs `w.show(); w.moveTop(); w.focus()` on the prompt window. Ember is not the active app, so the card appears on top without becoming the key window. The user types the password and it goes into whatever app is frontmost (Slack, Mail), in plain text. The card also lacks `acceptFirstMouse`, so the first click on Allow or Connect only activates Ember and is swallowed. Windows: the same when the task was started by voice or an earlier hotkey and Ember has not received input recently, because SetForegroundWindow is refused by the foreground lock and the window only flashes. The prompt page only calls `field.focus()` in the DOM and never checks that the OS window has the keyboard.
evidence: Read end to end: createPromptWindowController takes only {create, ipc, log, os}; `os` is never used for focus, and reveal() just calls show/moveTop/focus. Every other Ember window that takes the keyboard uses the platform hooks: bringToFront (main.ts:274-283) calls sys.lifecycle.focusOwnApp() and inputRef.activate(); the quit question (main.ts:472) and the startup error box call focusOwnApp(); the ask box's takeFocus (main.ts:716-717) does the same. platform/types.ts:469-478 states the rule: "Before one of Ember's own normal windows takes the keyboard ... focusOwnApp", and for win32 "activateOwnWithInput ... (foreground rules)". main.ts comments also say a hotkey does not activate Ember on macOS. createPromptWindow (windows.ts:72-96) is an ordinary window, not a panel, and has no acceptFirstMouse. Could not run on a real Mac or PC; the conclusion follows from Ember's own documented platform rules and Electron's documented focus() behaviour.
fix: Give createPromptWindowController an `activate(win)` callback that main wires exactly like bringToFront: sys.lifecycle.focusOwnApp(), then inputRef.activate(ownId(win)) and focusInput where activateOwnWithInput is true. After showing, check win.isFocused() and, when it is not, say so on the card and in a notification so nobody types a secret blind. Add `acceptFirstMouse: true` to the macOS prompt window.

title: macOS: any app's Secure Keyboard Entry is reported as "a system dialog (such as a password prompt) is open"; the accurate reason can never be shown
scenario: Terminal's Secure Keyboard Entry (often enforced on CIS-hardened Macs), a password field left focused, or an app that crashed with secure input on, makes IsSecureEventInputEnabled() true. Ember then refuses every mouse and keyboard action and every screenshot, and the user and model are told "A system dialog (such as a password prompt) is open on the user's screen ... wait" or "(No screenshot: a system dialog is open, so Ember looks away)". No dialog exists, and waiting never helps. The settings setup check has no Secure input row (inspectMac in environment.ts); only `--doctor` names the holder.
evidence: darwin/windows.ts:218-226 makes systemDialogOpen() return true whenever secure().on !== false. withCursor (worker.ts:3095-3099) and perceive (perception/index.ts:415) call that before borrow.begin(), so CursorBorrow's x.blockedReason() (borrow.ts:334), which returns secureInputReason(app) ("Secure keyboard entry is on in Terminal ... until it's off"), is never reached. I bundled darwin/windows.ts with a fake desktop where only secure input is on (secureInput()=true, holder pid 777 = Terminal, no security windows): systemDialogOpen() returned true and secureInput() returned {on:true,pid:777,app:"Terminal"}.
fix: Make the platform answer with a reason, not a bare boolean: systemDialogOpen(): null | string, or add `systemDialogReason()`. Use "Secure keyboard entry is on in <app>" in the worker denial and the no-screenshot note. Alternatively check input.blockedReason() before the generic dialog gate. Add a Secure input row to inspectMac so the settings setup check shows it too.

title: macOS without Screen Recording (never granted, or revoked while running): screenshots fail with "the window is off screen"
scenario: A user who skips or later revokes Screen Recording (a common first-run choice, and the setup row is only a warning) asks Ember something that needs a picture. captureRect() returns null at once (darwin/capture.ts:56, `if (!allowed) return null`) and perceive() answers "(No screenshot: the window is off screen, or the screen couldn't be captured safely.)". The model then tells the user the window is off screen. Only the settings window's Screen Recording row, or `--doctor`, mentions the permission, so a user who never opens them is never told.
evidence: Read the path: darwin/windows.ts capture() -> captureRect() returns null without the permission -> captureRect in perception/capture.ts returns null -> perception/index.ts:507 uses the generic note. grep for "Screen Recording" outside platform/darwin, environment.ts and the vocabulary returns nothing in perception or agent code, and PlatformWords has no field for this reason.
fix: Add a PlatformWords field (for example noScreenshot) or let the window system's capture report why. On macOS the note should say "Ember doesn't have the Screen Recording permission (System Settings > Privacy & Security)" and the conductor could mention it once.

title: Command and prompt windows are excluded from capture, so remote-access software and screen magnifiers that capture the desktop cannot show them
scenario: createCommandWindow (line 67) and createPromptWindow (line 93) call setContentProtection(true) on Windows and macOS, so these windows are excluded from capture. Electron 44's own docs say a Remote Desktop client still shows such a window, but "remote access software that works by capturing the desktop cannot". Someone using Ember over TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Quick Assist or VNC, or on macOS through Screen Sharing, or with a capture-based magnifier, sees nothing where the command card or the SSH password/consent card should be. That is where commands are approved and secrets typed. The card still reports "whole command in view" to main, because the page's visibility is true locally. The relevant documented limits (L11) rely on this protection and do not mention the downside.
evidence: node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:6140-6159 documents the behaviour and the Chromium feature `AllowWindowCaptureExclusionInRemoteSessions` that turns it off. Perception already blacks out Ember's own windows by their stack frames (ownWindows/coveringRects), so for Ember's own screenshots the protection is belt and braces. The platform knows the session kind (win32 environment sessionKind: console/rdp/service) but nothing uses it here. Not verified against a real remote tool.
fix: Decide deliberately: either keep protection and document in COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md that these windows cannot be seen through screen-capture remote tools, or turn the Chromium feature off (or skip setContentProtection) when SM_REMOTESESSION or a remote session is detected. Optionally show a one-line hint in the bubble when the card cannot be seen.

title: macOS: Apple apps on non-English systems are not found by localized name, and a window opened by open_app is not recognised
scenario: On a German or French Mac the window owner name of Apple's own apps is localized ("Rechner", "Systemeinstellungen"). The catalogue only knows the bundle file name ("Calculator", "System Settings"), CFBundleName, the executable and the bundle id, and never reads the localized InfoPlist.strings. open_app("Rechner") finds nothing. open_app("Calculator") launches the app, but worker.ts:1141 compares AxWindow.app against `programs`, so the new window never matches. After 10 s the tool answers "Started Calculator, but its window hasn't appeared yet. Use list_windows and switch_window", and the task has to recover by hand.
evidence: Read: bundleApp() builds `name = path.basename(bundle)` (line 94) and `programs: uniqueLower([name, bundleName, exe, bundle id])` (line 107), using only Info.plist keys, with no lproj lookup. The types.ts contract and the comment in bundleApp say the sidecar's `app` and the window owner are the localized name. worker.ts:1139-1146 matches new windows by programs or by `x.name.includes(app.name)`. Could not run on a localized Mac.
fix: When listing a bundle, also read Contents/Resources/<preferred lproj>.lproj/InfoPlist.strings (CFBundleDisplayName, CFBundleName) with the existing plist reader, and add those names to `keywords` and `programs`.

title: Wayland session is explained but never refused: Ember starts anyway through XWayland and greets as if it works
scenario: RHEL 8's default login is GNOME on Wayland. The launcher always forces --ozone-platform=x11 (packaging/ember:25), so Ember runs against XWayland. The only effect of environment.ts:147-151 failing the "session" check is a row in the settings window and in `ember doctor`; start-up just logs app.ready with failing:["session"]. Ember then shows its greeting ("I'll stay by your cursor ..."), registers shortcuts, and reads and captures through XWayland (root pointer, XTest and XGetImage only see X11 clients). With "Start Ember when I log in" turned on from an earlier Xorg session, a Wayland login gives no explanation at all, because settings is not opened.
evidence: Ran `electron . --doctor --ozone-platform=x11` under Xvfb with XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland and WAYLAND_DISPLAY set: the Desktop session row FAILs with the fix text, and the process exits 1. Ran the app itself with --show-settings in the same environment and took a screenshot: it starts normally, logs the failing checks and shows "needs a couple of things fixed", but only below the consent card. Nothing at start-up refuses or interrupts, and nothing in greet() looks at env.checks.
fix: When the session check fails, have greet() say so ("This is a Wayland session ...: log out and choose GNOME on Xorg") and stay out of tier-3 and screenshot work, or exit with startupFailed()'s dialog when the session type is wayland and the check fails. At minimum open settings on every start while a check is failing, even with --autostart.

title: macOS: after every update the ad-hoc-signed Ember asks for the login keychain password, can freeze Ember while it waits, and Deny silently signs the user out; README's update steps do not mention it
scenario: The stored GitHub token is encrypted with Electron's safeStorage, whose key lives in the login Keychain under an access list tied to the app's code identity. Ember is signed ad hoc, which the README says is a new identity on every build. After the user drags a new Ember.app over the old one, the first start (or the first login start) makes macOS show "Ember wants to use your confidential information stored in ... Safe Storage". decryptString() is synchronous on the main process, so the overlay, hotkeys and Stop are unresponsive until the user answers. Choosing Deny or Cancel makes decryptString throw, load() catches it and returns null, and Ember silently shows "not connected". The README update section lists only the TCC permissions (Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring).
evidence: auth.ts:37-45: `load()` wraps `this.box.decryptString(raw)` in try/catch and returns null. startBrain calls resolveToken(tokens, ...) on the main thread (main.ts around line 1540). docs/DEVELOPING.md:894 confirms the token is encrypted with a key in the login Keychain. PLAN.md and README say an ad-hoc signature is a new identity to macOS on each build. The prompt itself is standard behaviour for ad-hoc-signed Electron apps that use safeStorage; I could not run a Mac.
fix: Document the keychain prompt next to the TCC re-grant steps in README ("choose Always Allow"). Read the token off the critical path (after the window and overlay are up, with a short "waiting for the keychain" status) and, when decryption throws, say "macOS didn't let Ember read its saved sign-in; sign in again" instead of the generic not-connected state.

title: Windows Contrast themes (forced-colors) make switches, the consent checkbox, slider, character selection, button edges and all state symbols invisible
area: Accessibility settings: forced-colors / high contrast (all windows)
platforms: windows (Contrast themes in Win10/11; Chromium forced-colors on any OS)
scenario: A low-vision user on Windows with a Contrast theme (Aquatic, Desert, High Contrast Black or White) installs Ember. The first-run screen shows 'I've read how Ember works and I agree' with no visible checkbox and a bare 'Start Ember' word with no button shape, so the consent gate cannot be seen. After setup, every switch in Settings, the Size slider, the selected-character ring and tick, 'Sign out', 'Add', the select boxes and the text fields have no outline or fill. In the command window 'Allow' and 'Not now' are floating words, the selected tab is indistinguishable, and the done, failed and stopped symbols are gone. The overlay task cards lose their working, failed and needs-you symbols, and the handle loses its mic dot, so state is no longer conveyed at all. Everything is built from background-colour, mask and box-shadow, and forced-colors drops all three. No CSS or JS in the app mentions forced-colors, and docs/DESIGN.md says Increase Contrast reaches every surface; on Windows that mechanism is forced-colors, not prefers-contrast.
evidence: Emulated forced-colors:active with prefers-contrast:more (dark and light) in Chromium 141 and rendered every page. Computed styles in that mode: #login and #login::before background rgb(255,255,255) (Canvas), box-shadow none, border 0; .btn.quiet, select, text input, .card[aria-checked=true] and .group box-shadow none; .card::after (the tick mask) and .dot background Canvas. grep for 'forced-colors|forcedColors|HighContrast' across app/, docs/ and test/ finds nothing relevant. Screenshots: shots/home-forced-dark.png, shots/home-first-forced-light.png (the checkbox and Start button are missing), shots/overlay-forced-light.png, shots/overlay-forced-dark.png, shots/content-forced-combo.png (command window and prompt cards). Harness: forced-home.mjs, forced-first.mjs, shot-forced-float.mjs, shot-content.mjs, forced-css.mjs.
fix: Add one @media (forced-colors: active) block to ember.css (it reaches every page) and mirror it in the bubble CSS. Give controls real borders in system colours: .btn, .start, .card, select, input, .tab, .eb-actions button, .task-actions button and the overlay and handle buttons get border:1px solid ButtonText. For the switch use border:2px solid ButtonText, ::before background ButtonText, and :checked background Highlight with ::before HighlightText. For the checkbox use a 1px ButtonText border and a CanvasText tick when checked. For the slider use a ButtonText track and thumb. For .card[aria-checked=true] use outline:3px solid Highlight. For every mask symbol (.task::before, .tab::before, .pending-line::before, .card::after, .dot, .mic, .eb-dot, the sidebar tiles and the terms icons) set forced-color-adjust:none and background:CanvasText (or Highlight). Keep the glass as Canvas with a ButtonText border. Re-run the forced-colors emulation to confirm.

title: Default Electron application menu is left on Windows and Linux: Ctrl+Q quits Ember with no 'still working' question, Ctrl+Shift+I opens DevTools in every window, Alt reveals File/Edit/View/Window
area: Window chrome / keyboard shortcuts (settings, command, prompt, Ask windows)
platforms: linux (verified with real key events), windows (same Electron default menu)
scenario: main.ts calls Menu.setApplicationMenu only when sys.lifecycle.appMenu is true (macOS). On Windows and Linux Electron keeps its default menu: File > Quit (Ctrl+Q), Edit, View > Reload (Ctrl+R) / Force Reload / Toggle Developer Tools (Ctrl+Shift+I) / Zoom / Toggle Full Screen (F11), Window > Close (Ctrl+W). A user typing in Settings, the Ask box or a prompt who presses Ctrl+Q (or Alt+F then Q) quits Ember instantly while a task is running or SSH hosts are connected. quitEmber's 'Ember is still working on a task' question (the quit confirmation at main.ts:466) is bypassed, and will-quit stops the agent. Ctrl+Shift+I opens a DevTools window on the password and host-key prompt window and on the command window. Ctrl+W in the Ask box destroys it. Pressing Alt in Settings, the command window or the fixed 440x300 prompt window shows an Electron menu bar (autoHideMenuBar) and shrinks the content.
evidence: Real Electron 44 under Xvfb: Menu.getApplicationMenu() lists File:Quit[CommandOrControl+Q], Edit, View:Reload|Force Reload|Toggle Developer Tools[Ctrl+Shift+I]|Zoom|Toggle Full Screen[F11], Window:Close[CommandOrControl+W]. XTest key events sent to the focused settings window (scratch xkey.py + ctrlq2.mjs): Ctrl+Shift+I gave isDevToolsOpened=true for the home window, and Ctrl+Q ended the process ('exited after Ctrl+Q: true'). askkeys.mjs: Ctrl+W in the focused Ask window removed it from BrowserWindow.getAllWindows(). windows.ts sets autoHideMenuBar:true on home, command and prompt.
fix: On non-macOS call Menu.setApplicationMenu(null), or a minimal menu that keeps only Edit and zoom (zoom is a useful accessibility feature the default menu accidentally provides) and has no Quit, Reload, DevTools, Close or fullscreen. Do it before app ready and in the same place as the macOS menu. If a Quit shortcut is wanted, route it through quitEmber() so the question is asked.
