title: Increase Contrast: the keyboard focus ring is the same colour as accent-filled controls, so focus on primary buttons, checked switches and the selected character card is not visible as a ring
area: Accessibility settings: Increase Contrast and focus visibility
platforms: all (macOS Increase Contrast, GNOME high contrast, Windows when forced-colors is off)
scenario: With the OS asking for more contrast, --focus-ring becomes '0 0 0 3px var(--accent)' and --accent is #ffa056. Every prominent control is also filled with var(--accent): .btn, .start, the command card's Allow, the prompt's 'Install and connect', the bubble and handle primary buttons, checked switches and checkboxes, and the selected card's inner ring. Tabbing onto one only makes it look 3 px bigger. There is no separate ring, so a keyboard user cannot tell which of 'Not now' and 'Install and connect' (or 'Allow') is focused before pressing Enter. In normal mode the ring is 75% orange, a faint dark band at about 1.6:1 against the button.
evidence: Pixel scan across the left edge of a keyboard-focused primary button at 2x (prompt consent card): default mode ring (195,113,40) then button (255,146,48); Increase Contrast mode (255,160,86) all the way from the ring into the button, with no edge. Screenshot: shots/focus-primary-combo.png (top: default, bottom: Increase Contrast). The home Tab walk (walk-home.mjs) shows large pixel diffs on every stop, but only because the ring grows the shape.
fix: Make the ring two-tone so it separates from accent fills, for example --focus-ring: 0 0 0 2px var(--surface-0), 0 0 0 5px var(--label) in prefers-contrast:more (and a surface-coloured 2 px gap under the accent ring in normal mode for filled controls). Apply it to the bubble's and handle's own focus rules, which reuse the token.

title: Native window chrome follows the OS theme while every Ember window is dark-only (nativeTheme.themeSource is never set)
area: Window backgrounds / native chrome per OS
scenario: The settings, command and prompt windows paint #121011 (a dark surface). There is no light appearance anywhere in the CSS: no prefers-color-scheme rule, and ember.css sets color-scheme:dark. A user in Windows or macOS light mode gets a bright title bar, light native menus, and light native dialogs (the quit question, window.confirm for 'Forget host') around a near-black window. The result looks like two apps. The same applies to the handle's native right-click menu.
evidence: Real Electron: nativeTheme.themeSource === 'system' and shouldUseDarkColors === false in the running app; grep for nativeTheme/themeSource in app/ finds only a gsettings read in hands/system.ts. DESIGN.md confirms the design is intentionally dark-only.
fix: Set nativeTheme.themeSource = 'dark' at startup (before windows are created). That gives dark title bars on Windows 11 and macOS and dark native menus and dialogs, and it matches what the pages already assume. If a light appearance is ever wanted, that is a separate design task.

title: Handle's microphone badge is colour-only (orange / grey / red 8 px dot) and sits on Cinder's orange mitten
scenario: The only on-screen sign that Ember's microphone is open, muted or broken is an 8 px dot at the lower right of the face: accent orange while listening or waiting, grey when muted, red on error. With the default Cinder character that orange dot lands on Cinder's right mitten and reads as a second hand. With the other three characters it is a plain orange dot with no mic shape. For a colour-blind user, orange and red are close and there is no symbol or word. The tooltip only helps on hover, and the handle window is focusable:false, so assistive tech never reads it. This breaks the design's own 'never colour alone' rule for the one privacy-relevant indicator.
evidence: Rendered the handle at 3x for all four characters, waiting vs muted: shots/mic-chars.png (the Cinder row shows a mitten and a dot side by side). Code: handle/main.ts sets mic.title only; .mic is an <i aria-hidden> with background colours (handle/styles.css:99-105).
fix: Draw a small mic glyph (a slashed mic when muted, an exclamation when it has a problem) in a dark glass disc, or put the indicator beside the text line instead of on the face. Keep the accent for 'listening'. Add the state word to the line while the mic is in an error state, and expose it in the live region for the no-compositor card.

title: App icon is unreadable at 16 and 24 px, and Ember's Linux windows set no icon at all
platforms: windows (taskbar, Explorer lists), linux (AppImage, unpackaged), macOS (tiny Dock/menu sizes)
scenario: The same SVG (a 104 px tile on a 128 px canvas) is used for the ICO (sizes 16 to 256), the iconset and the Linux PNG. The visible tile covers 81% of the canvas, so at 16 px it is a 13 px graphite square with Cinder reduced to a brown smudge and two orange dots, and the dark tile nearly disappears on a dark taskbar. On Linux the BrowserWindows are created without an icon option, so _NET_WM_ICON is empty and GNOME shows an icon only when the .desktop entry matches (RPM). Running the AppImage without desktop integration, or from a build tree, gives the generic gear in Alt-Tab and the dash.
evidence: Rendered with sharp at 16/24/32/48/64/256 on white, #202020 and Windows-blue backgrounds: shots/icon-sheet.png; opaque bounding box at 256 px is 24..231 (81% of the canvas). X11 properties read from the running app (xprops.py): windows 'ember' and 'Ember' have WM_CLASS ember/ember and _NET_WM_ICON longs=0. grep for 'icon:' / nativeImage / setIcon in app/main finds none; icons only reach the exe and bundle (scripts/package/icon.mjs, stage.mjs).
fix: Export dedicated 16 and 24 px (and optionally 32) artwork for the ICO and iconset: fill the canvas, no baked shadow, a simplified Cinder (eyes and the glow) and a lighter rim so it holds on dark taskbars. On Linux pass icon: path to the packaged PNG in createHomeWindow, createCommandWindow and createPromptWindow (and the other BrowserWindows) so AppImage and dev runs show it.

title: Ember's Calm setting does not reach the Ask, command, prompt and desk windows
scenario: Calm mode is meant to mean 'nothing springs or slides', and html.calm is the only hook that stops the shared controls. Only home, handle and overlay set it (handle/main.ts:34, overlay/main.ts:81, home/main.ts:47). The command, prompt, Ask and desk pages never receive the setting (their preloads expose nothing about settings). With Calm on and the OS preference off, the .btn press spring (transform 220ms var(--spring-snappy)), the hover filter fades and the desk's button transitions still run in those windows. The effect is small, but the setting's promise is not kept.
evidence: grep -rn calm over app/renderer shows toggles only in handle, overlay and home. Animation counts via document.getAnimations() with Calm only: overlay 0, handle 0, home 0, so the three wired windows behave (motion.mjs). The other four windows have no calm hook and rely on prefers-reduced-motion alone; ember.css:187 and :194 give .btn its transform and transition.
fix: Broadcast the settings' reduceMotion to every page (main already sends settings to the overlay and handle) and toggle html.calm there, or have main insert the CSS with webContents.insertCSS for the four pages when the setting is on.

title: First launch can show the full settings layout (sidebar, 'Checking…') before the first-run consent screen replaces it
platforms: all (worse where target checks are slow, e.g. WSL or SSH rows on Windows)
scenario: The settings window is shown on ready-to-show, which fires after first paint, but the first-run state (body.first-run, the Welcome card, no sidebar) is applied only when getStatus resolves. getStatus awaits the targets runtime's rows for up to 3000 ms (main.ts:359-363, waitMs:3000). Until then a brand-new user sees the post-setup page, with the sidebar, Copilot 'Checking…', Conversation, Voice and Privacy sections and the first-run tagline, which then collapses into the consent screen. A stale 'body.loading' removal remains in the code (main.ts:136 and 125), but nothing in the CSS or HTML defines that gate any more.
evidence: Stubbed getStatus with a 1.5 s delay: shots/home-before-status.png shows the sidebar layout with 'Checking…' while the tagline already reads the first-run text. In real Electron, reloading the settings window and recording when body.first-run was applied: 118 ms in one run but about 1540 ms in two of three runs after cold-ish restarts (flash-real.mjs). A cold launch under Xvfb applied it within 500 ms, so the flash length depends on how long the status takes.
fix: Hide the body (visibility:hidden or opacity:0) until the first status has been applied, with the existing 1.5 s timer as the cap, which is what the removed body.loading gate did. Or return the settings first and stream the slow target rows in afterwards.

title: Settings sidebar is cut off at the window's minimum height with no visible scrollbar
scenario: The sidebar is fixed, overflow:auto and scrollbar-width:none (the horizontal pill row's setting is inherited by the vertical sidebar too). With Computers and Commands shown it has 11 links and needs 438 px, but the window may be as short as 420 px (windows.ts minHeight:420). 'About' (and part of 'Setup') sit past the bottom and the only way to reach them is the mouse wheel or Tab, with nothing hinting that the list scrolls.
evidence: Rendered home at 760x420 with the targets runtime present: #jump scrollHeight 438 vs clientHeight 420, overflowY auto, scrollbar-width none (sidebar.mjs, shots/home-minheight.png).
fix: Raise the home window's minHeight to at least 480, or remove scrollbar-width:none from the wide-sidebar rule so the slim ember.css scrollbar shows (keep it only for the narrow horizontal row).

title: Ember's own spoken announcement says “Say 'Ember, stop' to cancel.” and its microphone hearing it fires the kill switch (Windows, macOS, Linux without parec)
platforms: windows, macos (and linux when parec/pulseaudio-utils is missing)
scenario: A user on a Windows or macOS laptop, with “Speak replies” on (or Narrator/VoiceOver running, which also turns speaking on), says “Hey Ember, delete the build folder”. That is a D4.4 announced command: the bubble shows “It starts in 4 seconds”, and Ember speaks the announcement plus “Say 'Ember, stop' to cancel.” through the laptop speakers. The microphone hears Ember's own voice say “Ember, stop”. Windows and macOS have no speaker-output stream (speakerMonitor:false), so nothing rejects it, and the kill phrase deliberately works while Ember speaks. The engine emits stop, and main runs stopEverything('voice'). That cancels the command, or interrupts it half-run if the 4 s countdown has already elapsed (the phrase comes at the end of a 4-6 s sentence). It also aborts every other running task and command on every target. Headphones hide the problem; speakers do not.
evidence: host.ts:1226 appends `Say 'Ember, stop' to cancel.` to every announcement, and main.ts:1545 speaks it via voice.speak(spokenText(text)). platform/win32/system/index.ts:77 and platform/darwin/system/index.ts:111 set speakerMonitor:false. engine.ts:583 and 748 let ember_stop through while Ember speaks, rejecting only when the speaker stream said it. I ran the real models (scratch script self-stop.cjs): with selfSpeaking(true), a TTS 'Ember, stop' on the mic and no speaker stream gives `stop` at gain 0.1, 0.3 and 1.0 (about -20 dB is enough); with the speaker stream present it gives `rejected:speakers`. In the real app (dev build, fake mic playing the clip while the voice process was told Ember is speaking), the log shows `voice.event stop` and `killswitch.pulled {source:'voice'}`. docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:161 documents the spoken sentence but says nothing about this side effect, and it is not among L1-L26.
fix: Never speak the kill phrase where Ember cannot tell its own voice from the user's. In host.ts, use the platform's stop chord words instead of the phrase (sc.stop.say, e.g. “Press Windows key, Alt, X to cancel”), or only append the phrase when speaker rejection is actually running (voice 'monitor' on). More generally, in the engine, while Ember speaks and no speaker stream is arriving (!hearsSpeakers), require ember_stop to stand well above Ember's own level, or accept only the chord. Also strip the wake and stop phrases from spokenText for platforms without a monitor.

title: A spoken request from any audio source counts as “the user's own words” for announced dangerous commands, and Windows/macOS have no speaker rejection
scenario: A call participant, a video or podcast, or a web page playing audio says “Hey Ember, delete the build folder” (or “push my branch to GitHub”) through the user's speakers. On Windows and macOS nothing tells that audio from the user, because speaker-output rejection exists only on Linux with parec. The transcript goes through askEmber() exactly like typed text, and D4.4 treats “only what you typed or said” as the user's own words, so a dangerous command it names exactly takes the announce path: run after a 4 s countdown unless Stop is pressed. A user who is away from the screen, or not looking, sees nothing until it has run.
evidence: Code reading, not an end-to-end run (no LLM or real audio here). main.ts:747 askEmber(text) and host.ts userWordsOf() carry no voice-origin flag, so voice and typed requests are indistinguishable downstream. docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §2.5: “Only what you typed or said counts”. voice/engine.ts only rejects audio when a speaker stream exists (Linux/parec). L1-L26 do not list this, and the voice docs only say speaker rejection 'needs parec'.
fix: Tag requests that came from voice and, when speaker rejection is not active (Windows, macOS, Linux without parec), do not let voice-origin words satisfy D4.4's “you asked for exactly that”: dangerous commands then ask with the card (the same rule as a task with no user words). Or require a typed confirmation. At minimum, document it as an accepted limitation.

title: VoiceEngine.bargeIn transcribes an empty pre-roll ring; sherpa throws a bare WASM number out of feed() and the voice process dies
platforms: linux (needs the parec speaker stream, so Linux with parec only)
scenario: A wake window is open (the user said “Hey Ember” and Ember waits for the request; replayPreRoll has emptied the ring, and listening mode does not refill it). Ember then starts to speak, for example a finished task is announced. The user says “Hey Ember” again over it, and the speaker stream is live but did not say it. bargeIn() calls backend.transcribe(ring.read()) on 0 samples. sherpa's Moonshine throws a bare number; nothing catches it, so the exception escapes engine.feed() in process.ts's port handler. The utility process exits with code 1, and main shows “The voice process stopped. Trying again in 1 s…”. The user is deaf for the 3-6 s model reload and loses the request in progress; repeats climb the 1/5/30 s backoff.
evidence: Deterministic repro with the real models (scratch repro-bargein.cjs): wake clip, wait for the check, selfSpeaking(true), feed the wake clip with the monitor stream live: 'EXCEPTION out of engine.feed(): number 92691224'. Stack: bargeIn engine.ts:769, decideStop:726, feed:599. A 15-minute randomized soak with real models threw the same number within about 60 s on 3 of 3 seeds, always from transcribe() on a zero-length array. A direct fuzz shows backend.transcribe throws a number for fewer than about 1000 samples (800 samples throws, 1600 does not). In an Electron utilityProcess, a throw in a MessagePort handler exits the process with code 1 (verified). Nothing else threw in four 20-minute soaks once short transcribes were guarded.
fix: In sherpa.ts transcribe(): return '' (or zero-pad to 0.1 s) when samples.length < 1600, and wrap the recognizer calls in try/catch so a WASM exception can never kill the process. Also try/catch around engine.feed()/feedMonitor() in process.ts and report a 'voice.engine_error' instead of dying. In bargeIn(), skip the transcript when the ring is shorter than about 0.1 s.

title: A damaged speech-model folder fails forever with the message “37825408”, and the only remedy (the download button) is hidden
scenario: An antivirus quarantines or truncates a model file, a disk error or manual cleanup removes one, or a package is damaged, while the `.ok` marker stays. Turning on “Hey Ember” then shows “Not working: 37825408” (a WASM exception pointer). There is no retry and no explanation. Settings hides the “Download speech models” button because modelsReady() only checks the marker and the folder name, so the user cannot repair it without deleting the models folder by hand.
evidence: Reproduced in the real app: truncate encode.int8.onnx in userData/models/sherpa-onnx-moonshine-tiny-en-int8 to 1000 bytes. Log: `voice.error {message:'37819256'}`; state 'error'; voice.modelsReady === true. Plain Node reproduces it too: sherpaBackend throws the number 37825408. process.ts:57 uses `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`, and sherpa-onnx's WASM exports no exception-message helper. models.ts:70 verified() trusts the marker; home/main.ts:800 hides the button when modelsReady. The unit test 'a model that won't load is an error to show' assumes a readable message.
fix: Treat any failure to load the models as 'damaged': in the voice process turn non-Error throws into 'The speech models couldn't be loaded', and in VoiceService delete the .ok markers and go to needs-models with “The speech models look damaged. Download them again.” so the existing download button repairs it. Optionally verify file sizes at start.

title: A dead-silent microphone is shown as “Listening for ‘Hey Ember’”
scenario: The default input is a monitor or the wrong device, the laptop mic-mute key or GNOME's input mute is on, or an HDMI/unused input is selected. getUserMedia succeeds and frames arrive, all zeros. Ember reports 'Listening for “Hey Ember”' (settings line and handle icon) while it cannot hear anything, and nothing ever tells the user why “Hey Ember” does nothing. With no microphone at all, Ember also keeps the speech models loaded (297 MB working set measured) while only showing an error.
evidence: Run with a 60 s all-silence fake mic: state stays 'waiting'; the only trace is the once-a-minute log line `voice.cpu {peak:0}`. process.ts accumulates `peak` and main/voice.ts:239 only logs it, and the watchdog only tests that frames arrive. With no device: state 'error', voice process 297 MB (getAppMetrics workingSetSize).
fix: Use the peak that is already measured: if peak is exactly 0 (a live mic always has some noise floor) across about 30-60 s of frames, send a 'silent' message and have main show “The microphone is sending silence. Check the input device or mute switch in Sound settings.” (state error or a warning detail). Optionally start the voice process only once the mic page reports 'capturing'.

title: teardown() right after utilityProcess.fork() kills nothing: the voice process is orphaned (about 300 MB) until Ember quits
platforms: all (windows/macOS most exposed: slower process spawn)
scenario: VoiceService.teardown() sets this.proc = null and calls p.kill(). Electron's UtilityProcess.kill() does nothing before the process has spawned, and main has dropped its handle, so a 'Ember voice' process with the models loaded stays alive for the rest of the session; each repeat adds another. Triggers are a mute or unmute double-press, or listening toggled off and on, within the spawn latency; or the mic page reporting a permission error within about 100 ms of start (macOS or Windows privacy denied) when spawning is slower than here.
evidence: In the dev app, 4 start-then-teardown pairs each at gaps of 0, 5, 20, 50, 100 and 200 ms (a repeat run gave a different count): leaked processes at the 0 ms gap and once at 5 ms, none at 20 ms or more. In another run 3 survived 15 s later and after a forced GC; a same-tick storm left 22 voice processes alive (a synthetic worst case). On this Linux box fork-to-spawn is 9-37 ms against 70-150 ms for a permission-denied error, so it does not leak here; spawn is slower on Windows. I could not test Windows or macOS.
fix: Keep the handle until exit: in teardown() call p.kill() and, if p.pid is undefined, also `p.once('spawn', () => p.kill())` (or track pending procs and kill on 'spawn'). Alternatively ask the child to exit by message.

title: No liveness check on the voice process: if it hangs, the UI says “Listening” and the mic page queues audio without limit
scenario: The frame watchdog runs inside the voice process, so a frozen or starved process (stuck WASM call, EDR/antivirus suspending it, thrashing) cannot report itself. Main only learns of a crash through 'exit'. Ember keeps showing “Listening for ‘Hey Ember’”, wake words do nothing, and the mic page keeps posting 64 KB/s into the MessagePort queue (about 230 MB per hour).
evidence: SIGSTOP on the voice utility process for 25 s: voice state stayed 'waiting' with no restart or message; on SIGCONT it processed the backlog in a burst. No real hang trigger was found; the recognizers are bounded (21 s of audio takes 1.4 s).
fix: Have the voice process send a heartbeat (it already ticks every second) and let VoiceService restart it when none arrives for about 10 s. A bounded queue or backpressure from the mic page would also cap memory.

title: Spoken text drops asterisks that are not emphasis: “5 * 3 * 2” is read as “5 3 2” and “*.tmp” as “.tmp”
scenario: Ember reads answers aloud (Speak replies, or a screen reader running). The italics rule treats `* ... *` pairs with spaces inside as emphasis, so multiplication and wildcard patterns lose their stars in what is said, while the bubble shows them. “Delete *.tmp and *.log” is spoken as “Delete .tmp and .log”, which also misreads a destructive command; `__init__` is said as “init”.
evidence: Run: spokenText('Delete *.tmp and *.log from the folder.') → 'Delete .tmp and .log from the folder.'; 'That is 6 * 7 * 1 = 42.' → 'That is 6  7  1 = 42.'; 'Use __init__.py and a * b * c.' → 'Use init.py and a  b  c.' The regex is /(^|[\s(])[*_]([^*_\n]+)[*_](?=[\s.,!?;:)]|$)/.
fix: Follow CommonMark flanking: the opening marker must be followed by a non-space and the closing one preceded by a non-space, e.g. /(^|[\s(])([*_])(?=\S)([^*_\n]*\S)\2(?=[\s.,!?;:)]|$)/, and do not treat `_` inside words or `__x__` in file names as emphasis.

title: The model download sits at “100%” while the archives are verified and unpacked
scenario: Progress counts compressed download bytes, so settings shows “Downloading speech models… 100%” while sha256 and in-process bzip2 unpacking run (the 107 MB Moonshine archive). That is long enough to look hung, and longer on 2-core machines or with antivirus scanning each written file.
evidence: In the dev app the progress callback reached 100% at 3.4 s of an 8.6 s download-and-install (about 5 s at 100%, on 4 fast cores). The unpack alone took 8.9 s in the standalone test.
fix: Report progress as (downloaded + unpacked) or cap the bar at about 90% until the move into place, and set the status text to “Unpacking…” once the last byte arrives.

title: Speaker rejection's parec is pinned to the sink that was default at start and may keep the sink awake
scenario: parec is started with --device=@DEFAULT_MONITOR@ once, when listening starts. PulseAudio resolves that name when the stream is created and does not move such a stream when the default sink changes. After the user plugs in headphones or a Bluetooth speaker, the monitor stays on the old sink: a video's “Hey Ember” or Ember's own voice through the new sink is no longer rejected, and Ember's barge-in logic believes the stream is alive (it still delivers silence). A permanent record stream on a monitor source also counts as activity, so the output device never idle-suspends (battery, DAC hiss).
evidence: Not verified here: the container has no PulseAudio or parec. Based on PulseAudio's behaviour for streams created with an explicit source name, and on the code: speakers.ts starts parec once and only restarts it when it exits. No docs mention output-device changes.
fix: Restart the monitor when the default sink changes (for example `pactl subscribe`, or the mic page's devicechange, which also fires for output devices), and mention the always-on monitor in the consent text or let it run only while Ember speaks or a wake is pending. Verify on RHEL 8 hardware with `pactl list short source-outputs` after switching sinks.

title: Keyboard trap in the terminal: Tab, Shift+Tab and Esc can't leave it, and Stop sits behind it
scenario: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user tabs through a running tab: tab, command block, then the terminal's hidden textarea. Focus stays in the textarea for every further Tab, Shift+Tab and Esc (WCAG 2.1.2), and Stop/Close come after the terminal in DOM order (panel.append(header, block, host, typing, foot)). On Linux/macOS interactive runs each Tab is also sent to the program as \t: tabbing around while sudo's password prompt is waiting adds a tab character to the password. The terminal shows no focus indicator at all. Only Shift+Tab from a fresh window (wraps to Stop), the mouse or the stop chord escape.
evidence: trap.mjs against the built page (xterm 5.5.0, real options): 'Tab trail: tab -> PRE.command -> TEXTAREA.xterm-helper-textarea -> TEXTAREA -> Shift+Tab=>TEXTAREA -> Escape=>TEXTAREA'. Interactive run: input messages [\t, ESC[Z, ESC, ESC[Z] were sent to the run. Non-interactive run: same trap, nothing sent. trap2.mjs: Shift+Tab from a fresh window lands on Stop. terminal.ts:32-36 only calls term.open(host); no tabIndex, no custom key handler, no :focus-within style on .term.
fix: Put the footer (status + Stop/Close) before the terminal in DOM order or give it its own landmark. For non-interactive runs set term.textarea.tabIndex = -1. For interactive runs add term.attachCustomKeyEventHandler so Esc then Tab (or Ctrl+Shift+M) hands focus back, say so in the typing hint, and add .term:focus-within { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) }.

title: Closing the command window leaves running commands running, unseen, with no way back except Settings
area: command window: lifecycle, how to stop it
scenario: A user watching a long command (npm install, a build, a copy) clicks the window's close button, as they would with a terminal, believing it stops. The window is destroyed, the command keeps running, and nothing says so. The task card only offers Stop for the whole task; Settings > Computers > 'Open the command window' is the only route back to the tab and its Stop. It also breaks the R1 promise that a command runs only where the user can watch and stop it.
evidence: closewin.mjs drives the real createCommandWindowController with a fake window: attach() a live run, then win.close(). The handler at window.ts:177-185 only sets win = null, view = null and cancels announcements. Result: 'run stopped by closing the window? null' and no second window is made until something else needs one. createCommandWindow (windows.ts:54) has no 'close' interception. The only ways back are Settings (home/computers.ts:181 -> runtime.ts:855) or a bubble question's 'Show the command'.
fix: While any tab is running (or a card/countdown is up), intercept the window's 'close' event: preventDefault and hide it, so tabs, Stop and output survive. If it must close, ask 'A command is still running. Stop it?' and call run.stop('user') on Yes. Add a 'Show' action to the task card and bubble while a command runs.

title: A command that asks for a password: nothing tells the user, later runs never raise the window, and it times out silently after 2 minutes
scenario: The worker prompt tells the model 'if a command asks for a password, the user types it in the command window'. After the first command the window stays open but is never raised again: reveal() only shows it when hidden or when a card/countdown is up. The user's browser sits on top; the model runs git clone https://github.com/acme/private; git prints "Username for 'https://github.com':" and waits. The bubble says 'Running a command', the window is buried, and at 120 s it ends 'Stopped after 2 min: it took too long.' The user was never told a prompt was waiting.
evidence: raise.mjs with the real controller: first attach -> calls 'showInactive'; with the window now visible, a second attach plus output "Username for 'https://github.com': " -> calls only 'send:output' (no moveTop, no show, no cue). grep of app/main/commands, targets and renderer/command finds no 'waiting for you' signal; prompts.ts only withholds the answer from the model. The task card's only action is Stop (tasks.ts:295).
fix: On every attach, raise the window without focus (setAlwaysOnTop pulse or moveTop). When an interactive run's output ends in a prompt (reuse SECRET_PROMPT, or no newline for ~2 s) flash the tab, put 'A command is waiting for you to type' in the task's bubble with a 'Show' button, and optionally notify. Reset the timeout clock while it waits for the user.

title: Typing an answer into a command: terminal isn't focused (keystrokes vanish) and Ctrl+V doesn't paste
scenario: The user approves 'sudo apt install ...' (or ssh-keygen, git over https). The tab appears showing '[sudo] password for ana:'. They type at once: nothing is received, because keyboard focus is on <body>, and with echo off they can't tell. After clicking the terminal they paste from their password manager with Ctrl+V: xterm sends a literal ^V (0x16) instead of pasting, so the password is wrong and sudo burns an attempt. Ctrl+Shift+V and Shift+Insert do paste but nothing says so. This hits Windows users too, for WSL and SSH runs (interactive PTY).
evidence: term-focus.mjs: after the state push and the prompt output, document.activeElement is BODY; page.keyboard.type('hunter2') produced no 'input' message. term-paste.mjs with the clipboard set: Control+v -> input '\u0016'; Control+Shift+v -> input 's3cret-passw0rd'; Shift+Insert -> pasted. grep: the only focus() call in renderer/command is the tab strip (main.ts:293); createRunTerminal never focuses.
fix: Focus the terminal when an interactive run's tab is shown and the window is active (term.focus()). Add term.attachCustomKeyEventHandler returning false for Ctrl+V (let the browser paste into the textarea; don't call navigator.clipboard, main denies that permission) and for Ctrl+C when term.hasSelection(). Mention paste in the typing hint.

title: Ask card: Allow and Not now fall below the fold for ordinary multi-line commands while a quarter of the window is empty
scenario: The model asks to run a 10-line script (a heredoc that overwrites a config file, a multi-command deploy) with a couple of reasons. At the default 760x480 window the card area is capped at 72vh, so the card shows heading, a 192 px scrolling command, some reasons, then is cut off. Why:, the 'Read the whole command' hint, Allow and Not now are inside the outer scroller, under the fold, with about 120 px of empty black window below the cap. Two nested scrollbars appear, and a non-expert will think the card is broken or close it (see the close-window finding).
evidence: cmd1.mjs screenshot shots/B-ask-ssh-long.png. probe-h.mjs for a 12-line command + 4 reasons: .cards bottom y=358, Allow top y=412 (cards scrollHeight 440 vs clientHeight 346), panels below it empty. sweep.mjs at 760x480 (X = Allow below the fold): 1 reason line + Why from 10 command lines; 2 reason lines from 9 lines; 4 reason lines from 6 lines. Long single lines wrap at about 90 characters, so a 550-character command is 6 lines.
fix: Don't cap .cards when nothing sits below it (max-height: calc(100vh - 24px), or flex:1 when there are no tabs/pending lines). Better, make the action row sticky (position: sticky; bottom: 0 with the card's background) inside the card area, so Allow and Not now are always visible and only the command and reasons scroll.

title: Mixed-script marker underlines the user's own folders (even ASCII words) on every card and tab for non-Latin usernames and folders, with no legend on tabs
area: command window: mixed-script marking, alarm fatigue
platforms: windows, linux, macos (users with non-Latin folder names)
scenario: A Russian, Greek, Arabic or Japanese user has C:\Users\Иван or ~/Документы. The main script is judged per whitespace token, and paths are one token, so the Cyrillic name in C:\Users\Иван flips the verdict and 'C:' and 'Users' are underlined yellow; in /home/ana/Документы/проект the ASCII 'home' and 'ana' are. Every card for this user shows the underlined header (the default cwd is the home folder) plus the legend 'Letters from another alphabet are underlined.'; every tab, even for a harmless Get-ChildItem that never asked, shows the same underlines with no legend at all. The one signal meant to catch a look-alike letter (buіld) becomes noise for this population.
evidence: vt.mjs: visibleText marks 'C:\Users\[Иван]', '/[home]/[ana]/Документы', 'cp ~/Загрузки/[file].[txt]', 'cd C:\Users\[Ανδρέας]\Desktop'. Renders shots/L-cyrillic-user.png and shots/V-tab-cyrillic.png. In buildTab (main.ts:259, 278) the legend returned by commandBlock/headerNode is discarded; document .legend count on the tab is 0. visible-text.test.ts only pins single filenames (日本語.txt), not paths.
fix: Judge the main script per word, not per whitespace token: split at path and punctuation characters (/ \ . - _ : ~ = ,) before counting scripts, so Иван, Users and project are each single-script while buіld, рm and gіt are still flagged. Show the legend on tabs too or don't mark in tabs. Consider a plain sentence line ('Some letters look like another alphabet') only for true intra-word mixing.

title: Windows High Contrast: Allow, Not now, Stop and tabs lose their borders, and keyboard focus is invisible
area: design system: forced colours on confirm and command UI
scenario: A low-vision user runs Windows with a contrast theme. On the ask card, Allow, Not now and Stop render as bare words: .btn is 'all: unset' and draws its edge and focus ring with box-shadow, which forced-colors mode removes. The command block, card and tab borders vanish and the selected tab can't be told from the others. With Tab on Allow, nothing shows where focus is.
evidence: forced.mjs with Playwright forcedColors:'active' (shots/Q-forced-colors.png): buttons are plain text, no ring while document.activeElement is Allow. grep -rn 'forced-colors' app packages finds nothing; ember.css:195 uses outline:none; box-shadow for focus. DESIGN.md covers prefers-contrast but not forced-colors.
fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) to ember.css: give .btn, .tab and .command a real 1px border (border: 1px solid ButtonText, selected tab Highlight), and focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px } on controls, tabs and .command.

title: Copying command output: Ctrl+C interrupts a live run (Linux) or does nothing (Windows), no context menu, and the window can't be screenshotted on Windows/macOS
scenario: A user selects an error message in the terminal and presses Ctrl+C. On a live Linux run, xterm sends ETX to the program (stopping it) and copies nothing. On an ended or Windows run nothing happens. There is no context menu or Copy button. Because the command window is content-protected on Windows and macOS (windows.ts:65), Snipping Tool or screen-share can't capture the output either, so to get an error out the user must retype it or know Ctrl+Insert.
evidence: term-copy.mjs: select a row, Control+c -> clipboard '' and, for an interactive run, input '\u0003'; Control+Insert -> clipboard has the selected line; Control+Shift+c and Meta+c -> nothing. The docs never mention copying. macOS works through the Edit menu.
fix: Custom key handler: Ctrl+C (Windows/Linux) with a selection copies and swallows the key, without a selection it is ^C; Ctrl+Shift+C always copies. Add a small 'Copy output' button next to Stop.

title: Announcement card (countdown) omits the plain-language lines and the stop chord, and Stop is the quietest button
scenario: The user said 'delete build/'. The command window shows 'Running this, as you asked', the raw rm -rf command, 'Starts in 4 s.' and a bordered grey Stop. The plain-language line ('Deletes build and everything in it.') and the model's Why: are in the card the window receives but buildAnnounce never draws them, so in 4 seconds the user must judge shell syntax. Nothing says the stop chord (Win+Alt+X / Ctrl+Alt+X) also works. The heading says 'Running' although nothing runs yet.
evidence: shots/C-announce.png; buildAnnounce (main.ts:203-226) renders where, heading, command, legend, count, Stop only; card.says is unused there (it is built as [...d.says, why] in flow.ts:703). The bubble carries the plain sentence, but it is a separate window that can sit on another display.
fix: Draw cardLines(card) under the command in the announcement, retitle it 'Starting in 4 s, as you asked', and add 'or press <stop chord>' under the countdown. Consider a 5-6 s countdown.

title: First-use consent cards are 2 screens of text in a fixed 440x300 window; the stop chord and the 'what it can reach' lines are below the fold, and yes needs no scroll
scenario: A user turning on commands or SSH sees the first paragraph and a scrollbar. Body heights vs the 198 px viewport: 294 px (commands), 356 px (SSH), 382 px (commands in WSL as admin). The stop chord, 'What a command already changed stays changed', the Windows-reach and administrator lines and, for SSH, 'Your voice and your GitHub sign-in stay on this computer' are all below the fold, yet 'Turn on' and 'Connect' are always clickable after 900 ms. The command card forces 'read all'; the consent card, which authorises installing software on another computer, does not. The window isn't resizable.
evidence: prompt1.mjs for linux/win32/darwin: scrollHeight vs clientHeight printed per card (294/198, 356/198, 382/198); shots/P-linux-consent-ssh.png, P-linux-consent-cmd-wsl.png.
fix: Size the prompt window to the card (up to the work area) or make it resizable with a larger default for consent cards (about 440x460). Put the stop chord and the 'what it can touch' line first; enable the yes button only after the body has been scrolled to the end, as for commands.

title: Command card can be left with both buttons dead if the Confirmer refuses the answer
scenario: Two tasks run; one is moving the mouse (borrow), or on macOS a key was just posted. The user clicks Allow on the command card, and Confirmer.answer() returns false while blocked(). The page has already set els.sent = true and disabled both buttons. Nothing re-enables them: re-showing the same card (the bubble's 'Show the command') keeps the same key, so the card stays frozen until the 2-minute expiry. The consent card has a recovery path for this (prompt-window.ts show()); the command card has none.
evidence: stuck.mjs: after clicking Allow, allow.disabled and deny.disabled are true; after pushing the same card again (rev 2) both are still true. runtime.ts:915 confirmAnswer ignores the boolean from confirmer.answer; confirm.ts:152 returns false when blocked().
fix: Have main push a state flag when an answer wasn't taken (or let the controller re-send the card with a new key/nonce), and let the page re-enable its buttons; or don't disable the buttons until the card actually leaves.

title: Command and prompt windows aren't placed on Ember's display or visible on all workspaces
scenario: With two monitors, Ember and the bubble ('May I run a command?', 'Needs you') are on the display the user is working on, but the always-on-top 760x480 command card, or the SSH password / consent window, opens with the default placement (the primary display's centre). On macOS the floating panel isn't on all Spaces or over a full-screen app. The user sees a bubble whose Allow lives in a window on another screen or Space; 'Show the command' makes it jump there.
evidence: grep -rn 'setPosition|setBounds|center()|setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces' over commands/, remote/prompt-window.ts, windows.ts: nothing for these two windows; the overlay does use visibleOnFullScreen (platform/linux/overlay-shaper.ts:13). Electron's default is a centred position. Not reproducible in this single-display Linux container, so inferred from the code.
fix: In reveal() (command) and prompt-window reveal(), place the window on the display nearest the cursor/Ember (screen.getDisplayNearestPoint) and call setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, { visibleOnFullScreen: true, skipTransformProcessType: true }) while a card is up.

title: RTL text reorders on the command card: what is shown is not the order that runs
scenario: The card's promise is that what you approve is what runs, and it makes explicit bidi controls visible. Plain Hebrew or Arabic letters need no control characters to be reordered by the Unicode bidi algorithm: digits and neutrals next to an RTL word swap places. The tokens aren't flagged because the characters are ordinary. For Hebrew or Arabic users (or a crafted command) the displayed argument order can differ from the real one; the terminal below shows logical order, so card and terminal disagree.
evidence: bidi.mjs: logical 'chmod -R 755 שלום 777 /srv/data'; rendered left to right 'chmod -R 755 777 שלום /srv/data' (shots/W-rtl.png). .command sets no direction or unicode-bidi.
fix: On .command and the header: direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: bidi-override (or wrap RTL runs in <bdo dir=ltr>), so the card shows logical order like the shell and xterm; note it in the legend.

title: After a remote helper's second check, a red 'refused it' tab for the same command lingers
area: command window: tabs, remote second ask
scenario: build-01's own gate finds more than the PC did, so the first run ends 'refused-remote' (needsConfirm) and the flow asks again with a new runId. The first tab stays: a red 'failed' symbol and 'build-01 refused it: build-01's own check wants the user's yes first: ...'. After the user says Allow a second tab for the same command runs. The user sees a failure for something they then approved, double-negative text included.
evidence: flow.ts:749 assigns runId = newRunId() for the retry; window.ts:469 only drops a tab with the same runId ('a retry after the remote asked: its old tab goes'), so the comment's intent isn't met. command-flow.test.ts:1448 pins two different runIds. Code-read, not run live.
fix: Have the flow tell the window to drop (or relabel 'Waiting for your OK again') the tab of a run that ended refused-remote with needsConfirm, or give the retry the same tab key.

title: Card hierarchy: where a command runs and why are the quietest text; all asks look alike; leftover programs have no remedy
area: command card: communication of place, reason, danger
scenario: The computer a command will run on ('On build-01 as deploy') is 12 px at 66 % opacity above the heading, which says only 'Ember wants to run this command'. The model's Why: reason is 12 px at 52 %. A git push, a recursive delete, an 'ask every command' policy ask and a root ask all look the same, orange Allow included (the host-key card does demote its risky button, the command card doesn't), so with many cards users habituate. Ended tabs say '2 programs it started are still running: a, b.' with no Stop or hint how to end them, and a tab strip entry doesn't say which computer.
evidence: shots/A-ask-local.png, B-ask-ssh-long.png, G-ended.png; styles.css:15 (.where) and :27 (.why); statusLine/stragglerText in copy.ts:82-110.
fix: Put the computer in the heading for non-local targets ('...on build-01', with a small badge in the tab), give destructive classes a subtle marker (not a red alarm), and add a tip to the straggler line ('Ask Ember to stop them, or end them yourself').

title: Stalled-link countdown re-announces every second to screen readers
area: command window: accessibility of the status line
scenario: When an SSH link goes quiet, remote-runner.ts:529 updates the status text every second ('This command stops in 14 s...' down to 0) and the page writes it into a role='status' (polite live) element, so a screen reader reads about 17 near-identical announcements over the grace period.
evidence: main.ts:267 sets role='status' on each tab's status line; remote-runner.ts:521-531 steps the countdown each second; window.ts note() pushes state per change.
fix: Keep the visible countdown but move it out of the live region (aria-live='off' on the countdown), announce once when the link stalls and once when it resumes or the command stops.
